lines.japanese: そう、今日のように―――
lines.english: Yes—on a day like today.

lines.japanese:
早い時間帯では連れもいない。
　隣家の住人は、きっと眠っているに違いない。
lines.english: At this hour, he had no one to walk with. The girl next door was surely still asleep.

lines.japanese: （起こしてもいいんだけど……起きないしなぁ）
lines.english: (I could wake her up… Not that she'd actually get up.)

lines.japanese:
しかし当の住人―――紅緒あずさに、早起きがで
きるはずもない。
lines.english: But there was no way his neighbor, Azusa Benio, could get up early.

lines.japanese: 選択を迫られる。
lines.english: He had to choose.

lines.japanese:
なぜ葛藤が生じるのかと言うと、置いて行かれる
ことをあずさが極度に嫌がるからだった。
lines.english: What made it a dilemma was Azusa's fierce hatred of being left behind.

lines.japanese: 泣くのだ、彼女は。
lines.english: She would cry.

lines.japanese: 「うーん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
起こすべきか。
　否か。
lines.english: Wake her? Or not?

lines.japanese: 起こそうとした場合―――
lines.english: If he tried waking her—

lines.japanese: 「起きなよ、学校行くよ」
lines.english: “Wake up. We're going to school.”

lines.japanese: 「うーーん……」
lines.english: “Mmmmm…”

lines.japanese: 苦しそうに唸る。
lines.english: She groaned as though in agony.

lines.japanese: 「あずさ、一緒に通学しないの？」
lines.english: “Azusa, don't you want to walk to school together?”

lines.japanese: 「うおーーーん……」
lines.english: “Uooooooh…”

lines.japanese: 地獄の亡者を思わせた。
lines.english: She sounded like a damned soul in hell.
“Azu—”

lines.japanese: 「あぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁぁっ……」
lines.english: “Aaaaaaaaaaaah…”

lines.japanese: 不機嫌そうに奇声を発する。
lines.english: She let out a strange, deeply aggrieved cry.

lines.japanese: 「……いってきます」
lines.english: “…I'm off.”

lines.japanese: 諦めた。
lines.english: He gave up.

lines.japanese: 起こさないで行った場合―――
lines.english: If he left without waking her—

lines.japanese: 「起こしてくんなかった……」
lines.english: “You didn't wake me…”

lines.japanese: 「いや……起こしたって」
lines.english: “No… I did.”

lines.japanese:
放課後。
　あとをついてくる。
lines.english: After school. She followed close behind.

lines.japanese: 「起こしてくんなかった……」
lines.english: “You didn't wake me…”

lines.japanese: 「起こしたって。あずさが起きなかったの」
lines.english: “I did. You wouldn't get up.”

lines.japanese: 「起こしてくんなかった～～～っ」
lines.english: “You didn't waaaake me!”
“…… Like I said…”

lines.japanese: 「明日も起こしてくんないのかな……」
lines.english: “Maybe you won't wake me tomorrow either…”

lines.japanese: どこまでもついてくるのであった。
lines.english: She followed him wherever he went.

lines.japanese:
天秤を傾けるのは忍自身だ。
　どちらを選んでも結果に変わりはないのだが。
　楽な方を選ぶものである。
lines.english: The scales were Shinobu's to tip. Either choice led to the same result. So naturally, he chose the easier one.

lines.japanese: （ごめん……あずさ）
lines.english: (Sorry… Azusa.)

lines.japanese:
歩き出す。
　皆と通う道も、一人だとまた違う。
　静かで変化の見えない街並み。
lines.english: He set off. The road he walked with everyone felt different alone. The town lay quiet, its scenery changeless.

lines.japanese:
自らの足で、一歩ごとに光景をたぐり寄せていく
ような。
lines.english: As though with every step he pulled another piece of the landscape toward himself.

lines.japanese:
無為な空想がよぎるのである。
　樋口章二と落ち合う場所にさしかかるが、やはり
というか誰もいない。
lines.english: An idle fancy crossed his mind. He reached the spot where he usually met Shouji Higuchi, but sure enough— or perhaps inevitably—no one was there.

lines.japanese: 時間が早すぎた。
lines.english: It was simply too early.

lines.japanese:
それ以前に章二は通学すること自体に、判定過程
を持っている。
　通学率５０～７０％といったところだ。
lines.english: Besides, Shouji had to pass through a decision-making process before he attended school at all. His attendance rate hovered somewhere between fifty and seventy percent.

lines.japanese:
あまり学校には来ない。
　早朝ともなれば、問題は確率から可能性へと降格
していく。
lines.english: He rarely came to school. At this early hour, the question was demoted from probability to mere possibility.

lines.japanese: ５％もあるかどうか。
lines.english: Five percent, if that.

lines.japanese:
あいもかわらず、忍はひとり。
　塚本兄妹と笛子については、ときおりこの時間帯
にも姿を見せる。
lines.english: As ever, Shinobu was alone. The Tsukamoto siblings and Fueko did sometimes appear at this hour too.

lines.japanese:
しかし。
　―――今日はいないようだ。
lines.english: But. —Apparently not today.

lines.japanese: （結局、早出となると、こんなもんか……）
lines.english: (So this is what leaving early gets you…)

lines.japanese:
たまには一人の通学も悪くはない。
　しかし単独で道を歩いていると、取り残された
ような気分になった。
lines.english: Walking to school alone was not so bad once in a while. Yet walking the road by himself left him feeling as though he had been left behind.

lines.japanese:
仲間どころか、早すぎて人通り自体が少ない。
　時折、背広を着たサラリーマンらしき姿が、急ぎ
足で忍を追い抜いていく。
lines.english: Not only were his friends absent; it was so early there was scarcely anyone about. Now and then, someone in a suit, apparently an office worker, hurried past him.

lines.japanese:
当然、見ず知らずの人間だ。
　言葉を交わすこともない。
lines.english: Strangers, naturally. They exchanged no words.

lines.japanese:
いや、毎日通う道となれば、顔くらい見覚えのあ
る他人もいるものだ。
lines.english: Still, on a road he walked every day, there were strangers whose faces he recognized.

lines.japanese:
しかしあくまで他人。
　寂寥とした忍の気持ちを、潤すには至らない。
lines.english: They were still strangers. They did nothing to relieve the desolation in Shinobu's heart.

lines.japanese: （いや、いいんだけどね……たまには）
lines.english: (It's fine, though… Once in a while.)

lines.japanese:
視線を持ち上げ、空を眺めつつ歩いていく。
　寂しさを楽しむ心境は、自己憐憫と似ている。
　ふと、忍はそう思った。
lines.english: He raised his eyes to the sky as he walked. Taking pleasure in loneliness was much like self-pity. The thought came to Shinobu unbidden.

lines.japanese: いくつかの角を曲がった時だった。
lines.english: It was as he rounded yet another corner.

lines.japanese:
忍の背筋が、ことさら真っ直ぐに伸ばされた。
　彼女がいた―――
lines.english: Shinobu's spine straightened sharply. There she was—

lines.japanese:
背中だった。
　前方１０メートルほど先を歩いている。
　人は他人の歩き方を見分けることができる。
lines.english: Her back. Walking some ten meters ahead of him. People can recognize others by the way they walk.

lines.japanese:
飼い猫が靴音を見分けるように。
　慣れ親しめば、あるいは、憧憬を胸に目線を投じ
続ければ。
lines.english: As a house cat recognizes its owner’s footfalls. With enough familiarity—or enough time spent watching with longing.

lines.japanese:
忍は迷った。
　先ほどまでの淡い感傷も失せていた。
　冷静でいるつもりが、胸がいっぱいになっている。
lines.english: Shinobu hesitated. His faint melancholy of a moment ago was gone. He meant to be calm, but his heart was already full.

lines.japanese:
嬉しい誤算だったためだ。
　友達が誰もいないと思った朝。
　不意の遭遇に、心が躍る。
lines.english: A welcome miscalculation. This morning, he had expected to find none of his friends. The chance encounter set his heart dancing.

lines.japanese:
見付けたのが彼女―――本堂沙也加ということにも
原因があることは、この瞬間忍の網膜から入力された
視覚情報が視神経に運搬され外側膝状体ニューロン
lines.english: The fact that the person he had found was her—Sayaka Hondou—was clearly part of the reason. At that very instant, visual information entering Shinobu's retina traveled along the optic nerve, furiously firing the axons of his lateral geniculate neurons

lines.japanese:
軸索を猛烈に発火させつつ視覚野へと連絡されたこ
とからもわかる。
lines.english: as it was relayed to the visual cortex. The evidence was plain.

lines.japanese: その情報は特別なものであった。
lines.english: That information was special.

lines.japanese:
優先順位を高く設定された反復学習によって、沙
也加情報処理回路ともいうべき認識パターンが形成
されているためである。
lines.english: Through repeated learning given high priority, he had formed a recognition pattern that might fairly be called a dedicated Sayaka-processing circuit.

lines.japanese:
同様のものはあずさや章二らにも用意されている
が、沙也加のそれは、少しばかりおもむきが異なる。
lines.english: Similar circuits existed for Azusa, Shouji, and the others, but Sayaka's was subtly different.

lines.japanese:
好意の軽重を示すものではない。
　ただ視覚認識上の優先度が高い。
lines.english: This did not mean he felt more or less affection for her. She simply had higher priority in visual recognition.

lines.japanese:
つまり視野に入った光景に沙也加が含まれている
場合、忍の脳は細胞活性を著しく高める。
lines.english: In other words, whenever a scene in Shinobu's field of view included Sayaka, his brain sharply increased its cellular activity.

lines.japanese:
より強い認知が行われる―――ついつい目が行く、
のである。
lines.english: More intensive cognition occurred— which is to say, his eyes tended to find her.

lines.japanese:
水の流れを思わせる歩き方を、目にする機会も増
える。
lines.english: He had more and more chances to see that walk of hers, which brought flowing water to mind.

lines.japanese:
もう何年になるだろうか。
　初めてその姿を目にしてから―――
lines.english: How many years had it been? Since he first laid eyes on her—

lines.japanese: 余暇と言っていい時間だった。
lines.english: It was what one might call leisure time.

lines.japanese:
施設から引き取られ、自分の部屋というものを持
ったのもはじめてなら、完全に自由な時間というも
のも初体験であった。
lines.english: Since leaving the institution, he had been given a room of his own for the first time—and this was also his first taste of time that was entirely his own.

lines.japanese:
窓から街並みを眺める。
　燦然とした光が、世界を覆っていた。
lines.english: He gazed through the window at the city. Resplendent light blanketed the world.

lines.japanese:
窓枠から飛び込んでくる温度のない光のシャワー
が、冷水を浴びるのとはまた違う、独特の心地よさ
を連想させた。
lines.english: The shower of heatless light spilling through the window evoked a peculiar pleasure unlike the feeling of dousing himself in cold water.

lines.japanese:
貴宮忍は何をしても良かった。
　階下に降りて腹を満たしても良い。
　質素なベッドに飛び乗って、惰眠を貪っても良い。
lines.english: Shinobu Atemiya could do anything he wished. He could go downstairs and fill his stomach. He could leap onto the plain bed and gorge himself on sleep.

lines.japanese:
叫び声を上げて街に飛び出し、子供同士で遊びほ
うけても良い。
lines.english: He could rush into the streets with a shout and spend the day playing with other children.

lines.japanese:
用もなく机の引き出しを開けてみる。
　カラッポだ。
lines.english: For no reason, he opened one of the desk drawers. Empty.

lines.japanese:
下から順番に、効率の良い泥棒のように開け放っ
ていく。
lines.english: Starting at the bottom, he opened them one by one like an efficient burglar.

lines.japanese:
無意味な行動。
　施設では目立つ行動をとることは、許されなかった。
lines.english: A meaningless act. At the institution, conspicuous behavior had not been permitted.

lines.japanese:
罰されるわけではないが、精神的な異変と見なさ
れることがあった。
lines.english: No punishment followed, but it could be taken as evidence of a disturbance in his mental state.

lines.japanese:
大人はあらゆる行動に意味を付随させようとする。
　正直、辟易していたものだ。
lines.english: Adults tried to fasten meaning onto every action. Frankly, he had found it tiresome.

lines.japanese:
しかし今、忍は自由だ。
　身が軽くなる思いで、忍は部屋の外に出た。
lines.english: But now Shinobu was free. Feeling almost weightless, he left his room.

lines.japanese:
千鳥はいなかった。
　保護者がいない。
lines.english: Chidori was not there. There was no guardian.

lines.japanese:
それもまた、新鮮な気持ちとともに受け入れられ
る事実である。
lines.english: Even that was a fact he could welcome as something new.

lines.japanese: 少し空腹を感じた。
lines.english: He felt a little hungry.

lines.japanese: （いい、のかな？）
lines.english: (Is it… all right?)

lines.japanese:
冷蔵庫を開けると、雑多な食料品が詰めてあった。
　統一性のなさに少しぎょっとする。感覚的なものだ。
lines.english: When he opened the refrigerator, he found it crammed with assorted food. The lack of any pattern startled him a little. It was an instinctive reaction.

lines.japanese:
普通、料理を作るための素材には傾向があり、無
闇に雑然と買い込みはしないものだ。
lines.english: Normally, ingredients bought for cooking followed some pattern; people did not buy a random jumble for no reason.

lines.japanese:
貴宮家の冷蔵庫はそういった秩序がなく、混沌と
していた。
lines.english: The Atemiya refrigerator had no such order. It was chaos.

lines.japanese: だが忍には、違和感だけしか受け取れなかった。
lines.english: But Shinobu could perceive only that something felt wrong.

lines.japanese:
空腹をいかにして満たしたものか。
　幼い忍ははたと考える。
lines.english: How was he to fill his stomach? Young Shinobu stopped and thought.

lines.japanese:
引っ越しに際し、千鳥は好きにして良いと言った。
　こう言った。
lines.english: When they moved, Chidori had told him to do as he liked. Her exact words were:

lines.japanese:
『忍さん、これからは新しいルールで生きて
　ください』
lines.english: ‘Shinobu, from now on, you must live under a new set of rules. ’

lines.japanese:
『あなたはあなたの責任で賄える範囲で、好きに行
　動してください。いちいち許可なんて求めること
　はありません』
lines.english: ‘You may do as you please, as long as you can take responsibility for it. You no longer need to ask permission for every little thing.’

lines.japanese: 『責任というものを学んでください』
lines.english: ‘You must learn what responsibility means.’

lines.japanese: 『少し早いかも知れませんが……』
lines.english: ‘Perhaps it is a little early…’

lines.japanese: 『この家には、父親も母親もいないんですから』
lines.english: ‘But this house has neither a father nor a mother.’

lines.japanese:
『そして私も、たくさんしなければならないことが
　あるんですから』
lines.english: ‘And I, too, have a great many things I must do.’

lines.japanese:
『なるたけ、私を煩わせないように。これは以前と
　変わりありません』
lines.english: ‘Try not to trouble me any more than necessary. In that respect, nothing has changed.’

lines.japanese: 『ただ私はそれほどうるさくはないはず』
lines.english: ‘Though I don't imagine I'll be quite so strict.’

lines.japanese: 『すべて、あなた次第です―――』
lines.english: ‘Everything is up to you—’

lines.japanese:
食事制限もないということだ。
　忍も自らの消化器官が弱いことは承知している。
lines.english: That meant there were no restrictions on what he ate, either. Shinobu knew his digestive system was weak.

lines.japanese:
食べ過ぎは良くない。
　これからは点滴さえ簡単には受けられない。
lines.english: Overeating was unwise. From now on, even an IV would not be readily available.

lines.japanese: （体調管理も、自分の責任か）
lines.english: (My health is my own responsibility too.)

lines.japanese: 冷蔵庫の前、低く落ちる冷気にため息を混ぜた。
lines.english: Standing before the refrigerator, he let his sigh mingle with the cold air pooling near the floor.
“Ugh…”

lines.japanese:
腹部を押さえながら外に出た。
　やはり、ハムだろう。
　ずっしりと胃を重くしたものは。
lines.english: He went outside with a hand pressed to his stomach. It was probably the ham, after all. That was what weighed so heavily in his stomach.
“Urrgh…”

lines.japanese:
３０分ほど横になっていたのに、一向に楽になら
ない。
lines.english: He had lain down for nearly half an hour, but felt no better at all.

lines.japanese: （火を通すべきだったかな……）
lines.english: (Should I have cooked it…?)

lines.japanese:
しかし忍は調理などできない。
　ひとりの時に火を使うのも少し危険である。
　千鳥に確認しておいた方がいいだろう。
lines.english: But Shinobu could not cook. Using fire alone was somewhat dangerous, too. Better ask Chidori.

lines.japanese: そして調理についても学んでおくべきだ。
lines.english: And he should learn to cook.

lines.japanese:
それはそれとして、美味だった。
　胃がもたれるのは、食べ過ぎたからだ。
lines.english: Even so, it had tasted good. His stomach felt heavy because he had eaten too much.

lines.japanese:
ほとんどそのままの食材であっても、流動食など
とは比べものにならない。
　当然の話ではあるが、点滴に味などない。
lines.english: Even ingredients eaten almost as they came were incomparably better than liquid meals. And of course an IV had no flavor.
“…Urp.”

lines.japanese: げっぷをして、空を見た。
lines.english: He burped and looked up at the sky.

lines.japanese:
信じられないのである。
　今の有様が。
　心境をうまく言葉にすることができない。
lines.english: He could not believe it. The state he found himself in now. He could not put the feeling into words.

lines.japanese:
それは高揚と似ていた。
　同時に静かな感動でもあった。
　少しばかりの不安も混じる。
lines.english: It resembled exhilaration. At the same time, it was a quiet wonder. A little anxiety mingled with it.

lines.japanese: 「……生きるって、ことなんだ……これが」
lines.english: “So this… is what it means to live…”

lines.japanese:
初めて知ったかのように、忍は呟く。
　空が広い。
　どこまでも続く。
lines.english: Shinobu murmured as though discovering it for the first time. The sky was vast. It stretched on forever.

lines.japanese:
自らの人生も、同様に感じられるのは、仕方ない
ことだった。
lines.english: He could hardly help feeling that his own life was the same.

lines.japanese:
街をそぞろ歩く。
　昼下がり、住宅街の奥深くに人通りは見られない。
lines.english: He wandered through the streets. It was early afternoon, and deep within the residential district, no one was about.

lines.japanese:
車も滅多には入ってこないため、人気さえも感じ
られない。
lines.english: Cars seldom entered either, and there was scarcely even a sense of human presence.

lines.japanese:
（今、この家の中のどれくらいに、人が住んでいる
　んだろう？）
lines.english: (How many of these houses have people living inside them right now?)

lines.japanese:
世界の人口は８０億人と言われている。
　日本だけなら、１億と少々。
lines.english: The world's population was said to be eight billion. Japan alone had a little over a hundred million.

lines.japanese:
相変わらず世界は不穏だったり、紛争していたり、
平和だったり、豊かだったり、貧しかったりした。
lines.english: As ever, the world was uneasy, at war, at peace, prosperous, and poor.

lines.japanese:
日本はそのどれにも当てはまらないような立場を、
前世紀から維持している希有な国家だ。
lines.english: Japan was a rare country that had maintained, since the previous century, a position fitting none of those descriptions.

lines.japanese:
各国から、消費型国家と蔑まれるようになって何
年かが経っている。
lines.english: For several years now, other nations had derided it as a nation of consumers.

lines.japanese:
末期的だと叫ばれつつも、国としての形を残して
いる。
lines.english: Though decried as terminally ill, it retained the shape of a nation.

lines.japanese: 輝かしい未来はないが、過去から続く今がある。
lines.english: There was no shining future, only a present extending out of the past.

lines.japanese: （あ、そうだ）
lines.english: (Oh. That's right.)

lines.japanese:
忍は学校に足を向けた。
　毎日通う場所だ。
　事前に慣れ親しんでおいても損はない。
lines.english: Shinobu turned toward the school. He would go there every day. There was no harm in getting used to it beforehand.

lines.japanese: 門は開放されていたので、勝手に入った。
lines.english: The gate stood open, so he let himself in.

lines.japanese:
時間のせいか、誰もいない。
　無人の校庭を見渡す。
　目新しいところのない学校だった。
lines.english: Perhaps because of the hour, no one was there. He surveyed the deserted schoolyard. There was nothing novel about the school.

lines.japanese:
埋めタイヤ、鉄棒などの当たり障りのない遊具が
あるばかりで、特別なものは何もない。
lines.english: There was only innocuous playground equipment: half-buried tires and horizontal bars. Nothing special.

lines.japanese:
過去、子供の不注意で死亡者が出たため、のぼり
棒とシーソーが撤去されてしまった。
lines.english: In the past, deaths caused by children's carelessness had led to the removal of the climbing pole and the seesaw.

lines.japanese:
前者は落下、後者はシーソーの下に頭部を入れた
ことによる頭蓋陥没。
lines.english: In the first case, a fall; in the second, a child had put their head beneath the seesaw and suffered a depressed skull fracture.

lines.japanese:
危険がなくなったはずの校庭は、安全というより
もただ広漠とした心象を与える。
lines.english: The schoolyard, supposedly purged of danger, felt less safe than simply desolate.

lines.japanese: 忍の心にも、躍るものはない。
lines.english: Nothing stirred in Shinobu's heart either.

lines.japanese:
転ばないよう段差さえも取り払われた場所を、子
供らはどう駆け回るのだろうか。
lines.english: How did children run about a place where even changes in level had been removed lest they fall?

lines.japanese:
さだめし健全な風景であろう。
　と、少し皮肉げなことを、忍は思った。
　何もないと思った兎小屋には、本当に兎がいた。
lines.english: A wholesome sight, no doubt. The thought came to Shinobu with a shade of irony. The rabbit hutch he had assumed empty actually held rabbits.

lines.japanese:
実を抜かれて虚と化した場所で、ただそこだけが
生きていた。
lines.english: In a place gutted of substance and reduced to hollow form, that alone was alive.

lines.japanese: よく見ようとフェンスに指を絡める。
lines.english: He curled his fingers around the fence to get a better look.

lines.japanese:
カシャ、と鳴る。
　兎が物憂げに顔を持ち上げた。
lines.english: The fence rattled. A rabbit languidly raised its head.

lines.japanese:
二羽。
　どちらも怯えている風ではない。
　雌雄の一耳だろうか。
lines.english: There were two. Neither seemed frightened. Perhaps they were a male and female pair.

lines.japanese:
殺風景な兎小屋とその主を、忍はまじまじと観察
した。
lines.english: Shinobu studied the barren hutch and its inhabitants at length.

lines.japanese: （僕の部屋と似てるな、ここ）
lines.english: (This place is like my room.)

lines.japanese:
必要なものがある。
　必要なものしかない。
lines.english: It had what was necessary. It had nothing but what was necessary.

lines.japanese:
無表情に眺めていた。
　冷気めいたものを頬に感じ、視線を横にやった。
lines.english: He watched without expression. Feeling something like cold air upon his cheek, he looked to the side.

lines.japanese: いつやって来たのか、少女が立っていた。
lines.english: A girl was standing there. He had no idea when she had arrived.

lines.japanese:
黒髪の少女は、忍を見もしない。
　手にした鍵束で扉を開き、兎小屋に入る。
　飼育係のようだ。
lines.english: The black-haired girl did not even look at Shinobu. She unlocked the door with the ring of keys in her hand and entered the hutch. She appeared to be in charge of the animals.

lines.japanese:
餌の入ったバケツを下げている。
　声をかけるでもなく、忍は見守る。
　指先がフェンスに食い込んだ。
lines.english: A bucket of feed hung from one hand. Without speaking to her, Shinobu watched. His fingertips dug into the fence.

lines.japanese: （なんだ……この子？）
lines.english: (What is with this girl…?)

lines.japanese: 小屋を掃除する少女を、まじまじと見てしまう。
lines.english: He found himself staring as the girl cleaned the hutch.

lines.japanese:
長い黒髪。
　飾り気のない、しかし静かな迫力のある顔立ちが
印象的だ。
lines.english: Long black hair. Her face was unadorned, yet carried a quiet force that left an impression.

lines.japanese:
美形には属するのだろうが、それ以上に冷然とし
た様子が目立つ。
lines.english: She was probably beautiful, but more striking still was her cold composure.

lines.japanese: たおやめぶり、とでも言うのか。
lines.english: A kind of womanly grace, perhaps.

lines.japanese:
だが華奢なように見えて、瞳は大きく爛々とした
意志をのぞかせている。
lines.english: Yet despite her fragile appearance, her large eyes shone with a vivid will.

lines.japanese:
ただ掃除をしているだけだというのに強すぎるそ
の眼光は、周囲に憎しみを放射しているようにも感
じられた。
lines.english: The gaze was too intense for the simple work of cleaning, and seemed almost to radiate hatred into her surroundings.

lines.japanese:
握りしめたフェンスが、軋む音を立てた。
　強く握りすぎていた。
　少女はようやく、忍に視線の焦点を合わせた。
lines.english: The fence creaked in his clenched hands. He had been gripping it too hard. At last, the girl focused her gaze on Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
―――気圧される。
　初対面であるにも関わらず、双眼にこもる意志の
量は殺意と大差ない。
lines.english: —He shrank beneath it. Though they had never met, the sheer force of will in those two eyes was little different from murderous intent.

lines.japanese:
いや、おそらく少女にとっては平常の有り様なの
だろう。
lines.english: No. This was probably simply the girl's ordinary state.

lines.japanese:
あるいはカリスマというものは、こういう発露を
するものなのかも知れない。
lines.english: Perhaps this was simply how charisma manifested itself.

lines.japanese:
ただ生きているだけで、佇立しているだけで、存
在感を主張してやまない。
lines.english: Simply by living, simply by standing there, she made her presence impossible to ignore.

lines.japanese:
寡黙であれば体内より溢れる活力は、視線を成す
しかないのだから。
lines.english: Being so taciturn, she had no outlet for the vitality welling up inside her but her gaze.
“…Who?”

lines.japanese: 冷気をまとう音吐で、忍の耳を凍てつかせる。
lines.english: Her voice came wrapped in cold air and froze Shinobu's ears.
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 「何の用？」
lines.english: “What do you want?”

lines.japanese: 「用って……」
lines.english: “What do I…?”

lines.japanese:
口ごもる。
　少女は三秒も待たなかった。
lines.english: He faltered. The girl did not wait even three seconds.

lines.japanese: 「音を立てないで。動物が怯えるから」
lines.english: “Don't make noise. You'll frighten the animals.”

lines.japanese: 「……すまない」
lines.english: “…Sorry.”

lines.japanese:
少女は視線を外す。
　もう一片の興味もないとばかりに。
　忍は少し、ほっとしている。
lines.english: The girl looked away. As though he no longer interested her in the slightest. Shinobu felt a little relieved.

lines.japanese:
フェンスの中から睨み付けられたに過ぎない。
　だというのに、忍の方が閉所に追い込まれた感じ
がしてならなかった。
lines.english: She had merely glared at him from inside the fence. And yet Shinobu could not escape the feeling that he was the one who had been cornered in a confined space.

lines.japanese: （……別に帰れとは言われなかったよね）
lines.english: (…She didn't actually tell me to leave.)

lines.japanese:
忍は立ち去ることもなく、その場にとどまって作
業を見守った。
lines.english: Rather than go, Shinobu remained where he was and watched her work.

lines.japanese: フェンスからは手を離した。
lines.english: He did at least take his hands off the fence.

lines.japanese:
黙々と作業をこなす。
　楽しんでいるようでも、逆に嫌がっている風でも
ない。
lines.english: She worked in silence. She did not seem to enjoy it, nor did she appear to dislike it.

lines.japanese:
兎によって生み出された無秩序が秩序へと序列さ
れていく。
lines.english: The rabbits' disorder was being sorted back into order.

lines.japanese:
手順に無駄がないのは、慣れているせいだろうか。
　あれほど鋭利なものを発した少女だが、見られる
ことは意に介していないようだ。
lines.english: Perhaps practice explained the lack of wasted motion. For all the sharpness she had radiated, she did not seem to mind being watched.

lines.japanese:
ぶしつけな忍の視線を浴びながら、気にするでも
ない。
lines.english: Even under Shinobu's rude stare, she showed no concern at all.

lines.japanese: （怒りんぼなわけじゃないのか）
lines.english: (So she isn’t quick-tempered after all.)

lines.japanese:
それから十分間、忍と少女は静寂を共同のものと
した。
lines.english: For the next ten minutes, Shinobu and the girl shared the silence.

lines.japanese:
掃除が終わり、兎に餌をやる。
　気性が大人しい動物だ。
　食事も静かなものだった。
lines.english: She finished cleaning and fed the rabbits. They were mild-tempered animals. Even their meal was quiet.

lines.japanese:
物音一つ立てず、小屋を出る。
　その際、爪先が段差にかかり少女は身を持ち崩した。
lines.english: She left the hutch without making a sound. On the way out, her toe caught on the step and she lost her balance.

lines.japanese: 咄嗟に手を伸ばし、肩を救うように抱き止めた。
lines.english: Instinctively, he reached out and caught her by the shoulders.

lines.japanese: 「……触らないで」
lines.english: “…Don't touch me.”

lines.japanese:
小声である。
　しかし力強かった。
　慌てて、手を離す。
lines.english: Her voice was low. But it was forceful. He hurriedly let go.

lines.japanese:
その頃には、少女は足に力を込めて均衡を回復し
ていた。
lines.english: By then, the girl had braced her legs and recovered her balance.

lines.japanese:
少女は自分が痛烈な言葉を投げかけた相手を、一瞥
だにすることなく去っていく。
lines.english: The girl walked away without a glance at the person she had struck with those cutting words.

lines.japanese:
ただそこにいることしか許さず、存在を認めも接触
を望みもしない。
lines.english: She allowed him nothing but mere presence, neither acknowledging his existence nor desiring contact.

lines.japanese: 本堂沙也加とはそのような少女だった。
lines.english: That was the sort of girl Sayaka Hondou was.

lines.japanese: （あの子は……）
lines.english: (That girl…)

lines.japanese:
砂が舞う。
　季節はずれの寒風は、心中をも吹きぬけていった。
lines.english: Sand swirled. The unseasonable cold wind blew through his heart as well.

lines.japanese:
編入は滞りなく終わった。
　当たり障りのない挨拶に、対応。
lines.english: His transfer went off without a hitch. He returned each innocuous greeting in kind.

lines.japanese: 一週間が過ぎる頃には、もう忍は風景の一部だった。
lines.english: By the end of a week, Shinobu was already part of the scenery.

lines.japanese:
大人しい人間として認知され、別段目立つことも
ない。
lines.english: He came to be known as quiet and drew no particular attention.

lines.japanese:
病弱という印象付けがうまく行ってか、不意の欠
席もそう訝しがられることはなかった。
lines.english: The impression that he was frail had apparently taken hold, for his unexpected absences aroused little suspicion.

lines.japanese:
クラスに一人くらいは、そういう立場の人間がい
るものだ。
lines.english: A class usually had someone like that.

lines.japanese:
他の人間と距離を置き、侵略もされず、一人佇む
ような者が―――
lines.english: Someone who kept a distance from everyone else, suffered no incursions, and stood alone—

lines.japanese:
だが、忍が得た位置には、すでに先客がいたのだ
った。
lines.english: But the position Shinobu had carved out was already occupied.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、じゃ日直さん、号令」
lines.english: “Good morning. All right, who's on duty? Call the class to order.”

lines.japanese:
教師に一歩遅れて、後ろのドアから少女が入って
くる。
lines.english: A girl came in through the rear door a step behind the teacher.

lines.japanese: 「……本堂か」
lines.english: “…Hondou.”

lines.japanese: 無言で一礼。
lines.english: She bowed without a word.

lines.japanese: 「体はいいのか？」
lines.english: “Are you feeling all right?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「わかった、座りなさい」
lines.english: “All right. Take your seat.”

lines.japanese:
忍は横目でその姿を追う。
　彼女もまた、孤島の住人だ。
　そして忍よりいっそう、遠い場所にいる。
lines.english: Shinobu followed her with a sidelong glance. She too was an inhabitant of a solitary island. And her island lay even farther away than his.

lines.japanese:
話しかけてくれば笑顔で応じるくらいは、忍も如
才なくこなす。
lines.english: Shinobu could at least manage the social nicety of smiling when spoken to.

lines.japanese:
しかし沙也加は、一切を拒絶する。
　教師以外、誰もが彼女には声をかけない。
　いない者のように扱う。
lines.english: Sayaka, however, rejected everything. No one but the teachers spoke to her. They treated her as though she were not there.

lines.japanese:
教室はまだ定型化された空間だから、平穏は保た
れる。
lines.english: The classroom still followed a set routine, and that kept the peace.

lines.japanese:
だが不意に沙也加がまじった瞬間、ピリピリとし
た緊張に支配されることがよくある。
lines.english: But whenever Sayaka unexpectedly entered the mix, a prickling tension often took over.

lines.japanese: 怯えによって。
lines.english: Born of fear.

lines.japanese:
沙也加は寡黙である。
　なぜ怯えられねばならないのか。
　忍は初対面を思い出す。
lines.english: Sayaka was taciturn. Why, then, did people fear her? Shinobu remembered their first encounter.

lines.japanese: あの、目―――
lines.english: Those eyes—

lines.japanese:
強い人間の目だった。
　強すぎる者は、時に疎外される。
lines.english: They were the eyes of a strong person. Those who are too strong are sometimes cast out.

lines.japanese:
いや、沙也加の側から疎外しているのでは
なかったか？
lines.english: No—wasn't it Sayaka who was shutting everyone else out?

lines.japanese: 気になった。
lines.english: It nagged at him.

lines.japanese:
沙也加は黒板を注視しているが、時折、こちらに
視線を向けてくる。
lines.english: Sayaka watched the blackboard intently, but now and then she turned her eyes his way.

lines.japanese:
忍の方が窓に近い。
　そのたびに目をそらすのだが、沙也加の関心はど
うやら窓の外らしい。
lines.english: Shinobu sat closer to the window. Each time she looked, he averted his eyes, though Sayaka's interest seemed to lie outside.

lines.japanese:
目線には微妙なズレがあった。
　さて、きっかけは何なのだ？
lines.english: The lines of their gazes were subtly misaligned. What, then, had started all this?

lines.japanese:
どのようにして、誰も沙也加という島に立ち寄ら
なくなったのだろう？
lines.english: How had it come to pass that no one visited the island called Sayaka?

lines.japanese:
忍が相手にされないのは、目立たなく、つまらな
いからだ。
lines.english: People paid Shinobu no attention because he was inconspicuous and dull.

lines.japanese:
だが沙也加は、集団の中心にいてもおかしくはな
い器量を持っている。
lines.english: But Sayaka had all the qualities needed to stand at the center of the group.

lines.japanese:
簒奪されたのか？
　自ら遠いままに捨て置いたのか。
lines.english: Had that position been usurped? Or had she herself cast it aside and kept her distance?

lines.japanese:
少女は触るな、と言った。
　怒るでもなく、ただ必要な言葉を口にした。
lines.english: The girl had told him not to touch her. She had not been angry. She had simply said what needed saying.

lines.japanese:
嫌ではないのだ。
　他者などどうでもよい。興味がない。接触は拒否
する。
lines.english: It was not dislike. Other people simply meant nothing to her. She had no interest in them and refused contact.

lines.japanese:
もし攻撃性の発露としての孤高であるなら、忍が
傍観するのを看過したりはしない。
lines.english: If her chosen isolation were an expression of aggression, she would never have tolerated Shinobu watching her.

lines.japanese: 理由ある孤独なのではないか―――
lines.english: Perhaps there was a reason for her solitude—

lines.japanese: 「貴宮君」
lines.english: “Atemiya.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
思考は中断。
　黒板に意識を向ける。
lines.english: His thoughts broke off. He turned his attention to the blackboard.

lines.japanese: 「前の学校で、ここは？　やってたか？」
lines.english: “Did you cover this at your old school?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、先生。やっていました」
lines.english: “Yes, sir. We did.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、わかるか？」
lines.english: “Then can you solve it?”

lines.japanese: 忍は前に出て、そつなく問題を解いた。
lines.english: Shinobu went to the front and solved the problem without difficulty.

lines.japanese: 「お、よしよし。正解だ」
lines.english: “Oh, good. That's right.”

lines.japanese: 自席に戻り、窓の外などを見てみた。
lines.english: Back at his desk, he looked out the window.

lines.japanese:
正解したら、多少はお目こぼし。
　そんな暗黙のルールが、教室にはあるものだ。
lines.english: Get the answer right, and you were allowed a little leeway. Every classroom had that unspoken rule.

lines.japanese: 今日は曇天のためか、こころなしか外は薄暗い。
lines.english: Perhaps because of the overcast sky, the world outside seemed a little dim today.

lines.japanese:
窓ガラスは透けた鏡となって、教室内の光景を反
射している。
lines.english: The window glass became a translucent mirror, reflecting the scene inside the classroom.

lines.japanese: そのとき、気付いた。
lines.english: That was when he noticed.

lines.japanese:
本堂沙也加は、ガラス越しの反射で、忍を見てい
たことに。
lines.english: Sayaka Hondou was watching him in the window's reflection.

lines.japanese:
しばし呼吸が止まる。
　その程度にはショッキングだった。
lines.english: It was startling enough to stop his breath for a moment.

lines.japanese:
やがて沙也加は、慌てることもなく自分のタイミ
ングで視線を外した。
　ちょうど、
lines.english: Eventually, without any haste, Sayaka chose her own moment to look away. Just then—

lines.japanese: 「本堂、ここわかるか？」
lines.english: “Hondou, can you do this one?”

lines.japanese:
言葉短い返答を耳に、忍も教科書に目を戻す。
　心中に輪を重ねた波紋が、わずかに集中を乱した。
lines.english: At her terse reply, Shinobu returned his eyes to his textbook. The concentric ripples in his heart disturbed his concentration, if only slightly.

lines.japanese:
昼休みともなれば、まったく誰とも会話しないと
いうわけにはいかない。
lines.english: By lunchtime, it was impossible to get through the day without speaking to anyone.

lines.japanese:
特に同じ班になった人間とは。
　それを思うと少し気が重い。
lines.english: Especially the members of his own group. The thought weighed on him a little.

lines.japanese:
忍はわざと時間をかけて、配膳室からの帰路を歩
んだ。
lines.english: Shinobu deliberately took his time on the walk back from the school kitchen.

lines.japanese:
給食容器を返却しに行くのが、給食当番である忍
に割り振られた仕事だった。
lines.english: As one of the children on lunch duty, he had been assigned the job of returning the serving containers.

lines.japanese: 「貴宮、給食室わかった？」
lines.english: “Atemiya, you find the school kitchen all right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「ご苦労。もうだいぶ慣れたろ？」
lines.english: “Good work. You're pretty used to this place now, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「おっけ。次から一人な。まあ来週から次の班で
　カンケーねーけど」
lines.english: “Okay. Next time you can go by yourself. Not that it matters— another group's on duty next week.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
いつもなら、会話はここで終わる。
　積極的に弾ませることを忍はしない。
　できない、とも言える。
lines.english: Ordinarily, the conversation would end there. Shinobu made no effort to keep it lively. One might also say he was incapable of doing so.

lines.japanese:
笑い戯れる少年少女らの日々は、忍の理解を超え
ている。
lines.english: The laughing, playful lives of the other boys and girls lay beyond Shinobu's understanding.

lines.japanese:
一週間経過してもまだ慣れるものではない。
　戸惑いが表に出るタイプでもないため、ごく大人
しい少年に見えるに過ぎない。
lines.english: Even after a week, he still wasn’t used to them. Since he was not the sort to show his bewilderment, he merely seemed like a very quiet boy.

lines.japanese:
内面には、無垢といえば聞こえの良い、情緒の育
ち損ねた虚無の穴がぽっかりと無数に空いている。
lines.english: Countless voids yawned inside him where his emotions had failed to grow— a condition almost wholesome-sounding if one called it innocence.

lines.japanese:
穴はあらゆる喜怒哀楽を底へと吸い込む。
　人の有髄神経の軸索は髄鞘が形成されねば機能を
果たすことはできない。
lines.english: Those holes swallowed every emotion—joy, anger, sorrow, pleasure—to the bottom. The axons of human myelinated nerves cannot function unless their myelin sheath has formed.

lines.japanese:
言語面でのその発達は生後ある程度までの時期に
限定され、即ち狼少年はたとえ保護されても人語を
解するようにはならない。
lines.english: That same development in language is limited to a certain period after birth; thus even if a feral child is rescued, the child will never come to understand human speech.

lines.japanese:
栓のない湯船に水を張る行為にも似ている。
　忍の心にも、同様の病巣があった。
lines.english: It was like trying to fill a bathtub with no plug. Shinobu's heart bore a similar lesion.

lines.japanese:
忍は家族を持たない。
　忍は友を持たない。
lines.english: Shinobu had no family. Shinobu had no friends.

lines.japanese:
どう処して良いのか、判断するための力を持って
いなかった。

lines.english: “You picking a fight, string bean?”

lines.japanese: 「クク、オレ様の足の長さのことを言っているな？」
lines.english: “Heh. You mean my long legs?”

lines.japanese: 「検証します」
lines.english: “Let's test that.”

lines.japanese:
眼鏡が光る。
　章二が猛った。
lines.english: Her glasses flashed. Shouji flared up.

lines.japanese: 「来いやオラ！」
lines.english: “Bring it on!”

lines.japanese: 「ミス葉子」
lines.english: “Miss Youko.”
“Ma'am.”

lines.japanese: 「並んで」
lines.english: “Stand beside him.”
“Ma'am.”
“Heh…”

lines.japanese: 肩の高さが段違いであった。
lines.english: Their shoulders were at completely different heights.

lines.japanese: 「オレの方が高いようだ」
lines.english: “Looks like I'm taller.”

lines.japanese: 「背はね」
lines.english: “In height.”

lines.japanese: 「メジャーかもん」
lines.english: “Tape measure, come on.”

lines.japanese: 差し出す斎。
lines.english: Itsuki produced one.

lines.japanese: 「斎……おまえ？」
lines.english: “Itsuki… you too?”

lines.japanese: 「さすが、用意がいいわ」
lines.english: “Always prepared.”

lines.japanese: 「いいかな」
lines.english: “May I say something?”
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 「僕の目には、章二は劣勢に見える」
lines.english: “It looks to me like you're at a disadvantage, Shouji.”

lines.japanese: 腕を組み、他人事のように忍は言う。
lines.english: Arms folded, Shinobu spoke as though the matter had nothing to do with him.

lines.japanese: 「忍さん、しょうじのやつ、ニヤニヤしてますぜ？」
lines.english: “Sir Shinobu, that Shouji fellow is smirking.”

lines.japanese: 「一見互角」
lines.english: “They look evenly matched at first.”

lines.japanese: 「だが見るんだ。章二は汗を流して呼吸も荒い」
lines.english: “But look. Shouji is sweating, and his breathing is ragged.”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、本当だ！」
lines.english: “Y-you're right!”

lines.japanese: 「対して、葉子の方は息一つ乱れてない」
lines.english: “Youko, on the other hand, is not even breathing hard.”

lines.japanese: 「待てい！」
lines.english: “Hold it!”

lines.japanese: 「これは発電機を運んできたからだ！」
lines.english: “That's because I carried the generator here!”

lines.japanese: 「よってこの戦い、章二は不利だ」
lines.english: “Thus, Shouji enters this contest at a disadvantage.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほどー」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese:
「胴長短足のくせしてはぁはぁ言って、最低ですね
　こいつ」
lines.english: “Panting away on those short little legs under that long torso. What a loser he is.”

lines.japanese: 「待てぇぇぇい！」
lines.english: “I said hold iiiit!”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく葉子は体型がフィギュアのようによくで
　きてるから、章二だときついかも」
lines.english: “Anyway, Youko is built as perfectly as a figurine, so Shouji may be outmatched.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぃぎーる」
lines.english: “Fee-geer.”

lines.japanese: 「それ、フランス読みね」
lines.english: “That would be the French pronunciation.”

lines.japanese:
「章二も決して短足というわけではない。むしろモ
　デル体型と言っても良いんだけど、足の長さだけ
　で見ると―――」
lines.english: “Shouji's legs aren't short by any means. You could even say he has a model's build, but if we're judging the length of the legs alone—”

lines.japanese: 「計測をはじめます」
lines.english: “Commencing measurement.”

lines.japanese:
メジャーのはしを、床に当てた。
　章二は葉子から離れた。
lines.english: She set the end of the measuring tape against the floor. Shouji stepped away from Youko.

lines.japanese: 「こら、なぜ離れるの？」
lines.english: “Hey, why are you moving away?”

lines.japanese:
「つきあってられるか。
　オレは発電機をセッティングする」
lines.english: “I’m not playing along with this. I’m going to set up the generator.”

lines.japanese: 機械を乗せた台車を、奥に運んでいった。
lines.english: He wheeled the cart bearing the machine toward the back.

lines.japanese: 「逃げた……」
lines.english: “He ran away…”

lines.japanese: 「手伝え忍！」
lines.english: “Help me, Shinobu!”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい」
lines.english: “All right, all right.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあんたの不戦勝」
lines.english: “Then Youko wins by default.”

lines.japanese: ぽんぽん。
lines.english: Pat, pat.

lines.japanese: 「チャンピオーン」
lines.english: “Cham-pee-on.”

lines.japanese:
両腕を頭上に掲げた。
　重なった皆の時間が、廃工場という場所を軸に、
等しく刻まれていく。
lines.english: She thrust both arms over her head. Here in the abandoned factory, the time they shared was being measured out equally for them all.

lines.japanese:
それは六人の時間だった。
　平和で幸福な、ひとときだった。
lines.english: It was time that belonged to the six of them. A peaceful, happy interlude.
(But—)

lines.japanese:
何か足りない。
　忍はそう感じた。
lines.english: Something was missing. That was how Shinobu felt.

lines.japanese:
今、工場には沙也加がいる。
　書から顔をあげると、端正な横顔が忍同様、手元
のハードカバーに向けられていた。
lines.english: Sayaka was at the factory now. When Shinobu looked up from his own book, her finely cut profile was still turned toward the hardcover in her hands.

lines.japanese:
美しい、という言い回しは若い忍には遠い。
　単純な形容では、説明できないものが沙也加には
ある。
lines.english: The word beautiful still felt remote to the young Shinobu. There was something in Sayaka that no simple adjective could explain.

lines.japanese:
意志が透けるためか。
　苦難の過去があるためか。
　工場の独特の空気がそう見せるのか。
lines.english: Was it the will shining through her? The hardships in her past? Or merely the peculiar air of the factory?

lines.japanese:
わからないし、いずれでも構わなかった。
　淡い感動に包まれて、じっと見てしまう。
　理由が必要で、好ましく思うわけではない。
lines.english: He did not know, nor did it matter which. Wrapped in quiet wonder, he found himself staring. It was not as though he needed a reason to find her appealing.
“…What is it?”

lines.japanese: 実際は、もっと早くに気付いていたのかも知れない。
lines.english: In truth, she might have noticed much sooner.

lines.japanese:
一定量の感情を受けることで、トリガーが引かれ
たのかも知れない。
　戸惑いの見られない、沙也加の反応だ。
lines.english: Perhaps the trigger had been pulled only after she absorbed a certain measure of feeling. There was no confusion in Sayaka's response.

lines.japanese: 「君を見てた」
lines.english: “I was looking at you.”

lines.japanese:
面差しに、筋組織一本分の変化さえもない。
　白磁の彫像を思わせ……しかし本堂沙也加は生身
の人間である。
lines.english: Not so much as a single muscle fiber shifted in her face. She called to mind a statue of white porcelain… yet Sayaka Hondou was flesh and blood.

lines.japanese:
立ち上がった。
　忍に立ち寄る。
lines.english: She rose. Came over to Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
首に腕がまわされた。
　両者の隙間に、芳香がこもる。
　新雪が含む清冽な微香を夢想させた。
lines.english: Her arms slipped around his neck. The space between them filled with fragrance. It conjured the clean, faint scent one imagined in new-fallen snow.

lines.japanese: 間近に沙也加の顔。
lines.english: Sayaka's face, very close.

lines.japanese: 「……つらいわね」
lines.english: “…It's hard, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「そうでもないよ」
lines.english: “Not particularly.”

lines.japanese: 「いずれ、みんな散り散りになっていくのに」
lines.english: “Even though we'll all go our separate ways someday.”

lines.japanese: 「そうならなければいいと思う」
lines.english: “I hope it doesn’t come to that.”

lines.japanese: 「私たちは互いに、何も拘束するものじゃない」
lines.english: “We have no hold over one another.”

lines.japanese:
唇が、意味もなく頬をかする。
　黒曜石のような瞳を目蓋で隠してしまい、どこか
陶然としたものを怜悧さの中に感じさせた。
lines.english: Her lips brushed his cheek without meaning anything in particular. Her lids concealed those obsidian eyes, lending something almost rapturous to her cool intelligence.

lines.japanese: 理性は瞳に宿るものだからだ。
lines.english: Reason made its home in the eyes, after all.

lines.japanese:
「だから、誰かの行動を、止めることはできないの
　よ」
lines.english: “So we cannot stop anyone from doing what they choose to do.”

lines.japanese: 「……それをするには、支配するしかない」
lines.english: “…The only way would be to control them.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「そうすれば簡単だものね」
lines.english: “That would make it simple.”

lines.japanese: 「……沙也加はそういうのは、嫌い？」
lines.english: “…Would you hate that sort of thing, Sayaka?”

lines.japanese:
「私一人なら、何を拒むでもないと、あなたは知っ
　ているでしょう？」
lines.english: “You know that where I alone am concerned, there is nothing I would refuse.”

lines.japanese: 「あの誓いは、ナシでさ」
lines.english: “Let's set that vow aside for a minute.”

lines.japanese: 「ナシは、ナシよ」
lines.english: “No setting it aside.”

lines.japanese:
くすり、と耳元に笑う声が転がる。
　忍は両腕を伸ばし、沙也加の細い腰を引き寄せた。
lines.english: A soft laugh tumbled into his ear. Shinobu reached out with both arms and drew Sayaka's slender waist closer.

lines.japanese: 「……ん……しにくいわ」
lines.english: “…Mm… that makes it difficult.”

lines.japanese:
そのまま忍は沙也加の腹に、顔をうずめた。
　そして少しだけ、腕に力を込めた。
lines.english: Shinobu buried his face against her stomach. Then tightened his arms just a little.

lines.japanese:
長い時間が、過ぎ去った。
　沙也加は何も言わない。
lines.english: A long while passed. Sayaka said nothing.

lines.japanese: 「こないだの……笛子のこと、ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you… for what you did for Fueko the other day.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、当然のことよ」
lines.english: “No need. It was only natural.”

lines.japanese: 「私の友人でもあるのだから」
lines.english: “She is my friend too.”

lines.japanese: 「怖いんだ」
lines.english: “I'm afraid.”

lines.japanese: 「もしものことが起こったらって思うと」
lines.english: “When I think about something happening…”

lines.japanese:
「自分の意志で離れるのもいや。不慮の出来事で失
　うのもいや」
lines.english: “You don't want anyone to leave by choice, and you don't want to lose anyone to an accident.”

lines.japanese: 「欠けたくないのね」
lines.english: “You want no one missing.”

lines.japanese: 「欠けたくはないよ」
lines.english: “I don't want anyone missing.”

lines.japanese: 「輪っかが欠けたら、意味を失う」
lines.english: “A broken circle loses its meaning.”

lines.japanese:
「いっそのこと、ここに全員で住めば……と思った
　ことは？」
lines.english: “Have you ever thought… that perhaps we should all simply live here together?”

lines.japanese: 「あるよ。いつも考えてる」
lines.english: “I have. I think about it all the time.”

lines.japanese:
「でも……それをしたら、時間が止まってしまいそ
　うで……」
lines.english: “But… if we did, I feel as though time itself might stop…”

lines.japanese: 「今を閉じこめてしまうと？」
lines.english: “As though we would shut the present away?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、イヤ？」
lines.english: “Would that bother you?”

lines.japanese: 「……どうだろう。深く考えたことはないけど……」
lines.english: “…I don't know. I've never thought very deeply about it…”

lines.japanese: 「不健全じゃないか」
lines.english: “That can't be healthy.”
“Heh heh…”

lines.japanese: 珍しく、笑うのである。
lines.english: She laughed—an uncommon thing.

lines.japanese:
「ごめんなさい。不健全という言葉が、こんなに面
　白かったのははじめてだったものだから」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I don't believe I've ever found the word ‘unhealthy’ quite so amusing.”

lines.japanese: 「……おかしいかな」
lines.english: “…Was it that strange?”

lines.japanese: 少し憮然と、忍。
lines.english: Shinobu looked faintly put out.

lines.japanese:
「きっとあなたは、あるがままに平穏であることを、
　望んでいるのね」
lines.english: “I think you want a peace that leaves things just as they are.”

lines.japanese: 「あるがままに？」
lines.english: “Just as they are?”

lines.japanese:
「不自然に手を入れないまま、皆と一緒にいられる
　ような……そんな絵画のような、明日」
lines.english: “A tomorrow where you can remain with everyone without unnaturally changing anything… a tomorrow like a painting.”

lines.japanese: 「いいな、それ」
lines.english: “I like that.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、寂しくも、あるかな。絵画の中の幸せって」
lines.english: “Maybe there'd be something lonely about happiness inside a painting, though.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「いつか大人になって、こういうことを納得できる
　日が、来るんだろうか」
lines.english: “I wonder if, when we grow up, we'll come to accept things like this.”

lines.japanese: 「どちらにしても」
lines.english: “Either way…”

lines.japanese: 忍から身を離す。
lines.english: She drew away from Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「私の決断だけは終わっているのだから」
lines.english: “Whatever happens, I've already made my own decision.”

lines.japanese: 「……いつもありがとうね、沙也加」
lines.english: “…Thank you, as always, Sayaka.”

lines.japanese:
身をくの字に折って、忍の額にキスをした。
　恋愛というよりは、挨拶のキス。
lines.english: Bending at the waist, she kissed Shinobu's forehead. Less a lover's kiss than a kiss of greeting.

lines.japanese: 「何か持ってくるわね」
lines.english: “I'll get us something to drink.”

lines.japanese:
余薫だけを置き土産に、沙也加は湯を沸かしに行
った。
lines.english: Leaving only the last trace of her fragrance behind, Sayaka went to boil some water.

lines.japanese:
忍はしばらく、そのままぼんやりとしていた。
　一分ほど経っただろうか。
　入口の鉄扉が、遠慮がちに開かれる。
lines.english: Shinobu sat there in a daze for a while. Perhaps a minute passed. The iron door at the entrance opened hesitantly.

lines.japanese: 「やあ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese:
様子がおかしい。
　ぎこちない足取りで自分の椅子を広げ、おぼつか
ない様子で腰を下ろす。
lines.english: Something was wrong. With stiff, awkward steps, she unfolded her chair and lowered herself onto it none too steadily.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「ヴェ、別に？　何でもないわよ？」
lines.english: “B—Nothing. Why? Nothing's wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「ヴェってキミ……」
lines.english: “What's with the ‘b’?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっとどもっただけじゃない！」
lines.english: “I-I just stumbled over my words!”

lines.japanese:
忍は『むーん』と笛子を見つめた。
　笛子も見られているのはわかった。
　わかって、気付いていないフリをした。
lines.english: Shinobu stared at Fueko with a long ‘hmm.’ Fueko knew perfectly well he was staring. She knew, and pretended not to notice.

lines.japanese: 笛子には不利な戦いだ。
lines.english: Fueko was fighting a losing battle.

lines.japanese: 「……そうそう……面白い本があったから……」
lines.english: “…Oh, right… I found an interesting book…”

lines.japanese:
鞄を膝の上に乗せようとして、落とした。
　中身がざらっと地面に扇を描いた。
　教科書、ノート、小説数冊。
lines.english: She tried to set her bag on her lap and dropped it. Its contents fanned across the floor with a clatter. Textbooks, notebooks, several novels.

lines.japanese:
中には、有名な少年愛小説がまじっていたが、今
ツッコミどころはそこではない。
lines.english: A famous boys' love novel was among them, but that wasn't the thing worth remarking on just then.

lines.japanese:
沈黙。
　やがて、
lines.english: Silence. At length—
“…Did you see?”

lines.japanese: びく、と笛子の肩が震えた。
lines.english: Fueko's shoulders gave a start.

lines.japanese: 「見られたか」
lines.english: “So you did.”

lines.japanese: 忍は自分の頭を、拳固でこつと叩いた。
lines.english: Shinobu rapped himself lightly on the head with one fist.

lines.japanese: 「……キスシテタ……キスシテタ……」
lines.english: “…You were kissing… You were kissing…”

lines.japanese:
組んだ手を膝の間に吊るし、笛子は地面に視線を
落とす。
lines.english: Her clasped hands dangling between her knees, Fueko lowered her gaze to the floor.

lines.japanese: 「暗い」
lines.english: “That's dark.”

lines.japanese:
「……どっかの、馬の骨だったら、何か言ったと思
　う……そんくらいショック」
lines.english: “…If it had been some nobody, I think I'd have had plenty to say… That's how shocked I am.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、実はね」
lines.english: “Well, actually…”

lines.japanese: 冷静でいた方が勝つ。
lines.english: Whoever remained calm would win.

lines.japanese: 「ただのキスなんだ」
lines.english: “It was only a kiss.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、ただのキスか」
lines.english: “Oh. Only a kiss.”

lines.japanese: 「ふつーふつー」
lines.english: “Normal, normal.”

lines.japanese: 「だね。あはは」
lines.english: “Right. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは」
lines.english: “Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 胸ぐらを掴まれる忍であった。
lines.english: Fueko seized Shinobu by the collar.

lines.japanese: 「……んなわけあるかい」
lines.english: “Like hell it is.”

lines.japanese: 「スイマセン……」
lines.english: “I'm sorry…”

lines.japanese: 「詳細」
lines.english: “Details.”
“Actually…”

lines.japanese: 「知り合ってから、わりと普通にしてたんです」
lines.english: “Ever since we met, it’s been pretty normal for us.”

lines.japanese: 「……普通の意味がわからん」
lines.english: “…I no longer understand what ‘normally’ means.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、その……エロい意味じゃなくて、挨拶？
　みたいな」
lines.english: “I mean, it isn't… sexual. It's more like a greeting? Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 笛子が重いものを背負い始めた気がした。
lines.english: Fueko looked as though she had taken some grave burden upon herself.

lines.japanese:
「だ、だからさ、お米の国の人がよくやるじゃ
　ない。あんな感じで」
lines.english: “I-it's like in America. People do it all the time, right? Like that.”

lines.japanese: 「文字通り挨拶で？　キスを？」
lines.english: “Literally as a greeting? You kiss?”

lines.japanese:
「そうだね……親しみの証といいますか。沙也加は
　ほら、育ちが良すぎて、気軽な愛情表現とか知ら
　ないというか」
lines.english: “Right… A sign of affection, you might say. Sayaka was brought up so properly that she never learned easy, casual ways of showing it.”

lines.japanese: 「確かに、そういうところはあるわね……うーん」
lines.english: “She does have that side to her… Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
「こっちから無理矢理したとかないよ？　ただ知り
　合ってからしばらくは……向こうがすることを拒
　むことってしにくくって……」
lines.english: “It's not like I forced her, okay? It's just that, for a while after we met… it was hard to say no to anything she chose to do…”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……わかったわ。不問にしておく」
lines.english: “Fine… I understand. I'll drop it.”

lines.japanese: 「助かる」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなん、みんなにバレたら大変よあんた」
lines.english: “You'd be in serious trouble if the others found out.”

lines.japanese:
「なーんとなく沙也加もわかってはいるみたいなん
　だけど……だから人前ではしないし」
lines.english: “I get the sense Sayaka understands that too… so we never do it in front of anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとつ確認してい？」
lines.english: “Can I ask one thing?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだい」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ラブチュー？」
lines.english: “A romantic kiss?”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「間が気になるっての！」
lines.english: “That pause is what worries me!”

lines.japanese: ぎりぎりと締め上げられる。
lines.english: Her grip ground tighter.

lines.japanese: 「苦しい……」
lines.english: “Can't breathe…”

lines.japanese:
「わかっててやってんのかってたまに思う。
　このボウヤは」
lines.english: “Sometimes I think you know exactly what you're doing. This boy, honestly.”

lines.japanese: 「エンザイです……」
lines.english: “I stand falsely accused…”

lines.japanese: 「まあいいわ。女に二言はない」
lines.english: “Never mind. A woman doesn't go back on her word.”

lines.japanese:
ぽいっ。
　忍を打ち捨てる。
lines.english: Toss. She cast Shinobu aside.

lines.japanese:
「ごほ、ごほっ……
　笛子、うちらの中で一番男らしいよ……」
lines.english: “Cough, cough… Fueko, you're the manliest one of us all…”

lines.japanese: 「乙女に対して素敵な言葉ありがとう」
lines.english: “What a charming thing to say to a maiden. Thank you.”
“…Where's Hondou?”

lines.japanese: 「飲み物作ってるんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “Making drinks, I think.”

lines.japanese: 「時間、かかる……か」
lines.english: “That’ll take a while… won’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「沙也加だから」
lines.english: “She's Sayaka.”

lines.japanese:
どんなに時間がない時でも、一滴一滴真心を込め
てドリップ。
lines.english: No matter how little time remained, she poured every drop with loving care.
“Hey…”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「挨拶、って言ったよね」
lines.english: “You said it was a greeting.”

lines.japanese:
顔が少し赤い。
　彼女にしては、珍しいことに声も震えている。
lines.english: Her face was slightly red. Unusually for her, her voice trembled too.

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yeah.”
“Then—”

lines.japanese:
目を閉じて、大きく呼吸をする。
　開かれた瞳は、決意の色合いを帯びて、鋭い。
lines.english: She closed her eyes and took a deep breath. When she opened them again, they were sharp with resolve.

lines.japanese: 「私にもできる？」
lines.english: “Could you do that with me too?”

lines.japanese: 忍は数秒、呼吸と時間を忘れ去った。
lines.english: For several seconds, Shinobu forgot both time and breath.

lines.japanese: 「……ええと」

「深い意味はないから……ねえ、どうなの？
　できるの？　できないの？」
lines.english: “There’s no deeper meaning to it… Well? Can you, or can’t you?”

lines.japanese:
できる。
　できない。
lines.english: He could. He could not.

lines.japanese:
心中、むしられた花弁が細かに散っていく。
　しかしそれが何枚の花びらを持つ花なのかを決め
ていなかった。
lines.english: In his mind, plucked petals scattered in a fine rain. But he had never decided how many petals the flower possessed.

lines.japanese: 結局、忍は、
lines.english: In the end, Shinobu said—

lines.japanese: 「目、閉じてよ」
lines.english: “Close your eyes.”

lines.japanese:
少しぎょっとしたように身を竦ませ、そして……
男の言葉に従った。
lines.english: She flinched, a little startled, and then… did as the young man told her.

lines.japanese: 選択肢は次の階層に移る。
lines.english: The decision tree descended to its next level.

lines.japanese:
額。
　頬。
　目蓋。
lines.english: Forehead. Cheek. Eyelid.
…Lips.

lines.japanese:
こういう時、人は無数のことを考え、そして最初
の疑問に舞い戻るものだ。
lines.english: At times like this, a person thinks of countless things—only to return to the original question.

lines.japanese: 両肩に手を置く。
lines.english: He placed his hands on her shoulders.

lines.japanese:
男らしいはずの笛子の体が、非常に小柄であると
わかる。
lines.english: Fueko, supposedly so manly, was in fact very slight beneath his hands.

lines.japanese: 彼女は女の子でしかない。
lines.english: She was only a girl.

lines.japanese:
肩の関節が、すっぽりとてのひらにおさまってし
まった。
lines.english: Her entire shoulder joint fit snugly inside his palm.
“……Nngh.”

lines.japanese:
ぎゅっと、眉間に皺が寄った。
　爆発してしまいそうな羞恥に耐えていた。
　結局、忍が唇をつけたのは目蓋だった。
lines.english: Her brow knotted tight. She was enduring embarrassment intense enough to make her burst. In the end, Shinobu placed his lips against her eyelid.

lines.japanese:
唇を離す。
　ずっと笛子は震え続けていた。
lines.english: He drew his lips away. Fueko had been trembling all along.
“…Fueko?”
“Mm…”

lines.japanese: 「終わったよ」
lines.english: “It's over.”

lines.japanese:
片目を開けて、不満げな面持ち。
　その意味するところが、忍にも察せられた。
lines.english: She opened one eye, looking dissatisfied. Even Shinobu could guess what that meant.
“…Fue—”

lines.japanese:
そして忍は考えた。
　沙也加にしていることを、笛子にできない道理は
ない、と。
lines.english: And Shinobu thought: There was no reason he could not do with Fueko what he did with Sayaka.

lines.japanese: 片手で、うつむきかげんな顎を、持ち上げた。
lines.english: With one hand, he lifted her downcast chin.
“N-no…”

lines.japanese:
声があまりにも細く高かったので、忍は一瞬、
別人かと錯覚しかけた。
lines.english: Her voice was so thin and high that for an instant Shinobu almost mistook her for someone else.

lines.japanese:
しかし眼前、指に掛けられたのは、紛れもない
伊月笛子である。
lines.english: Yet the person before him, her chin resting on his fingers, was unmistakably Fueko Izuki.

lines.japanese:
やらねばならない。
　しかしためらいが、抜けない。
　顔を重ねるため、大きな意志の力を要した。
lines.english: He had to do it. Yet the hesitation would not leave him. Bringing their faces together demanded a great act of will.

lines.japanese: 唇が、唇に、触れる―――
lines.english: Their lips were about to meet—

lines.japanese: 「うがー！」
lines.english: “Raaagh!”

lines.japanese: 直前で、突き飛ばされたのである。
lines.english: At the very last instant, she shoved him away.
“…Whoa, whoa!”

lines.japanese: 尻餅をつく。
lines.english: He landed on his rear.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、つい……」
lines.english: “Sorry, I just…”

lines.japanese: 「なんという仕打ち……」
lines.english: “Such cruelty…”
“…Deepest remorse.”

lines.japanese: 「いいけど……いいの？」
lines.english: “It's fine… but are you sure?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だから」
lines.english: “No, I mean…”

lines.japanese: 戸惑い、ためらい、
lines.english: Confusion. Hesitation.

lines.japanese: 「悪いかなって思ってさ」
lines.english: “I thought it might be wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「……またそれは」
lines.english: “…That's rather…”

lines.japanese: 「こないだのコトもあるし」
lines.english: “After what happened the other day, too.”

lines.japanese:
「あとそこで隠れてる本堂沙也加、もういいから出
　てきてくんない？　せっかくのお茶がゆるくなっ
　ちゃ勿体ないでしょ」
lines.english: “Also, Sayaka Hondou, you've been hiding over there long enough. Would you come out now? It'd be a shame to let the tea go lukewarm.”

lines.japanese: と、給湯室から本当に沙也加が姿を見せた。
lines.english: And Sayaka did, in fact, emerge from the kitchenette.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの、怒鳴ったりして？」
lines.english: “Why were you shouting?”

lines.japanese: 「とぼけるわけね……ま、いいけどね」
lines.english: “So you're playing innocent… Fine. Whatever.”

lines.japanese: 盛大にため息をついた。
lines.english: She heaved an enormous sigh.

lines.japanese: 「はい、コーヒー」
lines.english: “Here. Coffee.”

lines.japanese: 盆に乗せたカップのうち、ひとつを笛子に渡した。
lines.english: She handed Fueko one of the cups on her tray.

lines.japanese: 「あんがと」
lines.english: “Thanks.”
“……Oh. What about mine?”

lines.japanese: 沙也加は微笑んだ。
lines.english: Sayaka smiled.

lines.japanese:
「時間がなくて用意できなかったの。自分で淹れて
　くれる？」
lines.english: “I ran out of time and couldn't make yours. Would you mind brewing it yourself?”

lines.japanese: 逆らえるはずもなかった。
lines.english: He couldn't possibly defy her.

lines.japanese:
いつも通りの時間。目が覚める。
　五時。
　運動着に着替えて外に。
lines.english: He woke at the usual time. Five o'clock. He changed into workout clothes and went outside.

lines.japanese:
夜気をわずかに残して肌寒い朝が、なぜかもっと
も体調の安定する時間帯だ。
　いわゆる個人差なのだろう。
lines.english: For some reason, the chilly morning, with a trace of night air still in it, was when his body felt most settled. People were different, he supposed.

lines.japanese:
忍は運動するに最適な時間として、朝を選ぶ。
　ランニング。
　いつものコースを時間をかけて踏みしめる。
lines.english: Shinobu had chosen morning as the ideal time for exercise. A run. He settled into his usual route, taking his time with every step.

lines.japanese:
時間を気にせずぼんやりと走る。
　同じリズムで足を運ぶうち、意識が霞がかってく
る気がした。
lines.english: He ran absently, paying no attention to the time. As his feet settled into an unchanging rhythm, his awareness seemed to grow hazy.

lines.japanese:
このタイミングが何よりも好きだった。
　自宅の前に戻る。
lines.english: He loved this moment more than any other. He returned to the front of his house.

lines.japanese:
少し走り足りない気もするが、足を止めてみれば、
それまで聞こえもしなかった心臓の音が直に鼓膜に
伝わってきてうるさい。
lines.english: He felt he could have run farther, but once he stopped, the heartbeat he hadn’t heard until then beat loudly right against his eardrums.
“…Whew.”

lines.japanese:
幸い、煩わしい頭痛もなく、呼吸を整えるわずか
な時間をまどろみのように過ごした。
lines.english: Fortunately, there was no nagging headache, and he spent those few moments steadying his breath in a kind of doze.

lines.japanese: 休み時間。
lines.english: Between classes.

lines.japanese:
沙也加が教室を出て行くのを見届け、意識の向く
先がなくなると、途端に周囲の雑然とした会話が意
味を持ち始めた。
lines.english: After watching Sayaka leave the classroom, Shinobu had nowhere left to direct his attention. The jumble of conversation around him abruptly began to make sense.

lines.japanese:
街でのこと。
　ネットでのこと。
　テレビでのこと。
lines.english: Things that had happened around town. Things from the internet. Things on television.

lines.japanese:
数十人分の会話が、忍を取り巻いている。
　カクテルパーティー効果というものがある。
lines.english: The conversations of dozens of people surrounded Shinobu. There was a phenomenon known as the cocktail party effect.

hyperlinks.preview: Even at a crowded party where many people are talking at once, conversations about us have a curious

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Even at a crowded party where many people are talking at once, conversations about us have a curious

lines.japanese:
自分に関係する言葉を雑音から抽出する、聴覚の
著しい機能のことだ。
lines.english: It was the remarkable auditory ability to pick personally relevant words out of a mass of noise.

lines.japanese:
忍がキャッチしたのは、自分自身についてではな
かった。
lines.english: What Shinobu picked up, however, wasn't about him.

lines.japanese: 「……本堂って、怪しくね？」
lines.english: “…Doesn’t Hondou seem kinda sus?”

lines.japanese: 発言がそこに至る経緯まで、認識は一瞬で遡った。
lines.english: His mind instantly retraced the conversation that had led to that remark.

lines.japanese: 「うっそ、マジで？」
lines.english: “No way. Seriously?”

lines.japanese:
「マジマジ。そんで大家が事情聞きに言ったんだけ
　ど、買い込んだ肉が腐ったんだって、こう扉の隙
　間から言うだけで、絶対開けない」
lines.english: “Dead serious. So the landlord went to ask what was going on, but the guy only spoke through the crack in the door. Said some meat he'd bought had gone bad. Wouldn't open up no matter what.”

lines.japanese: 「つか、それ……ヤバくな？」
lines.english: “Dude, that's… pretty bad.”

lines.japanese:
「だろ？　オレん家まで臭い来たもん。お袋ヒステ
　リーになるし、姉貴は男のとこ避難して帰ってこ
　ねーし」
lines.english: “Right? The stink reached my house. My mom threw a fit, and my sister fled to her boyfriend's place and wouldn't come home.”

lines.japanese:
「で、しばらくして……そいつ、いきなり蒸発しち
　ゃったの」
lines.english: “Then after a while… the guy just vanished.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、やべぇ」
lines.english: “Whoa. That's messed up.”

lines.japanese:
「で、大家も近所のオヤジとか集めてさ、鍵使って
　勝手に入ったんだよ、そいつの部屋に」
lines.english: “So the landlord got some guys from the neighborhood together, used his key, and went into the guy's apartment.”

lines.japanese:
「したら……別に死体とかはなかったんだけど、な
　んか変な汁が畳みにバーッと染みついてたって」
lines.english: “When they did… there wasn't a body or anything, but they found this weird fluid soaked all through the tatami.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ？」
lines.english: “What kind of fluid?”

lines.japanese: 「ションベンとかも混じってたみたいだけど……」
lines.english: “Apparently some of it was piss…”

lines.japanese:
「なんか、膿とか血とか、あと体液とか……なんか
　それっぽい感じのだって言ってた。オヤジ軍団に
　医者いてさ」
lines.english: “They said it looked like pus, blood, bodily fluids… Stuff like that. One of those neighborhood guys was a doctor.”

lines.japanese: 「っておい、作ってね？　リアリー？」
lines.english: “Come on, you're making this up. Reeeally?”

lines.japanese: 「リアリーリアリー。マジバナですよ」
lines.english: “Really, really. Swear it's true.”

lines.japanese:
「で、たぶん……自分の血とかじゃないのかって医者
　が言ったらしいぜ」
lines.english: “And the doctor apparently said… it was probably the guy's own blood.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ何。そいつ、生きてるのに腐ってたのか？」
lines.english: “So what? He was rotting while he was still alive?”

lines.japanese:
「臭いだけなら畳からってことらしいけど、そんだ
　け体液垂れ流してて、医者も行かずに部屋にこもっ
　てるのかとか、疑惑つきねー」
lines.english: “They figured the smell itself was probably coming from the tatami, but then you have to wonder why he was leaking that much fluid, refusing to see a doctor, and locking himself in there. So many questions.”

lines.japanese: 「あや（怪）」
lines.english: “Suuus.”

lines.japanese: 「マジあや」
lines.english: “Super sus.”

lines.japanese:
「例のアレってことなんだろうなってうちのオヤジ
　も言ってた。慣れてるな。あや慣れだな」
lines.english: “My old man said it had to be that thing again. Didn't even faze him. Guess he's sus-tomed to it.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そいやアレってさ……」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah. Speaking of that thing…”

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Yeah?”

lines.japanese: 「……本堂って、怪しくね？」
lines.english: “…Doesn't Hondou seem kinda sus?”

lines.japanese:
まったく脈絡なく、沙也加に話が飛ぶということ
が、忍には信じられなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu could not believe the conversation had leaped to Sayaka out of nowhere.

lines.japanese:
彼らが口にしていた都市伝説めいた話と、沙也加
とは何の関連性もない。
lines.english: The urban legend they had been discussing had nothing whatsoever to do with Sayaka.

lines.japanese:
いきりたって否定したい気持ちに駆られたが、そ
んなことをすればかえって怪しまれる。
lines.english: He wanted to leap up and deny it, but doing so would only make them more suspicious.

lines.japanese:
刺激することになる。
　信憑性が増してしまう。
lines.english: It would provoke them. Make the story seem more credible.

lines.japanese:
周囲に届かない程度に舌打ちしてみたが、まるで
気は晴れない。
lines.english: He clicked his tongue softly enough that no one else could hear, but it did nothing to make him feel better.

lines.japanese: 押し黙り、自らの胸裡を吹きすさぶ突風に耐えた。
lines.english: He held his tongue and weathered the gale raging through his chest.

lines.japanese: 「なんかあったけ、本堂てー？」
lines.english: “Wait, what happened with Hondou again?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、おま地元じゃないの？」
lines.english: “Oh, you're not from around here?”

lines.japanese: 「おう、生粋の地元じゃない派」
lines.english: “Yeah. Born-and-bred nonlocal.”

lines.japanese:
「ばかくさ。いや、本堂てよ、子供の頃魔女て言わ
　れてたんよ」
lines.english: “That's dumb. Anyway, Hondou used to be called a witch when we were kids.”

lines.japanese: 「出たよ第二レジェンド。今度は何よ？」
lines.english: “Here comes urban legend number two. What's the story this time?”

lines.japanese:
「それってアレだろ？　あの集団失踪事件と関係し
　てたってヤツ」
lines.english: “You mean the thing about her being involved in that mass disappearance?”

lines.japanese: 第三者が会話にまじってくる。
lines.english: A third student joined the conversation.

lines.japanese:
「おいおい、オレをさしおいておまえも知っちゃっ
　てんの？」
lines.english: “Come on, you know about it and I don't?”

lines.japanese: 「つうか有名だっつ」
lines.english: “It's, like, famous.”

lines.japanese:
「今は大人しいだけだけど、前はなんか怖がられた
　んだろ？」
lines.english: “She's just quiet now, but people used to be scared of her, right?”

lines.japanese: 「おー。すんげービビッてたよ、みんな」
lines.english: “Yeah. Everybody was terrified.”

lines.japanese:
「……なんでビビッてたんかな。ちっと忘れたけど。
　なんかあったんだろ。で、誰もあいつと話そうと
　しなかった」
lines.english: “…Can't quite remember what everyone was so scared of. Something happened, though. Anyway, nobody would talk to her.”

lines.japanese: 「よくわかんねーぞ。さっきの、集団なに？」
lines.english: “You're losing me. What was that mass whatever you mentioned?”

lines.japanese:
「いや、本堂と関係あんのかどうかわかんねぇんだ
　けど、昔はそう言われてて」
lines.english: “I don't know if it actually had anything to do with Hondou, but that's what people said back then.”

lines.japanese:
「１０人くらいだっけ？　なんか同時にいなくなっ
　ちまってさ」
lines.english: “About ten people, I think? They all disappeared at the same time.”

lines.japanese:
「で、捜索隊とか結成されたり学校休みにナッタリ
　ー」
lines.english: “They organized search parties, school got canceled and all thaaat—”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、あったあったそんなこと！」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah! That did happen!”

lines.japanese: 「見つからなくて。で、どうなったんだっけ？」
lines.english: “They couldn't find them. What happened after that?”

lines.japanese:
「何人か戻ってきたらしいけど……なんか医者とか
　に入れられて。つうか全員、学校に戻る間もなく
　どっかに行っちゃったしな」
lines.english: “I heard a few came back… but they got put under some doctor’s care or something. Before any of them made it back to school, they’d all gone somewhere else.”

lines.japanese: 「どこによ」
lines.english: “Where?”

lines.japanese: 「……国の秘密施設とか？」
lines.english: “…A secret government facility?”

lines.japanese:
「うふぉ（ＵＦＯ）くせえなそれ。インプラントミ
　ーティレーションだろ」
lines.english: “That reeks of UFOs. Implant mutilation, right?”

lines.japanese:
「ばかくさ。で、とりあえずそいつら全員ロストし
　たあと、誰も本堂イジメなくなった」
lines.english: “Yeah, right. Anyway, after that whole bunch got ‘lost,’ nobody picked on Hondou anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「それまで本堂ってイジメられてたんだよな？」
lines.english: “She'd been bullied before then, right?”

lines.japanese:
「影でな。なんかそのあたりは俺クンも詳しくしら
　ねーけど」
lines.english: “Behind her back. Yours truly doesn't know the details, though.”

lines.japanese: 「うっわ、超やべえじゃん本堂」
lines.english: “Damn. Hondou is seriously bad news.”

lines.japanese: 沙也加が戻ってきた。
lines.english: Sayaka returned.

lines.japanese:
生徒らはそちらを横目で確認することもなく、気
配だけで自然に会話を切り替えた。
lines.english: Without so much as glancing her way, the students sensed her presence and effortlessly changed the subject.

lines.japanese:
「ちゅことでな、おまえ昨日俺クンの登録弾いた
　ろ？」
lines.english: “Anyway, you rejected my registration yesterday, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「なんじゃいですのん？」
lines.english: “Whatever could you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「カイロ呼べつうたのおまえだろが」
lines.english: “You're the one who told me to call Cairo.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あの怪しいメール？　スパムかと思って
　キック」
lines.english: “Oh, that shady email? Thought it was spam, so—kick.”

lines.japanese: 「蹴ってんじゃねて。殺意プリ芽生え」
lines.english: “Don't kick me. Murderous impulse budding over here.”

lines.japanese: 「ソリソリ。許せよ。して、もっかコール」
lines.english: “Sorries, sorries. Forgive me. Call me again.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、俺もカイロやりたい」
lines.english: “Hey, I want to try Cairo too.”

lines.japanese: 「いよ、夜な。で、おまえ今度蹴ったら砂」
lines.english: “Sure, tonight. Kick me again and you eat sand.”

lines.japanese: 「砂勘弁」
lines.english: “No sand, please.”

lines.japanese: 彼らの会話は、再び雑音へと還元されていく。
lines.english: Their conversation receded into noise once more.
(…A witch.)

lines.japanese: 根も葉もない、というと嘘になるかも知れない。
lines.english: To say the story was utterly groundless might itself have been a lie.

lines.japanese:
本堂沙也加について語るとき、饒舌・寡黙のいず
れに徹することも忍には困難に感じられる。
lines.english: When it came to Sayaka Hondou, Shinobu found it hard either to talk freely or to keep quiet.

lines.japanese: （そう……確か昔、彼女は―――）
lines.english: (Yes… I remember. Long ago, she was—)

lines.japanese: （魔女だった―――）
lines.english: (A witch—)

lines.japanese:
魔女と呼ばれる者ではあった。
　それは間違いない。
　ただ理由がいまいち思い出せなかった。
lines.english: People had indeed called her a witch. That much was certain. He simply couldn't quite remember why.

lines.japanese: （知り合った時から、魔女って呼ばれていて……）
lines.english: (They had called her a witch ever since I met her…)

lines.japanese: （みんな怯えていた）
lines.english: (Everyone was afraid of her.)

lines.japanese: （曖昧、だな……）
lines.english: (It's all so vague…)

lines.japanese:
軽く頭痛がした。
　良くない兆候だ。
　気分を切り替える。
lines.english: His head gave a faint throb. Not a good sign. He forced his thoughts elsewhere.

lines.japanese: 精神的に沈むと、ストレスから痛むことがあるのだ。
lines.english: When his spirits sank, stress sometimes made his head ache.

lines.japanese: （鬱禁止）
lines.english: (No brooding.)

lines.japanese:
沙也加を見る。
　座り、前方を見据えている。
lines.english: He looked at Sayaka. She sat gazing straight ahead.

lines.japanese:
誰とも話さず、読書に逃げることもせず、何もし
ていないことを臆しもせず。
lines.english: She spoke to no one, sought no refuge in a book, and felt no unease at doing absolutely nothing.

lines.japanese: 鎮座している様が忍個人には、少しだけ微笑ましい。
lines.english: Her regal stillness struck Shinobu as almost endearing.

lines.japanese:
彼女のことを悪く言われるのは、腹が立つことだ
った。
lines.english: It angered him to hear anyone speak ill of her.

lines.japanese:
そのことで忍が声高に何か言うという選択肢はない。
　かえって注目を浴びてしまう。
lines.english: Speaking up loudly in her defense was not an option. It would only draw more attention to her.

lines.japanese: （……そんな縁もない、か）
lines.english: (…Not that we're close enough for that.)

lines.japanese:
同じ教室にいながら、隔たりを感じる。
　立ち上がってすぐ触れることもできる距離だが、
実行してどうなるだろう？
lines.english: They shared a classroom, yet he felt a gulf between them. She was close enough to touch if he stood up— but what would happen if he did?

lines.japanese: もやが晴れることがあるだろうか？
lines.english: Would the haze clear?

lines.japanese: （いや、ない）
lines.english: (No. It wouldn't.)

lines.japanese: 過去をねじ曲げることなどできはしない。
lines.english: The past could not be twisted into another shape.

lines.japanese:
（歴史のＩＦか。もし、時間を遡って、出来事をい
　じくることができたら―――）
lines.english: (A historical what-if. Suppose I could go back in time and alter what happened—)

lines.japanese:
つまらないことを考えもする。
　振り払った。
　授業のため、教科書を取り出す。
lines.english: What a pointless thing to imagine. He shook it off. Then took out his textbook for class.

lines.japanese:
見れば沙也加も同じように、準備をはじめていた。
　時計を見た。
　あと三分。
lines.english: Sayaka, he noticed, had begun getting ready too. He checked the clock. Three minutes to go.

lines.japanese:
次の教師はいつも遅刻してくるから、五分か六分
は猶予がある。
lines.english: The next teacher was invariably late, so in practice they had another five or six minutes.

lines.japanese: 「ふわ」
lines.english: “Yaaawn.”

lines.japanese:
本当にやることがない。
　ひとりでサムライのように座っているのも、ガラ
じゃない。
lines.english: There really was nothing to do. Sitting there alone like some solitary samurai was not his style.

lines.japanese: 机の上に突っ伏して、目を閉じた。
lines.english: He laid his head on the desk and closed his eyes.

lines.japanese:
まどろみの中で夢を見た。
　古い夢だ。
lines.english: In the shallows of sleep, he dreamed. An old dream.

lines.japanese:
浅い眠りのためか、映像がぼけている。
　目を凝らすようにして記憶に触れる。
　触れかけて、大きな信号に叩き起こされた。
lines.english: Perhaps because his sleep was so light, the images were blurred. He reached toward the memory as if squinting to make it out. Just before he touched it, a powerful signal jolted him awake.

lines.japanese: 教室だ。
lines.english: The classroom.

lines.japanese:
それまでは遮断されていた周囲の笑い声が、急に
クリアな音質となって意識に染みてくる。
lines.english: The laughter around him, shut out until then, suddenly came through crystal clear and seeped into his awareness.

lines.japanese:
「お疲れの所申し訳ないがね、貴宮。そろそろ目覚
　めてくれないと、おまえさんテストの時に後悔す
　ることになると思ってな」
lines.english: “Sorry to disturb your rest, Atemiya. But I thought you’d regret it come test time if you didn’t wake up soon.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あう……すいません……」
lines.english: “Ah—uh… Sorry…”

lines.japanese:
笑い声の矛先は、どうやら自分だったようだ。
　顔に血液がほとばしり、赤面が抑制できない。
　穴に入りたい。
lines.english: The laughter, it seemed, was at his expense. Blood rushed to his face. There was no hiding his blush. He wanted to crawl into a hole.

lines.japanese:
「では、この前の続きから。じゃ英気を養って調子
　の良い貴宮、読んでくれ」
lines.english: “Now, picking up where we left off. Atemiya, well-rested and in fine form, would you read for us?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes.”

lines.japanese:
教科書を手に立ち上がる。
　前回の続き。
lines.english: Textbook in hand, he stood. Where they had left off last time.

lines.japanese:
文字列を一瞬で検索し、歴史を綴った文章を読み
上げる。
lines.english: His eyes found the passage instantly, and he began reading the historical account aloud.

lines.japanese:
「―――この年、大陸は統一される。２５９年ごろ、
　王位継承者同士の対立が深刻化し、国家は分裂の
　兆しを―――」
lines.english: “—In this year, the continent was unified. Around the year 259, conflict between the claimants to the throne intensified, and the nation began to show signs of division—”

lines.japanese:
沙也加をちらと盗み見た。
　集団の中、ただ彼女だけが忍を見てもおらず、笑
ってもいなかった。
lines.english: He stole a glance at Sayaka. Of everyone there, she alone was neither looking at him nor laughing.

lines.japanese:
寂しいような、誇らしいような、そんな面妖な
気分に包まれた。
lines.english: A peculiar feeling settled over him—part loneliness and part pride.

lines.japanese:
うさぎの飼い方。
　草食のこの大人しい生き物を飼育する際に、注意
しなくてはならない点はいくつかある。
lines.english: How to care for rabbits. There are several points to remember when raising these gentle herbivores.

lines.japanese:
猫などのように放し飼いはできない。
　単に餌をやる以上の、毎日の世話が必要である。
lines.english: They cannot roam freely like cats. They need daily care beyond simply being fed.

lines.japanese:
ブチとマルは相性の良いメス同士であり、同じ小
屋で飼育されている。
lines.english: Spot and Roly are two females who get along well and share the same hutch.

lines.japanese:
小屋は風通しの良い広場と、隠れるための小部屋
二間が奥に区切られている。
lines.english: The hutch has a well-ventilated open area and two compartments in the back where they can hide.

lines.japanese:
特にケンカをすることもなく、二羽はそれぞれの
スペースを寝床にしている。
lines.english: The two rarely fight and use separate compartments as their beds.

lines.japanese:
小屋に行くと二羽はたいてい寝ている。
　人の気配を察知すると、のそのそと起きてきて邪
魔になるので、そうなる前に素早く掃除を済ませる。
lines.english: When someone visits the hutch, both are usually asleep. Once they sense a human, they lumber out and get underfoot, so the cleaning must be finished quickly before that happens.

lines.japanese:
小屋内を掃き、水気があった場合は拭き取る。
　餌入れを洗い、トイレを整える。
lines.english: Sweep the hutch and wipe away any moisture. Wash the food bowls and tidy the litter box.

lines.japanese:
うさぎは湿気に弱い。
　水滴が残らないよう、洗ったものは乾布で拭き取る。
lines.english: Rabbits are vulnerable to damp. Dry everything with a cloth so that no droplets remain.

lines.japanese:
うさぎも水を飲む。
　飲まないといわれてるのはデマだ。
lines.english: Rabbits drink water too. The claim that they do not is a myth.

lines.japanese:
ボトル式の給水器が用意されている。皿だとひっ
くり返してしまうためだ。
lines.english: They have a bottle-style water dispenser, since they would overturn a dish.

lines.japanese:
吸い口を交換しなければならない。
　また、交換した吸い口はあとで入念に洗う必要が
ある。
lines.english: Its drinking nozzle must be replaced. The removed nozzle must later be washed thoroughly.

lines.japanese:
だいたいこのあたりで、ブチとマルが幽鬼の如く
寝床から這いでてくる。
lines.english: Around this point, Spot and Roly generally crawl from their beds like ghosts.

lines.japanese: 交換されたばかりの、新鮮な餌にありつくためにだ。
lines.english: They come to claim the fresh food that has just been put out.

lines.japanese:
衛生面での問題（食い残しをぶちまけ環境を悪化
させる）のため、野菜が食べられるのは人間がいる
時のみであることを、彼女らは知っている。
lines.english: They know vegetables are available only while a human is present, for sanitary reasons: leftovers scattered about would foul their environment.

lines.japanese:
乾燥したペレットとは別の器に用意された、小松菜
とパセリと少量の人参を食す。
　ペレットよりは野菜が好みのようだ。
lines.english: From a bowl separate from the dry pellets, they eat Japanese mustard spinach, parsley, and a little carrot. They appear to prefer vegetables to pellets.

lines.japanese:
たいていは残さず平らげる。
　残した時は体調が悪くないか、注意深くチェック
しなければならない。
lines.english: Usually they finish every bite. If they leave any, check them carefully for signs of illness.

lines.japanese:
この日は、完食。
　食べたあとには毛繕いをしていたが、やがて人間
の存在が気になってくる。
lines.english: Today they ate every last bite. Afterward they groomed themselves, but soon the human’s presence began to draw their attention.

lines.japanese:
周囲をぐるぐる回る。二羽で。
　こうなるともう、掃除はしにくくなる。
lines.english: Round and round they circled him. Both of them. At that point, cleaning became difficult.

lines.japanese:
世話をしはじめてだいぶ経つが、いまだに慣れて
いるのかわからない。
　以前のように警戒されることはなくなった。
lines.english: He had been caring for them for some time, yet still could not tell whether they had grown used to him. They were no longer as wary of him as before.

lines.japanese:
緊張もしていないようだ。
　しかし……周囲を巡りながら、ごつごつと足首に
頭突きを繰り返すのは何の感情表現なのだろう。
lines.english: They did not appear tense either. But what feeling were they expressing as they circled him, bumping their heads against his ankles again and again?

lines.japanese: 二羽揃ってとなると、ますますわからない。
lines.english: With both of them at it, he understood even less.

lines.japanese:
ごつごつごつごつ。
　痛くはないが、いつまでも終わらない。
lines.english: Bump, bump, bump, bump. It didn't hurt, but it went on and on.

lines.japanese:
懐いている、と思えなくもないが、攻撃されてい
るのかも知れない。
lines.english: It might mean they had grown fond of him, or it might mean they were attacking him.

lines.japanese: 難しい、と忍は思った。
lines.english: Hard to tell, Shinobu thought.

lines.japanese:
ごつごつごつごつ。
　頭突きは際限なく続く。
lines.english: Bump, bump, bump, bump. The headbutts went on without end.

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮君」
lines.english: “…Atemiya.”

lines.japanese: フェンスの外に、所在なく沙也加が立っている。
lines.english: Sayaka stood awkwardly outside the fence.

lines.japanese: 「やあ」
lines.english: “Hello.”

lines.japanese: 「鍵はあいてる」
lines.english: “It's unlocked.”

lines.japanese: 扉を指さすと、無言でゲージに入ってくる。
lines.english: When he pointed to the door, she entered the enclosure without a word.

lines.japanese: 「……残っている仕事は？」
lines.english: “…What work is left?”

lines.japanese: 「体調管理」
lines.english: “Checking their health.”

lines.japanese:
沙也加は小屋に立てかけてあった記録ノートを取
りあげる。
lines.english: Sayaka picked up the logbook propped against the hutch.

lines.japanese:
真横を通り過ぎたかすかな呼吸の乱れが、彼女ら
しからぬ感情的なものに思え、忍は少し当惑を示した。
lines.english: As she passed close beside him, the faint catch in her breath struck Shinobu as uncharacteristically emotional, leaving him a little confused.

lines.japanese: 少し考えれば、理由は明白だ。
lines.english: A moment's thought made the reason obvious.

lines.japanese:
長らく空位だった二人目の飼育委員に任ぜられた
貴宮忍が、本堂沙也加の仕事を奪うようになり、一
週間が過ぎ去った。
lines.english: A week had passed since Shinobu Atemiya was appointed to the long-vacant post of second animal caretaker and began taking Sayaka Hondou's work from her.

lines.japanese: きっとそれは、侵略にも等しい。
lines.english: To her, that must have felt like an invasion.

lines.japanese:
忍が世話の手順を覚え、合理的になっていくに従
い、沙也加の果たすべき義務は減少していった。
lines.english: As Shinobu learned the routine and grew more efficient, Sayaka's share of the duties diminished.

lines.japanese:
だというのに沙也加は不平不満の一つも、漏らし
たことはない。
lines.english: And yet Sayaka had never uttered a single complaint.

lines.japanese: 彼女がうさぎを大切にしていることはわかる。
lines.english: He knew she treasured the rabbits.

lines.japanese:
世話にかける手間と時間は、惜しくはないものだ
ろう。
lines.english: Surely she did not begrudge the time and effort their care required.

lines.japanese: 忍が剥奪したようなものだ。
lines.english: It was as though Shinobu had taken that from her.

lines.japanese: 「……怒ってる？」
lines.english: “…Are you angry?”

lines.japanese: 「どうして？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
しゃがみこみ、ノートに書き込む姿勢を崩すこと
なく、沙也加は応じる。
lines.english: Still crouched over the logbook, Sayaka answered without changing her posture.

lines.japanese: いつもの声色。
lines.english: Her usual tone.

lines.japanese: 「仕事を取ったから」
lines.english: “Because I took your work.”

lines.japanese: 「怒ることじゃないから」
lines.english: “That isn't something to be angry about.”

lines.japanese:
ぴしゃりと言われる。
　だが性急な物言いが、少しばかりの遺憾を表明し
ている。
lines.english: The words came down like a slap. Yet the haste of her reply betrayed a little displeasure.

lines.japanese: 「……先生がやれと言ったから、断れない」
lines.english: “…The teacher told me to do it. I can't refuse.”

lines.japanese: 「断りたいの？」
lines.english: “Did you want to refuse?”

lines.japanese: 「いや」
lines.english: “No.”
