lines.japanese: 「問題があるようには思えないけど」
lines.english: “Then I don't see a problem.”

lines.japanese: 「不満じゃないのかな」
lines.english: “I wondered if you were unhappy about it.”

lines.japanese: 「ここはキミの場所だったんだろう？」
lines.english: “This used to be your place, didn't it?”

lines.japanese: 応じない。
lines.english: She did not answer.

lines.japanese: 「来るなと言うなら、来ないけど」
lines.english: “If you tell me not to come, I won't.”

lines.japanese: 「来たくないと言うのなら、来なくてもいい」
lines.english: “If you don't want to come, you needn't.”

lines.japanese: 本音の所在を秘めた会話は、隔靴掻痒の感がある。
lines.english: With neither revealing what they truly felt, the conversation was like scratching an itch through a boot.

lines.japanese:
手探りしながら相手の本音を探る、そんな技術さ
え忍にはまだ備わっていない。
lines.english: Shinobu didn't yet have even the knack of feeling his way toward what another person truly felt.

lines.japanese: 押し黙る。
lines.english: He fell silent.

lines.japanese: しばしの時間、互いに背を向けての作業が続く。
lines.english: For a while, they continued working with their backs to each other.

lines.japanese:
寝床のわらを引っ張り出し、湿っていない新しい
ものと取り替える。
　不安がるので、こすりあわせて少し臭いをつけた。
lines.english: He pulled the straw from the beds and replaced it with fresh, dry straw. To keep the rabbits from growing anxious, he rubbed the old and new together, leaving a little of their scent on it.

lines.japanese: 「私に関わらなければ良かったわね」
lines.english: “You'd have been better off never getting involved with me.”

lines.japanese:
いきなりに沙也加は言った。
　忍もまた、それをいきなりとは感じなかった。
　会話のあやというものを、知らなかったためだ。
lines.english: Sayaka spoke without warning. It did not strike Shinobu as abrupt. He knew nothing about the flow of conversation.

lines.japanese: 「どうしてそんなことを言うの？」
lines.english: “Why would you say that?”

lines.japanese:
「この子たちだけじゃなくて、私の監視も兼ねてい
　るってわからない？」
lines.english: “Don't you understand that you were assigned not merely to watch these rabbits, but to watch me?”

lines.japanese: 「私のこと、聞いてるでしょ」
lines.english: “You've heard about me, haven't you?”

lines.japanese: 「……一応は」
lines.english: “…More or less.”

lines.japanese:
「誰も引き受けたがらない。でもあなたは、見られ
　てしまったから」
lines.english: “No one wants the job. But you were seen.”

lines.japanese: 「私と話しているところを」
lines.english: “Speaking to me.”

lines.japanese:
「クラスの誰もが知っているわ。だからあなたは、
　もう彼らの仲間にはなれない」
lines.english: “Everyone in the class knows. So now you can no longer be one of them.”

lines.japanese:
告げる口調は淡々としていて真実味に欠けるが、
事実なのだろう。
lines.english: Her dispassionate tone made it all sound unreal, but it was probably true.

lines.japanese: 「それで、猛獣使いという立場のままなのだから」
lines.english: “Which leaves you playing beast tamer.”

lines.japanese: 「……猛獣使い？」
lines.english: “…Beast tamer?”

lines.japanese: 「そうでしょう？」
lines.english: “Isn't that so?”

lines.japanese: 「猛獣って？」
lines.english: “Who's the beast?”

lines.japanese:
冷笑。
　珍しく皮肉げな沙也加だった。
lines.english: A cold smile. Sayaka was being sarcastic, unusually for her.

lines.japanese: 「私のことよ」
lines.english: “Me.”

lines.japanese: 「よくわからない」
lines.english: “I don't understand.”

lines.japanese: 「女の子じゃないか。猛獣とは違う」
lines.english: “You're a girl. That isn't the same as a beast.”

lines.japanese:
馬鹿正直な反応が気に入らなかったのか、沙也加
は瞬時に無表情に戻る。
lines.english: Perhaps his painfully literal answer displeased her; Sayaka's face instantly went blank again.

lines.japanese: 「たとえ」
lines.english: “It was a figure of speech.”

lines.japanese: 「でも」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese: 「もういいわ」
lines.english: “Never mind.”

lines.japanese: 忍はただばつの悪さだけを感じる。
lines.english: Shinobu was left feeling awkward.

lines.japanese: 「……仕事ちゃんと分担した方がいいのかな」
lines.english: “…Maybe we should divide the work properly.”

lines.japanese: 「きみの仕事を、僕が取らないですむように」
lines.english: “So I don’t take yours away from you.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことする必要ないわ」
lines.english: “There is no need.”

lines.japanese:
「あなたの仕事にもなったんだから、取る取らない
　の話じゃないでしょう」
lines.english: “It's your work too now, so this isn't about whether you take it from me.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだけど」
lines.english: “I know, but…”

lines.japanese: 「気になる」
lines.english: “It bothers me.”

lines.japanese:
「難儀ね。話してどうにかなることでもないと思う
　けど」
lines.english: “That's difficult. I don't think talking will solve it, though.”

lines.japanese: その通りだった。
lines.english: She was right.

lines.japanese:
一連の流れがどういう意味を持ち、いかなる糸口
を差し出したのか、忍にはうかがい知ることさえ難
しい。
lines.english: Shinobu could barely guess what the exchange had meant, or what kind of opening it had given him.

lines.japanese: 「……ふたりの体調はどう？」
lines.english: “…How are the two girls doing?”

lines.japanese: 「問題ないわ」
lines.english: “There are no problems.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Say…”

lines.japanese: 「なに」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「言われた通りにやってるけど、うまくできてるの
　かな？」
lines.english: “I'm doing what you told me, but am I doing it right?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「問題は？」
lines.english: “Any problems?”

lines.japanese: 「ないわ」
lines.english: “None.”

lines.japanese: 「ならいい」
lines.english: “Then it's fine.”

lines.japanese:
それぞれの作業に戻る。
　掃除の物音と、強めの筆致が奏でる音が、奇妙な
調和をもって小屋の静寂を押さえつけた。
lines.english: They returned to their respective tasks. The sounds of cleaning and the forceful scratch of a pen held down the hutch's silence in strange harmony.

lines.japanese: 「今日は、よく話すんだね」
lines.english: “You're talking a lot today.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？」
lines.english: “Am I?”

lines.japanese: 「会話、好きだ」
lines.english: “I like talking.”
“…What?”

lines.japanese:
食べ散らかされた野菜のかすを拾い、ビニール袋
に捨てていく。
lines.english: He gathered the scattered scraps of vegetables and dropped them into a plastic bag.

lines.japanese: 「相手とは話さないとだめなんだ」
lines.english: “You have to talk to another person.”

lines.japanese:
「……話してどうしたいの？
　相手のこと、わかりたいの？」
lines.english: “…And what do you want to accomplish by talking? Do you want to understand them?”

lines.japanese: 「話せば、わかるというものでもないけど。ただ」
lines.english: “Talking doesn't mean you'll understand them. But…”

lines.japanese:
忍はフェンスから、格子縞に区切られた空を見上
げた。
lines.english: Through the fence, Shinobu looked up at a sky divided into a grid.

lines.japanese: 「そこに誰かいるって、わかるから」
lines.english: “It lets you know someone is there.”

lines.japanese:
沙也加はノートを閉じた。
　床に膝をついて、小さく身を折り曲げたその背中
が、小さく震えていた。
lines.english: Sayaka closed the logbook. She knelt on the floor, bending low, her back trembling faintly.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、あなた、なんなの？」
lines.english: “Hey—what are you?”
“Mm?”

lines.japanese: 「私と話して、どうなるの？」
lines.english: “What will come of talking to me?”

lines.japanese: 視線を戻す。
lines.english: He looked back.

lines.japanese:
沙也加とその左右に立つ二羽のうさぎ、計三対の
視線が忍に向けられていた。
lines.english: Three pairs of eyes—Sayaka's and those of the rabbits standing to either side—were fixed on Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
水によって隔てられているわけでもないが、対岸
を連想させた。
lines.english: Though no water lay between them, he thought of the opposite shore.

lines.japanese: 視線もまた会話の一つだと理解した。
lines.english: He understood that a gaze, too, was a form of conversation.

lines.japanese: 「ずっとひとりだったから」
lines.english: “I've always been alone.”

lines.japanese: 「だから考えてた」
lines.english: “So I've been thinking.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとりじゃないことについて、考えてた」
lines.english: “Thinking about not being alone.”

lines.japanese:
「群れのかたちはいろいろあるんだけど……
　いちばん身近なのは、友達だった」
lines.english: “Groups take many forms… The closest kind was friendship.”

lines.japanese: 「家族もないし、国も遠いし」
lines.english: “I don't have a family, and a nation is too distant.”

lines.japanese: 「……あなた、孤児？」
lines.english: “…Are you an orphan?”

lines.japanese: 「たぶん」
lines.english: “Probably.”

lines.japanese: 「壊れてる」
lines.english: “You're broken.”

lines.japanese: 「きっとね」
lines.english: “I'm sure I am.”

lines.japanese:
頷く。
　うさぎが短く鳴いて、地を蹴った。
lines.english: He nodded. A rabbit gave a short cry and kicked the ground.

lines.japanese: 「だから友達には興味があるんだ」
lines.english: “That's why I'm interested in friends.”

lines.japanese: 「友達って……」
lines.english: “Friends…”

lines.japanese:
沙也加は戸惑う。
　光線めいた眼光が弱まり、真面から外れる。
lines.english: Sayaka faltered. Her beamlike gaze weakened and slid away from him.

lines.japanese:
「もしつきあいに理由があったら……
　それは友達と言えるのかな？」
lines.english: “If two people have a reason to spend time together… can they still be called friends?”

lines.japanese: 「わからない」
lines.english: “I don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「相手のことをわかるのが友達？」
lines.english: “Are friends people who understand each other?”

lines.japanese: 「わからないわ」
lines.english: “I don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで友達を作るの？」
lines.english: “Why do people make friends?”

lines.japanese: 「私は作らない」
lines.english: “I don't.”

lines.japanese: 「そう決めてるの？」
lines.english: “Have you decided not to?”

lines.japanese: 「わからない」
lines.english: “I don't know.”

lines.japanese:
「理由が必要なら大変なんだ。それをさがさないと
　いけない」
lines.english: “If you need a reason for friendship, that's hard. I'd have to go and find one.”

lines.japanese: 「けど、どうもそんな答えはないみたい」
lines.english: “But it seems there isn't any such answer.”

lines.japanese: 「なら話は簡単だ」
lines.english: “Then it's simple.”

lines.japanese:
「別にクラスのみんなが、僕を仲間にしないのなら
　それでいいよ」
lines.english: “If nobody in the class wants me as one of them, that's all right.”

lines.japanese: 「好きになる相手は自分で決めたい」
lines.english: “I want to decide for myself who I like.”

lines.japanese: いつしか両者は再び、背中同士で会話していた。
lines.english: Before they knew it, they were speaking back-to-back once more.

lines.japanese: だが各々の手は、もう仕事には携わっていなかった。
lines.english: But neither of them was working any longer.

lines.japanese:
顔を背けることが目的であるかのようだった。
　しかしふたりは、繋がりについて会話している。
lines.english: It was as though they had turned away for the sake of not looking at each other. Yet they were talking about connection.

lines.japanese: 忍は顔に手を当てた。
lines.english: Shinobu put a hand to his face.

lines.japanese:
そして、
　微笑する。
lines.english: And then— he smiled.

lines.japanese:
沙也加に向きなおった。
　向こうもまた後ろ目を忍に向けて、
lines.english: He turned back to Sayaka. She too looked over her shoulder at Shinobu, and—

lines.japanese: 「貴宮君、は……」
lines.english: “Atemiya, you…”

lines.japanese:
「好きになるのに理由はいらないって、マンガで読
　んだんだ。このフレーズ、気に入ってるんだけど」
lines.english: “I read in a manga that you don't need a reason to like someone. I like that line.”

lines.japanese: 沙也加は少しきょとんとする。
lines.english: Sayaka blinked at him for a moment.

lines.japanese: 「でも嫌われているのには理由があるんだろうな」
lines.english: “But I suppose there must be a reason they dislike me.”

lines.japanese: 床を指さす。
lines.english: He pointed at the floor.

lines.japanese: 「僕がうさぎに嫌われているのはどうして？」
lines.english: “Why do the rabbits dislike me?”

lines.japanese: 「嫌われてるの？」
lines.english: “They dislike you?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「……毎日、足に頭突きをされるんだけど……」
lines.english: “…They headbutt my feet every day…”
“…Pff.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「……嫌ってはいないわ」
lines.english: “…They don't dislike you.”

lines.japanese:
一瞬、吹き出したのかと思ったが、返ってきたの
は取り澄ました声だ。
lines.english: For an instant he thought she had burst out laughing, but the voice that answered was perfectly composed.

lines.japanese: また向こうを向いてしまって、顔だってわからない。
lines.english: She had turned away again, so he could not see her face.

lines.japanese:
沙也加が吹き出す顔など想像もできない。
　だからきっと勘違いだろうと忍が考えたのも、無
理からぬことだ。
lines.english: Shinobu could not imagine Sayaka ever bursting out laughing. So it was only natural that he decided he must have been mistaken.

lines.japanese: 「それは、嫌っているわけじゃない」
lines.english: “That does not mean they dislike you.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなのか」
lines.english: “It doesn't?”

lines.japanese: 「触れてるのよ」
lines.english: “They're touching you.”

lines.japanese: 「触れている？」
lines.english: “Touching me?”

lines.japanese: 「触れたいのね、きっと」
lines.english: “They must want to touch you.”

lines.japanese: 「よくわからないな」
lines.english: “I don't really understand.”

lines.japanese: 「あなた、不思議だから」
lines.english: “Because you're strange.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ」
lines.english: “Then…”

lines.japanese: 「僕がキミに触れたいと言ったら？」
lines.english: “What if I said I wanted to touch you?”

lines.japanese:
時間が止まった。
　呼吸も止まっていた。
　沙也加は動かなかった。
lines.english: Time stopped. Breathing stopped too. Sayaka did not move.

lines.japanese: 計測することなどできない心理的な時が過ぎていく。
lines.english: Psychological time beyond all measurement passed between them.

lines.japanese: 「鍵渡しておくね。さようなら、また明日」
lines.english: “I'll leave the key with you. Goodbye. See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese:
忍は小屋を出て行った。
　二羽のうさぎがぴょんと飛び跳ねた。
　沙也加は気付いた。
lines.english: Shinobu left the hutch. The two rabbits gave little hops. Sayaka realized something.

lines.japanese: 忍は二羽のうさぎを“ふたり”と言った。
lines.english: Shinobu had called the two rabbits ‘the girls.’

lines.japanese:
放課のあと、忍は特に用事もなく教室にとどまった。
　物思いにふけりたかった。
lines.english: After school, Shinobu remained in the classroom with nothing in particular to do. He wanted to lose himself in thought.

lines.japanese:
自分の部屋はあまりにも質素で、考え事には向く
が感傷に浸るには向かない。
lines.english: His own room was too austere: good for thinking, no good for indulging in sentiment.

lines.japanese:
窓から街並みを見ていると、違う自分に取り憑か
れたように、思いも掛けない思考が飛来しては去っ
ていく。
lines.english: When he looked out over the town, thoughts came swooping in unbidden and vanished again, as though another self had possessed him.

lines.japanese:
あるいはそれは、市街崩壊の光景であったり、コ
ールタールのようなものが空から降り注ぐ悪夢めい
たものであり、時に光り輝く何かだった。
lines.english: Sometimes they took the form of a city collapsing; at others, a nightmare of something like coal tar raining from the sky; and sometimes, something radiant.

lines.japanese:
無論、夢想ばかりではなく、現実の出来事も視覚
情報には含まれる。
lines.english: But his eyes took in events in the real world as well as reveries.

lines.japanese: 校門から三々五々、出て行く生徒ら。
lines.english: Students trickled out through the school gates in twos and threes.

lines.japanese:
校内への用事で入ってくる車。
　威勢良く出て行く運動部のランニング部隊。
lines.english: Cars arriving on school business. Sports teams heading out for an energetic run.

lines.japanese:
窓際に寄り、気怠げな様子で茶飯の風景を摂取し
ていると、感受性が刺激された。
lines.english: As he lingered listlessly by the window, taking in the everyday scene, something in him stirred.

lines.japanese:
哀しいのか、満たされているのか、憂鬱なのかわ
からない。
lines.english: He could not tell whether it was sadness, contentment, or melancholy.

lines.japanese: ただ根底に流れるのは得体の知れない不安だった。
lines.english: Yet beneath it all ran an anxiety he could not name.

lines.japanese:
弥増さる感情が、幾度忍の目蓋を用途以外で降ろ
したことか。
lines.english: How many times had that swelling emotion made Shinobu lower his eyelids for something other than their intended purpose?

lines.japanese: （……寂しいって、ことなのかな）
lines.english: (…Maybe I'm lonely.)

lines.japanese:
ぼんやりと考えていると、眼下を通過する制服集
団に、沙也加の姿を発見した。
lines.english: As his thoughts drifted, he spotted Sayaka among a stream of uniforms passing below.

lines.japanese:
背を弓のように張って、颯爽と歩く。
　帰宅するようだ。
　沙也加は部活動の類には参加していない。
lines.english: Back taut as a bow, she strode briskly. She appeared to be going home. Sayaka belonged to no club.

lines.japanese: 「さもありなん」
lines.english: “As one might expect.”

lines.japanese:
彼女は何者にも縛られない。
　ただ己だけに縛られるものである。
　人は群れる。
lines.english: Nothing bound her— nothing but herself. Human beings formed herds.

lines.japanese: 群れねば人にならず、また立つことができない。
lines.english: Without the herd, they could neither become human nor remain standing.

lines.japanese:
だが沙也加はどうだろう？
　もちろん本堂沙也加も人である以上、摂理を免れ
るものではないはずだ。
lines.english: But what of Sayaka? Sayaka Hondou was human too, and surely no more exempt from that law than anyone else.

lines.japanese:
だがもしかして、とも思わされる。
　個の新しい可能性を、見せてくれるのではないか
と思うのだ。
lines.english: And yet she made him wonder. Perhaps she might reveal some new possibility for the solitary individual.
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese:
ふと見れば、沙也加が正門のあたりで何者かに呼
び止められた。
lines.english: Then he noticed someone stop Sayaka near the front gate.

lines.japanese:
私服の男たちだ。
　遊び慣れた風。
　三人ほどで連れ立っている。
lines.english: Men in street clothes. They had the look of men who knew their way around a good time. There were about three of them.

lines.japanese:
よくできた数だ。
　二人で前を、一人が後ろを。逃げられないように
挟む。
lines.english: A well-chosen number. Two in front and one behind, boxing her in so that she could not escape.

lines.japanese:
交互に話しかけている。
　馴れ馴れしげに。
lines.english: They spoke to her by turns. With an air of easy familiarity.

lines.japanese:
窓枠を強く掴む。
　危険、ではないはずだ。
　人目も多い。
lines.english: He gripped the window frame. She should not be in danger. There were plenty of people around.

lines.japanese:
事実、通り過ぎる生徒たちの多くが、境界線上に
立つ三人の闖入者に視線という攻撃を仕掛けている。
lines.english: Indeed, many passing students attacked the three intruders at the boundary with nothing but their eyes.

lines.japanese: だが楽観もできない。
lines.english: But he could not be optimistic either.

lines.japanese: 強引に連れて行かれることもあるだろうから。
lines.english: They might take her by force.

lines.japanese: （どうする？　どうするんだ？）
lines.english: (What do I do? What am I going to do?)

lines.japanese:
咄嗟に飛び降りたくなった。
　足を折るのが関の山だ。
lines.english: For an instant, he wanted to leap from the window. At best, he would break a leg.

lines.japanese:
沙也加が応じていない様子が、まったく動かない
唇から逆に読みとれた。
lines.english: The perfect stillness of Sayaka's lips made it clear that she had not answered.

lines.japanese: だが、
lines.english: But—

lines.japanese:
３対１である。
　漠然とした不安が膨れあがっていく。
　本音を言えば、今すぐ介入してしまいたかった。
lines.english: Three against one. His shapeless anxiety swelled. Truthfully, he wanted to intervene then and there.

lines.japanese: そういう感情が、無機的に抽出されたのは確かだ。
lines.english: That feeling, at least, had emerged with mechanical clarity.

lines.japanese: （でも……そんなことをしても―――）
lines.english: (But… even if I did—)

lines.japanese:
男たちはしつこく食い下がっているようだ。
　沙也加は黙殺を続けている。
lines.english: The men seemed determined to keep at her. Sayaka went on ignoring them.

lines.japanese:
包囲網を抜け出ようとするが、男がそれを笑いな
がら阻む。
lines.english: She tried to break out of the cordon, but one of them laughingly barred her way.

lines.japanese:
笑顔ではあるが、三人ともかなり強硬な態度に思
えた。
lines.english: All three were smiling, but their behavior struck him as remarkably forceful.

lines.japanese: 沙也加に友人がいないことが仇となる。
lines.english: Sayaka's lack of friends had turned against her.

lines.japanese:
皆知っているのだろう。彼女についての噂を。
　誰も助けようとしない。
　教師も来ない。
lines.english: Everyone must have known the rumors about her. No one tried to help. No teacher came.

lines.japanese:
校舎から逃げるように飛び出し、正門のあたりに
駆けた。
lines.english: He burst from the school building as though escaping it and sprinted toward the front gate.

lines.japanese: 「はっ、はっ、はっ……」
lines.english: “Hah, hah, hah…”

lines.japanese:
体を回転させて、周囲を見渡す。
　人影がない。
lines.english: He whirled around and searched. No one was there.

lines.japanese:
周辺に目線を飛ばす。
　運動量に比しても異様とおもえるほど、激しく鼓
動していた。
lines.english: His gaze shot across the area. His heart pounded far harder than the exertion could explain.

lines.japanese: （……連れて、いかれた？）
lines.english: (…Did they take her?)

lines.japanese: 荒野のような世界に、忍は一人取り残された。
lines.english: Shinobu had been left alone in a world like a wasteland.
“Hah… hah…”

lines.japanese:
膝をつく。
　誰も通らない。
　話し声ひとつ拾うことができない。
lines.english: He dropped to his knees. No one passed by. He could not pick out a single voice.

lines.japanese: （この世界は、異常だ―――）
lines.english: (This world is wrong—)

lines.japanese: 美しいものが、ほんの気まぐれで破壊されてしまう。
lines.english: Beautiful things could be destroyed on the merest whim.

lines.japanese:
全ての快いものは有限だった。
　それが、忍には許せない。認めがたい事実だった。
lines.english: Every pleasant thing was finite. Shinobu could neither forgive nor accept that fact.

lines.japanese:
いつか終わることが確約され、ただ今と過去にし
か存在しない幸福の全てを、忍はどうしようもなく
好いている。
lines.english: Every happiness was fated to end, existing only in the present and the past. Shinobu was helplessly in love with all of it.

lines.japanese:
愛おしんでいるだけに、喪失による悲嘆も大きい。
　血が流れそうなほどに心を傷つける。
lines.english: The more he cherished them, the greater the grief of losing them. It hurt his heart as though it might bleed.

lines.japanese: （断って、帰ったのかも知れない）
lines.english: (Maybe she turned them down and went home.)

lines.japanese: （教師が出てきて、追い払ったのかも知れない）
lines.english: (Maybe a teacher came out and chased them away.)

lines.japanese:
（わからないじゃないか。
　連れ去られたとは限らない）
lines.english: (You don't know what happened. It doesn't mean they took her.)

lines.japanese: （確定もされていないことで悩んで……僕はバカだ）
lines.english: (I'm agonizing over something that isn't even certain… I'm an idiot.)

lines.japanese: （こんなことで、苦しんで何になる……）
lines.english: (What do I gain by suffering over this…?)

lines.japanese: （だけどもし、明日彼女が来なかったら―――）
lines.english: (But if she doesn't come tomorrow—)

lines.japanese:
（捜しだして、あいつらのスイッチを止めてしまう
　かも知れない）
lines.english: (I might track them down and shut off their switches.)

lines.japanese: （だって）
lines.english: (Because…)

lines.japanese: （キレイなんだ）
lines.english: (She's beautiful.)

lines.japanese: （好きなんだ）
lines.english: (I like her.)

lines.japanese: 生まれてはじめて持った、憧れだったから―――
lines.english: Because she was the first person he had ever admired—

lines.japanese: 工場には沙也加がいた。
lines.english: Sayaka was at the factory.
(…Huh?)

lines.japanese: 会釈してくる。
lines.english: She nodded to him.

lines.japanese: 「……帰ったんじゃなかったんだ？」
lines.english: “…Didn't you go home?”

lines.japanese:
「いるべき場所に向かうことをそう言うなら、もう
　帰ったことになるわね」
lines.english: “If going where one belongs is what you mean by going home, then I already have.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「歩きまわって、疲れなかった？」
lines.english: “Didn't all that walking tire you out?”

lines.japanese:
意味深な言葉を咀嚼しようとするが、うまくいか
ない。
lines.english: He tried to digest her loaded words, but could make nothing of them.

lines.japanese: 彼女の言うとおり、忍は疲れていた。
lines.english: She was right about one thing: Shinobu was tired.

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「座って。何か作るわ」
lines.english: “Sit down. I'll make you something.”

lines.japanese:
幸せな気分で椅子に腰をおさめる。
　奥の―――炊事スペースがわりの空間から、陶器
の触れる小気味よい物音が届く。
lines.english: He settled happily into a chair. From the space at the back that served as a kitchen came the pleasing clink of dishes.

lines.japanese: 心地よい時間には決まって眠気が訪れる。
lines.english: Pleasant moments invariably made him sleepy.

lines.japanese:
今日もまた例外ではなく、忍は自然と半眼に細る
瞳を、そのまま閉じてしまうか抗うかの狭間で持て
あました。
lines.english: Today was no exception. Shinobu's eyes naturally drooped half shut, leaving him caught between letting them close and struggling to keep them open.

lines.japanese:
用事を思い出す。
　微睡むわけにはいかなくなり、忍は立ち上がった。
　工場には拾いものの本棚が置かれている。
lines.english: He remembered an errand. No longer free to doze, he stood. The factory contained a bookshelf they had salvaged.

lines.japanese:
粗大ゴミの登録処分が登録制度化された今、家の
前からの直の持ち帰りは咎められる。
lines.english: Now that municipal registration was required to dispose of oversized trash, carrying it away directly from someone's curb could get one in trouble.

lines.japanese:
だが忘れられた工業地域に、無断で投棄される粗
大ゴミは少なくない。
lines.english: But plenty of oversized trash was dumped illegally in this forgotten industrial district.

lines.japanese:
そういうものの中で、利用価値のあるものを選び、
必要に応じて修理し、再利用する。
　工場にある家具の多くがそれだ。
lines.english: They selected whatever remained useful, repaired it when necessary, and gave it another life. Most of the factory's furniture had come to them that way.

lines.japanese:
住むには適さない場所ではある。
　だがある者たちにとっては、人々のひしめく街中
が、他者の存在に満ちた圧迫感ある世界となる。
lines.english: It was no place to live. But to some, the crowded city was an oppressive world, packed tight with the presence of others.

lines.japanese:
年老いた者が都会に疲れを感じるように、だ。
　忍らは、閑静な廃棄区画に安息を求めた。
lines.english: It was the way old people grew weary of the city. Shinobu and his friends sought peace in this quiet, abandoned quarter.

lines.japanese:
腰を据えて過ごせる場所が、他のどこにあるのだ
ろう。
lines.english: Where else could they truly settle in and stay?

lines.japanese:
自宅からも、街からも、学校からも、安息の場所
は消え失せた。
lines.english: Every place of refuge had vanished—from home, the town, and school alike.

lines.japanese: 濁流に呑まれるようにして。
lines.english: As though swallowed by a muddy torrent.

lines.japanese: （さてと）
lines.english: (All right.)

lines.japanese:
鞄から書物を取り出し、本棚に並べていく。
　忍は自室に棚を置かない。
　読み終わった本は全て、工場に持ってきてしまう。
lines.english: He took books from his bag and lined them on the shelf. Shinobu kept no shelves in his room. Every book he finished came here.

lines.japanese:
いや、この習慣のおかげで、読書が促進されたよ
うなものだ。
lines.english: Or rather, that habit itself had encouraged him to read.

lines.japanese:
以前は必要なものしか紐解かなかった。
　小説などの作り話を面白いと思えるのは、対話を
前提としているからだ。
lines.english: Before, he had opened only the books he needed. Fiction—novels and the like—could interest him only because it presupposed dialogue.

lines.japanese:
興味のない人間社会の、興味のないやりとりに感
情移入はできなかったのだ。
lines.english: He had been unable to invest himself in the uninteresting exchanges of a human society that did not interest him.

lines.japanese:
そんな悪癖も、緩和されて久しい。
　仲間がいるから―――
lines.english: That bad habit had softened long ago. Because he had friends—

lines.japanese:
古典が含む原石のようなドラマ技術は趣があるし、
最近の流行である全登場人物のタイムテーブルを設
定し破綻なくまとめることにだけ腐心した末端重視の
lines.english: The raw dramatic craft embedded in the classics had its charm. Recent mysteries, meanwhile, set timetables for every character and labored above all to make every last detail fit without contradiction. They were like bracing mathematical

lines.japanese: 推理小説は、刺激的な数学問題のようだ。
lines.english: problems.

lines.japanese:
登場人物たちの葛藤も興味深い。
　彼らは様々な倫理に振り回され、悩み、反抗し、
恭順する。
lines.english: The characters' struggles interested him too. Different systems of ethics tossed them about; they suffered, rebelled, and submitted.

lines.japanese:
絶対的な正義が曖昧になった現代である。
　相反する概念に立たされる登場人物の葛藤とその
結果は、いずれかを選択するものであることが多い。
lines.english: This was a modern age in which absolute justice had grown indistinct. When characters stood between opposing ideas, both their struggles and their conclusions often came down to a choice between the two.

lines.japanese:
それは明確な是非ではなく、左か右の選別とも似
ている。
lines.english: It was less a clear division of right and wrong than a choice between left and right.

lines.japanese:
どちらも正しくまた誤りとされ、結果、全ての物
語は“人を選ぶ”ものとなった。
lines.english: Both could be called right and wrong at once, until every story became something that ‘chose its reader.’

lines.japanese:
人が生み出してきた無数の価値観は、時代ととも
に変化し、硬質化を迎えている。
lines.english: The countless values humanity had created changed with each age, only to ossify.

lines.japanese:
たとえば勧善懲悪は否定されるが、その理由は単
純だ。
lines.english: Take the rejection of simple tales where good defeated evil. The reason was straightforward.

lines.japanese:
誰にでも人権がある。
　正当な手続きのない断罪が非―――感心できない、
とされるのは当然なのだ。
lines.english: Everyone had human rights. Naturally, condemning someone without due process was considered wrong— or, at the very least, distasteful.

lines.japanese:
子供にサンタクロースが存在するという教育は、
人格を歪め侵害するものとして非難されるようにな
った。
lines.english: Teaching children that Santa Claus existed had come to be condemned as something that warped and violated their developing personalities.

lines.japanese:
未成年の人格を拡大する反面、虐待が増加してい
ることも事実だ。
lines.english: Yet even as greater regard was paid to the personhood of minors, abuse had also increased.

lines.japanese:
峻別には、理性的な社会基盤が必要となる。
　忍には、今の社会がそれを備えているのかどうか、
判断できない。
lines.english: Making such distinctions required the foundation of a rational society. Shinobu could not judge whether the present society possessed one.

lines.japanese: 例えば自己責任の概念。
lines.english: Take, for instance, the concept of personal responsibility.

lines.japanese: これは近年もっとも拡大したものの一つだろう。
lines.english: It was probably one of the ideas that had spread most widely in recent years.

lines.japanese:
ただしもっぱら、自業自得を正当な結果とするた
めの演繹として機能する。
lines.english: In practice, however, it served chiefly as a rationale for treating suffering as the deserved consequence of one's own actions.

lines.japanese:
あらゆる行動は糾弾対象になりうるということだ。
　行動するなら攻撃されることを覚悟すべきだ、と
いう論調が社会に定着している。
lines.english: Every action could become grounds for condemnation. The principle that anyone who acted had to be prepared for attack had taken root in society.

lines.japanese: 行動は社会的制裁のため晒される可能性がある。
lines.english: Anything a person did might be made public for purposes of social punishment.

lines.japanese:
インターネットは事実関係ならびに個人発言を固
定化する力があり、相互監視社会を塗り固めること
を促進した。
lines.english: The internet had the power to preserve facts and personal statements permanently, helping cement society into a system of mutual surveillance.

lines.japanese:
実際の善悪よりも、多数派にとっての感情が優先
され、正当化されることがある。
lines.english: The majority's feelings could take precedence over actual right and wrong and then be justified as though they were.

lines.japanese:
ただ法に背かないというだけでは、非難を免れる
ことはできないのが近代だ。
lines.english: In the modern age, merely staying within the law could not shield one from condemnation.

lines.japanese: 法の枠組さえも越えて、人は生きねばならない。
lines.english: People had to live by standards beyond even the framework of law.

lines.japanese:
多数派に寄り添うような価値観を身につけること。
　この曖昧な掟を、子供の頃から誰もが身につけよ
うと労苦する。
lines.english: One had to adopt values aligned with the majority. Everyone labored from childhood to master that ambiguous unwritten rule.

lines.japanese:
冷静に考えれば、比較的容易なことなのだ。
　結果、危険性も減少し安定した生活を手に入れる
ことができる。
lines.english: Considered calmly, it was comparatively easy. It reduced risk and brought a stable life within reach.

lines.japanese:
節度ある大人とは、そういうものを差すようにな
ってもいる。
lines.english: Indeed, that was increasingly what people meant by a responsible adult.

lines.japanese: 社会の構成員になれば、逸脱することは困難だ。
lines.english: Once one became a member of society, stepping outside it was difficult.

lines.japanese:
人々のまなざしには社会的制裁に直結した威力が
ある。
lines.english: The eyes of others carried the force of social punishment.

lines.japanese:
元来は異なった原義の自己責任という言葉は、責
の最終的な帰属先として用いられるようになった。
lines.english: The phrase personal responsibility, whose original meaning had been different, came to name the place where blame finally came to rest.

lines.japanese:
それに応じることのできる倫理的に完全な存在は、
ない。
lines.english: No ethically perfect being could meet that demand.

lines.japanese:
結果、リスクのある行動への意欲をスポイルする
態勢ができあがる。
lines.english: The result was a system that discouraged any action involving risk.

lines.japanese:
多少息詰まるが、人に迷惑はかけられない。
　誰もがそう考えるべきとされた。
　８０億の人類で、ひとつの地球をわけあっていた。
lines.english: It was stifling, but one must not inconvenience others. Everyone was expected to think that way. Eight billion human beings shared one Earth.

lines.japanese:
表面上は等分に。
　現実問題、たぶんに差別を含んではいたが。
lines.english: Equally, on the surface. Reality, though, was steeped in discrimination.

lines.japanese:
権利については、人が享受しうる総面積を上回っ
ているのかも知れない。
lines.english: Taken together, those rights might occupy more space than humanity had to spare.

lines.japanese:
一人一人の権利はあまりにも大きすぎた。
　実際に機能するのは、多勢の側に立つ者の権利で
あることが多かったが。
lines.english: Each individual’s rights had grown far too large. In practice, though, the rights of those aligned with the majority tended to be the ones that carried any force.

lines.japanese:
だからだろうか。
　小説で価値観を提示することは罪になった。
lines.english: Was that the reason? Presenting values in a novel had become a sin.

lines.japanese:
結果、登場人物は狭間に立たされ、悩むばかりで、
正しい結論を見付けることができなくなった。
lines.english: As a result, characters were stranded between opposing sides, able only to agonize and unable to arrive at any right conclusion.

lines.japanese: イデオロギーの是非など、忍にはどうでも良かった。
lines.english: Shinobu did not care whether any ideology was right or wrong.

lines.japanese:
物語としてはそれでも楽しいのだから。
　ただ、何が正しいのか。
　何が誤りなのか。
lines.english: The stories remained enjoyable regardless. But what was right? What was wrong?

lines.japanese:
その正しさは、現実的に実現可能なのか。
　不可能であるならば、代案としてどうすべきなのか。
lines.english: Could what was right actually be made real? If not, what should be done instead?

lines.japanese:
結論の出ない命題だけが、捨て置かれた。
　だから、世界はテーマを失ってしまったのではな
いか。
lines.english: All that remained were questions with no answer, left where they lay. Perhaps that was why the world had lost its theme.

lines.japanese:
忍の手が止まる。
　大きな葛藤を抱えた者の憂いが、面差しを変える。
lines.english: Shinobu's hands stopped. The shadow of some great inner conflict passed over his face.

lines.japanese: （疲れている、のかな）
lines.english: (Maybe I'm tired.)

lines.japanese: （倫理に背かないように生きるって、大変だ）
lines.english: (It's hard to live without breaking some ethical rule.)

lines.japanese:
（誰に迷惑をかけていないようであっても、それを
　不快に思う人がいる……）
lines.english: (Even when it seems as if you aren't troubling anyone, someone out there will still be offended…)

lines.japanese: （別に誰かを傷つけたいわけじゃないんだ）
lines.english: (It's not as though I want to hurt anyone.)

lines.japanese: （……侵害したいわけじゃない）
lines.english: (…I don't want to violate anyone's rights.)

lines.japanese:
（けど……誰も侵害しないようにすると、大人しく
　してるしかないんだよな……）
lines.english: (But… if you try never to violate anyone's rights at all, your only choice is to sit quietly and do nothing…)

lines.japanese:
推測に落ち込むことができる忍だ。
　考え始めると、際限なく沈んでいく。
lines.english: Shinobu could sink into gloom on conjecture alone. Once he began thinking, there was no limit to how deeply he sank.

lines.japanese: （彼女は、沙也加は……みんなから弾かれてた）
lines.english: (She—Sayaka—was cast out by everyone.)

lines.japanese: （本当は、あんなに優しい子なのに）
lines.english: (Even though she's really so kind.)

lines.japanese: （いやだな……）
lines.english: (I hate this…)

lines.japanese:
うつむき、内面から噴出するどす黒い不快感に、
忍は堪えた。
lines.english: Head bowed, Shinobu endured the pitch-black revulsion erupting from within.

lines.japanese: 背中に触れたものがあった。
lines.english: Something touched his back.

lines.japanese: 「あ……沙也加？」
lines.english: “Oh… Sayaka?”

lines.japanese: 突然のことに戸惑う。
lines.english: The suddenness left him bewildered.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしたの？」
lines.english: “W-what's wrong?”

lines.japanese:
沙也加は黙って背中に張りついている。
　忍の動転を、無言で楽しんでいる節があった。
lines.english: Sayaka clung silently to his back. She seemed to be enjoying his confusion without a word.

lines.japanese: 「……あのー」

黙ったまま。
　背後から回った手が、胸板のあたりを抱いた。
lines.english: Still silent. Her arms came around from behind and held him across the chest.

lines.japanese:
驚きが過ぎ去ると、体が熱くなった。
　自分の体内に若いエネルギーがこれほど渦巻いて
いることを、忍は暗中の光を見る思いで受け止めた。
lines.english: Once the shock had passed, his body grew hot. The discovery of so much youthful energy churning inside him felt like a light in the dark.

lines.japanese:
上から、手を重ねる。
　呼応した沙也加が、指先を絡めてくる。
　きつく結びつく。
lines.english: He laid his hands over hers. In response, Sayaka laced her fingers through his. They locked tightly together.

lines.japanese:
抱きしめたくなる。
　もどかしい気持ちがいよいよ高まってくると、絶
妙のタイミングで黒髪の少女は声を出した。
lines.english: He wanted to embrace her. Just as his restless longing rose toward its peak, the black-haired girl spoke with perfect timing.

lines.japanese: 「今はあなたがいるから」
lines.english: “Because you’re here now.”

lines.japanese:
心でも読まれたのだろうか。
　荒唐無稽な空想だが、沙也加だったらあるかも知
れない。
lines.english: Had she read his mind? It was a preposterous fancy, but with Sayaka it somehow seemed possible.

lines.japanese:
心を読むにはいろいろな方法がある。
　不条理な力以外にも、経験や長いつきあいのうち
に、それを見取る術もあるのだ。
lines.english: There were many ways to read another's mind. Even without some impossible power, experience and long companionship could teach you how.

lines.japanese: （そうだ）
lines.english: (That's right.)

lines.japanese: （過去があって今がある）
lines.english: (The past is what makes the present.)

lines.japanese: （変えられない歴史の上に、今があるんだ）
lines.english: (The present stands on a history that cannot be changed.)

lines.japanese: （時間をさかのぼることはできない）
lines.english: (I can't go back in time.)

lines.japanese:
（今が気にくわないからといって、過去を改竄する
　ような真似は……できたとしても、みっともない）
lines.english: (Even if I could, rewriting the past because I disliked the present would be pathetic.)

lines.japanese: （みっともないってわかってるのに）
lines.english: (Even though I know it's pathetic.)

lines.japanese: （人生はゲームじゃないって、わかってるのに――）
lines.english: (Even though I know life isn't a game—)

lines.japanese: 「一人で抱え込むって、約束だものね」
lines.english: “That was the promise, after all: to carry it alone.”

lines.japanese: 「……よく覚えてるね」
lines.english: “…You remembered.”

lines.japanese: 「約束は忘れない」
lines.english: “I do not forget promises.”

lines.japanese: 「それにそう昔のことでもないじゃない」
lines.english: “Besides, it was not so very long ago.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうか、何年かしか経ってないのか」
lines.english: “…I guess it has only been a few years.”

lines.japanese: 「ずいぶんと昔のことに思える？」
lines.english: “Does it feel much longer?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「時間感覚、鈍いんだ」
lines.english: “I have a poor sense of time.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね、鈍いわね」
lines.english: “Yes. You do.”

lines.japanese:
優しい声。
　何を言われても、悪い気はしない。
lines.english: A gentle voice. She could have said anything in that voice and he would not have minded.

lines.japanese:
「忍は、ぼんやりとしているのが合っているんだと
　思うわ」
lines.english: “I think being dreamy suits you, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「年寄りみたいだね」
lines.english: “Makes me sound like an old man.”

lines.japanese: 「生き急いでも疲れるだけ」
lines.english: “All rushing through life does is wear you out.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうも言ってられないよ」
lines.english: “…I can't afford to think that way.”

lines.japanese: 「いつまで一緒にいられるか、わからないんだし」
lines.english: “We don't know how long we can stay together.”

lines.japanese: 「こわいことだよ、それは」
lines.english: “That's frightening.”

lines.japanese: 「失うことが？」
lines.english: “Losing someone?”

lines.japanese: 「こわいよ」
lines.english: “It scares me.”

lines.japanese: 「誰にもいなくなって欲しくない」
lines.english: “I don't want anyone to disappear.”

lines.japanese: 「私はいなくならない」
lines.english: “I will not disappear.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。もう、いなくならない」
lines.english: “Yes. I won't disappear again.”

lines.japanese: 「ずっといてよ」
lines.english: “Stay with me. Always.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、いる」
lines.english: “I will.”

lines.japanese: 「離れないで」
lines.english: “Don't leave me.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、離れない」
lines.english: “I won't.”

lines.japanese: 「どこかに行かれたら、守ってあげられなくなる」
lines.english: “If you go somewhere else, I won't be able to protect you.”

lines.japanese: 「守って欲しいから、離れない」
lines.english: “I want you to protect me, so I won't leave.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう約束だったね」
lines.english: “That was our promise.”

lines.japanese: 遠くはない過去に、忍は思いを馳せた。
lines.english: His thoughts went back to the not-so-distant past.

lines.japanese:
「私はいなくならない。けど、もし私たちの誰かが
　いなくなったとして……」
lines.english: “I won't disappear. But if one of us ever did…”

lines.japanese: 「そのとき、忍が傷つくのが心配だわ」
lines.english: “I worry about how much it would hurt you.”

lines.japanese: 「誰かなんて、考えられないよ」
lines.english: “I can't stand to think of it happening to anyone.”

lines.japanese: 「そうでしょうけど」
lines.english: “No, I suppose not.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、仕方ないこと。動かせないことだから」
lines.english: “But some things cannot be helped. Some things cannot be changed.”

lines.japanese: 「……嫌なんだよ」
lines.english: “…I don't want that.”

lines.japanese: 「ブチとマルを失った時、私もそうだった」
lines.english: “I felt the same when I lost Spot and Roly.”

lines.japanese: 「あの子たちは、私の心の一部だった」
lines.english: “They were part of my heart.”

lines.japanese: 「半身をもがれたように感じた」
lines.english: “I felt as though half of me had been torn away.”

lines.japanese: 「でも今は、こんな風にいられる」
lines.english: “And yet I can live like this now.”

lines.japanese: 「時間が解決するって？」
lines.english: “You're saying time heals it?”

lines.japanese:
「喪失したときは落ち込むけれど、立ち直った時、
　失意は前に進む力に転じる。形を変えて」
lines.english: “Loss casts us down. But when we rise again, despair changes shape and becomes strength to move forward.”

lines.japanese:
「何かを守ろうという願いは、昔の私にはなかった
　ものだもの」
lines.english: “The person I was before never wanted to protect anything.”

lines.japanese:
「あの子たちの心の一部が、変化したもののように
　も思える」
lines.english: “It feels as though that desire might be what a piece of their hearts became.”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん死なせてしまったことは哀しいけど……」
lines.english: “Naturally, I am still sad that I let them die…”

lines.japanese: 「そういった終わりを、認めてあげるしかない」
lines.english: “I can only accept that their lives ended that way.”

lines.japanese: 「……まるで強い人だよ、それじゃ」
lines.english: “…That makes you sound so strong.”

lines.japanese: 「忍は強くならないと」
lines.english: “You must become strong, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「私たち全員の思いを背負っていくんだから」
lines.english: “Because you're going to carry the feelings of all of us.”

lines.japanese:
何も言えない。
　沙也加は正しいことを言っていた。
lines.english: He could say nothing. Sayaka was right.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「……どうしてあやまるの？」
lines.english: “…Why are you apologizing?”

lines.japanese: 「わからない。けど、ごめん」
lines.english: “I don't know. But I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんって言えって、どこかで誰かが言ってる」
lines.english: “Somewhere, someone is telling me to say I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「……もしかして……」
lines.english: “…Could it be…?”

lines.japanese: 背後で沙也加の声が、不安に揺らいだ。
lines.english: Behind him, Sayaka's voice wavered with unease.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ」
lines.english: “Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 声に張りが戻る。
lines.english: The strength returned to her voice.

lines.japanese: 「そうね、じゃいいことを教えてあげる」
lines.english: “Then let me tell you something nice.”

lines.japanese: 「うん？」
lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese:
「さっきそばにいるって言ったけど……守ってもら
　いたいっていうのは嘘よ」
lines.english: “I said I would stay beside you… but wanting you to protect me was a lie.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ？」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese:
衝撃を受ける。
　痛ましい言葉を投げかけられるのではないかと、
心が萎縮した。
lines.english: The shock went through him. His heart clenched as he braced for whatever hurtful words might come next.

lines.japanese: 沙也加は鈴をころがすように笑う。
lines.english: Sayaka laughed with a silvery peal.

lines.japanese:
「逆だもの。本当は、私が守ってあげようと思って
　いたの」
lines.english: “It's the other way around. I was the one planning to protect you.”
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese: それはそれで意表を突かれる。
lines.english: That surprised him in an entirely different way.

lines.japanese: 「なにから？」
lines.english: “From what?”

lines.japanese: 「寂しさから」
lines.english: “From loneliness.”

lines.japanese: 一瞬考え込んだ。
lines.english: He thought for a moment.

lines.japanese: 「……ああ、一緒にいてくれるってことだ」
lines.english: “…Oh. You mean you'll stay with me.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうね」
lines.english: “…Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「悩んで、迷って、悔いて……それで立ち返った時、
　今の言葉を思い出して」
lines.english: “When you've agonized, lost your way, regretted… and finally found your way back, remember what I just said.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと？」
lines.english: “What do you mean?”

lines.japanese:
外から人の気配が近づいてきた。
　沙也加がすっと身を離す。
lines.english: Someone approached outside. Sayaka slipped away from him.

lines.japanese:
ぬくもりが失せ、冷たい空気が両者をわかつ。
　次の言葉が、忍をしたたかに打ちのめした。
lines.english: Her warmth vanished, leaving only cold air between them. Her next words dealt Shinobu a crushing blow.

lines.japanese: 「そのときまで、もたないかも知れないから」
lines.english: “Because I may not last until then.”

lines.japanese: 工場の扉が開いた。
lines.english: The factory door opened.

lines.japanese: 「おはよい！」
lines.english: “G'mornin'!”

lines.japanese: 「おかえりなさい」
lines.english: “Welcome home.”

lines.japanese: 「ただいまー」
lines.english: “I'm home!”

lines.japanese: 一目見て、沙也加は眉を集めた。
lines.english: Sayaka took one look and knitted her brows.

lines.japanese: 「……あなたね」
lines.english: “Honestly, you…”

lines.japanese: あずさが反射的にびくつく。
lines.english: Azusa flinched reflexively.

lines.japanese: 「ひ、久々に指導がっ！？」
lines.english: “A-a lesson? After all this time!?”

lines.japanese: 「せっかくの可愛い制服なんだから、ちゃんと着る」
lines.english: “It is such a pretty uniform. Wear it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「ちゃんとしてきたんだけどなぁ……」
lines.english: “But I did wear it right…”

lines.japanese:
「衿がよれてる。ほら、リボンも傾いて……ワンタ
　ッチのリボンじゃなくて、ちゃんと結ぶ方にしな
　さいな」
lines.english: “Your collar is crumpled. And look, your ribbon is crooked… Stop using a clip-on and wear one you actually have to tie.”

lines.japanese: 「は、結べませんです」
lines.english: “I-I can’t tie it, ma’am.”

lines.japanese: 「教えたでしょう」
lines.english: “I taught you.”

lines.japanese: 「は、覚え切れませんでした」
lines.english: “I-I could not remember it all, ma'am.”

lines.japanese: 沙也加はあずさの鼻をつまんだ。
lines.english: Sayaka pinched Azusa's nose.

lines.japanese: 「お馬鹿さん」
lines.english: “Silly girl.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶぃぎぃ」
lines.english: “Bweeghee.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしもそっちの制服がいいなあ」
lines.english: “I want your uniform instead.”

lines.japanese: 「……華がないわよ」
lines.english: “…It has no flair.”

lines.japanese: 「オトナノオンナって感じで」
lines.english: “It has that Grown-Up Woman look!”

lines.japanese: 「そんな黙っていてもなれるものに憧れない」
lines.english: “Don't aspire to something you'll become just by waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「……まーそうなんだけど」
lines.english: “…Well, true.”

lines.japanese: 「ミニを履きたくても、似合わない女もいるのよ」
lines.english: “Some women want to wear miniskirts but simply do not look good in them.”

lines.japanese: 「……それって、沙也加ねーさんですか？」
lines.english: “…You mean you, Sayaka?”

lines.japanese: ガスの元栓をひねるように、あずさの鼻を歪めた。
lines.english: She twisted Azusa's nose like the valve on a gas line.

lines.japanese: 「うぶぶぶっ」
lines.english: “Ubububuh!”

lines.japanese:
「あずさはこういう方が似合っているのだから、ちゃ
　んと着こなしなさい」
lines.english: “This style suits you better, Azusa, so learn to wear it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「は、着こなす方向で」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I’ll work toward wearing it properly.”

lines.japanese: 「……こうした方が可愛いかしら？」
lines.english: “…Would it look prettier like this?”

lines.japanese: 「うほ」
lines.english: “Ooh.”

lines.japanese: 楽しげに―――
lines.english: Happily—

lines.japanese:
だが忍は立ち尽くす。
　先ほどの沙也加の言葉は、雷のようだった。
　二人のじゃれあいを、遠く見ることしかできない。
lines.english: But Shinobu stood rooted in place. Sayaka's earlier words had struck like a thunderbolt. He could only watch their play from far away.

lines.japanese: 会話に加わっていくことができない気がした。
lines.english: He felt unable to join their conversation.

lines.japanese: （……もたない？）
lines.english: (…Not last?)

lines.japanese:
何かを忘れていた。
　いや、忘却ではない。
lines.english: He had forgotten something. No—this was not forgetting.

lines.japanese: （忘れてはいない……）
lines.english: (I haven't forgotten…)

lines.japanese: （けど、これは）
lines.english: (But this is…)

lines.japanese:
記憶をさらって、愕然とする。
　そこには見たくない出来事で渦巻いていた。
lines.english: He raked through his memory and recoiled. What he found there was a maelstrom of events he did not want to see.

lines.japanese:
刺すような頭痛。
　圧倒的な不安を、未来に見るかのように。
lines.english: A stabbing headache. As though he had glimpsed some overwhelming dread in the future.

lines.japanese: （なんだ……このビジョンは……？）
lines.english: (What… is this vision…?)

lines.japanese: 悪い予感に過ぎない。
lines.english: Nothing more than a bad premonition.

lines.japanese: （そうだ、予感だ……）
lines.english: (That's right. Just a premonition…)

lines.japanese: （だけどさ……予感でも、いやだよ……）
lines.english: (But… even if it's only a premonition, I don't want it…)

lines.japanese: （いやだよ、沙也加―――）
lines.english: (I don't want it, Sayaka—)

lines.japanese:
「どうしてもこの制服が欲しかったら、私のお下が
　りをあげるから」
lines.english: “If you want this uniform that badly, you can have mine as a hand-me-down.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほんと？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「みんなくれるわよ」
lines.english: “Everyone else will give you theirs too.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、みんなにもらおう！」
lines.english: “Yay! I'll get one from everybody!”

lines.japanese: 「イメクラ、コスプレ」
lines.english: “Fetish club. Cosplay.”

lines.japanese: 「……その言葉は、今すぐ忘れなさい」
lines.english: “…Forget those words at once.”

lines.japanese: 「いたたたたたっ！？」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, ow, ow!?”

lines.japanese: 遠い―――
lines.english: Far away—

lines.japanese: （……見えてしまう……）
lines.english: (…I can see it…)

lines.japanese: （これが未来だっていうのか）
lines.english: (Is this supposed to be the future?)

lines.japanese: （避けられない……未来だって）
lines.english: (An inescapable… future?)

lines.japanese: （だからこんなに……悲しいのか）
lines.english: (Is that why… I'm so sad?)

lines.japanese:
（……こんな悲しい思いをするんだったら……力な
　んていらない）
lines.english: (If this power is going to make me this sad… I don't want it.)

lines.japanese: （ＵＳＥＲでなくていい―――）
lines.english: (I don't have to be a USER—)

lines.japanese:
「どうしてもこの制服が欲しかったら、私のお下が
　りをあげるから」
lines.english: “If you want this uniform that badly, you can have mine as a hand-me-down.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほんと？」
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「みんなくれるわよ」
lines.english: “Everyone else will give you theirs too.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、みんなにもらおう！」
lines.english: “Yay! I'll get one from everybody!”

lines.japanese: 「イメクラ、コスプレ」
lines.english: “Fetish club. Cosplay.”

lines.japanese: 「……その言葉は、今すぐ忘れなさい」
lines.english: “…Forget those words at once.”

lines.japanese: 「いたたたたたっ！？」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, ow, ow!?”

lines.japanese: 遠い―――
lines.english: Far away—

lines.japanese: 「おい、フリョー」
lines.english: “Hey, punk.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだメスガキ」
lines.english: “What, brat?”

lines.japanese: 気怠い調子で樋口章二。
lines.english: Shouji Higuchi answered in a languid drawl.

lines.japanese: 「なんか面白い話しれ」
lines.english: “Tell me something interesting.”

lines.japanese:
いつもの反応からすれば、ここは『言ってろ乳児』
か『おまえが話せ。おもらしした時の逸話をな』で
ある。
lines.english: His customary response would have been either ‘Keep talking, infant,’ or ‘You tell one. The story of the time you wet yourself.’

lines.japanese: しかし、戯れる気分ではなかったのだろう。
lines.english: But perhaps he was in no mood for their usual games.

lines.japanese: 「よかろう―――」
lines.english: “Very well—”

lines.japanese: 珍しく、応じた。
lines.english: For once, he obliged.

lines.japanese:
「あれは、よく晴れた昼下がりだった。その日のオレ
　様は、薄汚れた事務所でうらぶれた我が身を嘆く為
　とっておきのワイルドなターキーを愉しんでいた」
lines.english: “It was a bright and cloudless afternoon. That day, I was sitting in my dingy office, nursing a choice Wild Turkey as I lamented my fallen fortunes.”

lines.japanese: 「いきなり酒かよ……」
lines.english: “Straight to the booze…”

lines.japanese:
「オレ様にはつらい過去があった。それは、宇宙空間
　の事故で２５年間冷凍睡眠状態で漂っていたため、
　時間の流れから取り残されてしまったことだ」
lines.english: “I had a tragic past. After an accident in space left me drifting in cryogenic sleep for twenty-five years, the flow of time had passed me by.”

lines.japanese:
実際に起こった面白い話ではなく、章二の素話を
愉しむという趣旨のようだ。
lines.english: Apparently the point was not to hear an amusing true story, but to enjoy one of Shouji's improvised tales.

lines.japanese: 「おいオッサ―――」
lines.english: “Hey, old ma—”

lines.japanese:
言いかけるあずさの肩を、左右から忍と笛子が掴
んで止めた。
lines.english: As Azusa started to speak, Shinobu and Fueko seized her shoulders from either side and stopped her.

lines.japanese: 小声で、
lines.english: In whispers—

lines.japanese: 「平気平気」
lines.english: “It's fine. It's fine.”

lines.japanese: 「なにゆえ？」
lines.english: “How so?”

lines.japanese: 「途中からネタ切れて実際の話になるパターンよ」
lines.english: “He’ll run out of material halfway through and switch to something that actually happened.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむう」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
「時からも忘れ去られたオレ様の探偵業は、残念な
　がら好調とは言えなかった。助手のヤスにも満足
　に給料を払ってやれず失踪され」
lines.english: “Forgotten by time itself, my detective agency was, regrettably, far from thriving. I couldn't even pay my assistant Yasu a proper salary, so he vanished.”

lines.japanese:
「共同経営者だった三郎もふらりとオホーツクに消
　え、風の噂ではクリオネ・ショウの司会者をおっ
　ぱじめたって話だ」
lines.english: “My partner Saburo wandered off to Okhotsk too. Last I heard, he'd started hosting a clione show.”

lines.japanese: 「めちゃくちゃだな……」
lines.english: “This is all over the place…”

lines.japanese: 「……美人助手が足りない」
lines.english: “…It needs a beautiful assistant.”

lines.japanese:
「銀色事件と呼ばれたとある国家的犯罪を暴いたこ
　とで、オレ様には多少のたくわえがあったことが
　幸いした。餓えることもなく、痛飲の日々が続く」
lines.english: “Fortunately, I had some savings from exposing a national crime known as The Silver Case. I did not starve, and my days of hard drinking continued.”

lines.japanese: 「……ヤスに給料……」
lines.english: “…But Yasu's salary…”

lines.japanese: 「金あるのに未払い……」
lines.english: “You had money and still didn't pay him…”

lines.japanese:
「そんなオレ様のもとに、ある日、一人の依頼人が
　訪れた」
lines.english: “Then one day, a client came to me.”

lines.japanese:
「素性のわからない依頼人だった。オレの刑事とし
　てのカンが、こいつは怪しいと告げた」
lines.english: “A client of uncertain background. My cop's instincts told me there was something suspicious about her.”

lines.japanese:
「美人の依頼人、そして高額のギャラ。だがオレは
　結局その仕事を受け、モスクワのチェルノートン
　研究所に飛んだ」
lines.english: “A beautiful client and a fat fee. Still, I took the case and flew to the Chernoton Research Facility in Moscow.”

lines.japanese:
「そこで大規模な災厄を未然に防いだオレ様だが、
　事件はそれだけでは終わらなかった。返す刀で、
　オレは新神戸シティに飛んだ」
lines.english: “I prevented a catastrophe there, but the case did not end. From there, I flew to Neo Kobe City.”

lines.japanese: 「そこでの情報集めは困難を極めた」
lines.english: “Gathering information there proved exceedingly difficult.”

lines.japanese:
「隔離閉鎖されたこの街では、何もかもが嘘っぱち
　で固められていた。オレは情報を得るため、ギャ
　ラクシ蟹という危険なゲームに没頭した」
lines.english: “In that sealed and quarantined city, everything was built from lies. To obtain information, I plunged into a dangerous game called Galaxy Crab.”

lines.japanese:
「バーに行くと若いパンクなバーテンが出て行けと
　言ってきた」
lines.english: “At a bar, a young punk bartender told me to get out.”

lines.japanese:
「チョコバーを差し出すと、猫なで声でどこで見付け
　たんだと言って情報をくれたが、もう一回同じ質問
　をしたらけんもほろろに出て行けと言ってきた」
lines.english: “When I offered him a chocolate bar, he cooed about where I'd found it and gave me the information. But when I asked the same question again, he coldly told me to get out.”

lines.japanese:
「狂っていた。さらに玄関先でボコボコに殴られた。
　何が何だかわかりゃしねぇ」
lines.english: “It was madness. Then someone beat me senseless outside the front door. I had no idea what was happening.”

lines.japanese: 「こっちの台詞だよ……」
lines.english: “That's my line…”

lines.japanese:
「情報にあった現場に行ってみたが、ひどい有様だっ
　たぜ。廃ビルみたいなところで、夜景側にパンツ
　一丁で行くと落ちて死んじまうんだ」
lines.english: “I went to the place my information pointed to, and it was a disaster. In some abandoned building, if you walked toward the night view wearing nothing but your underwear, you'd fall to your death.”

lines.japanese: 「昔はすげえ、その一言に尽きた」
lines.english: “The old days were wild. That’s all I can say.”

lines.japanese: 「世界がわからん……」
lines.english: “I no longer understand this world…”

lines.japanese:
「麻薬についての情報を集めるため、クラブ・ポピー
　に赴いたオレは、そこで時限爆弾の解体をすること
　になった」
lines.english: “Seeking information about the drugs, I went to Club Poppy, where I ended up defusing a time bomb.”

lines.japanese:
「イライラ棒みたいな解体を何度か失敗していると、
　相棒のエドが自分にかわれと言ってきた」
lines.english: “After I failed the wire-loop sort of disarmament several times, my partner Ed told me to let him take over.”

lines.japanese:
「かわった途端に迷路簡単になっていた。超なめや
　がって、トサカに来たぜ」
lines.english: “The instant he did, the maze got easier. They were seriously screwing with me. I was furious.”

lines.japanese: 「で、依頼人はどうなったの？」
lines.english: “What happened to the client?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ。結局のところ、クスリ絡みだった。隣街か
　ら来て売りさばいていたヤツがいて。で、巻き込
　まれた女がいて」
lines.english: “Right. In the end, it was about drugs. Some guy had come from the next town to sell them, and a girl got caught up in it.”

lines.japanese:
「しかもうちのガッコだったんで、オレのとこに
　来やがった」
lines.english: “She happened to go to our school, so she came to me.”

lines.japanese: 「オホーツク全然関係ねぇ」
lines.english: “Okhotsk had nothing to do with anything.”

lines.japanese: 「最後はどうなったのよ？」
lines.english: “How did it end?”

lines.japanese: 「倒した」
lines.english: “I beat him.”

lines.japanese: 「倒すな倒すな」
lines.english: “No beating people up. No.”

lines.japanese: 「……いたたまれないですね」
lines.english: “…That is painful to listen to.”

lines.japanese: 「クスリ関係増えたね」
lines.english: “There have been more drugs around lately.”

lines.japanese: 「リーガルも多いがな」
lines.english: “A lot of it's legal, too.”

lines.japanese: 「法律が追いついてないのよね」
lines.english: “The law hasn't caught up.”

lines.japanese: 「時代遅れなんだよ」
lines.english: “It's behind the times.”

lines.japanese: 「どうした？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、要点だなって思って」
lines.english: “Nothing. I just thought that was the heart of it.”

lines.japanese: 「法律じゃ全てをカバーできないもんね」
lines.english: “The law can't cover everything.”

lines.japanese: 「だから潤滑油がいる」
lines.english: “That's why you need someone to grease the wheels.”

lines.japanese: 「小銭を稼ぐ、と」
lines.english: “And make a little money on the side.”

lines.japanese: 「稼いでなどいない」
lines.english: “I'm not making any money from it.”

lines.japanese: 「なによ今の間は」
lines.english: “What was that pause for?”

lines.japanese:
「あ、あ、ちょっと前に校門のところで女の子から
　封筒もらってた」
lines.english: “Oh! Oh, I saw a girl give you an envelope at the school gates a little while ago.”

lines.japanese: 思い出したように言う。
lines.english: He said it as if the memory had only just returned to him.

lines.japanese: 「あれは図書券だ」
lines.english: “Those were book vouchers.”

lines.japanese: 「いくら分よ」
lines.english: “How much?”

lines.japanese: 「五万円」
lines.english: “Fifty thousand yen.”

lines.japanese: 「金券屋持って行ったわね？」
lines.english: “You took them to a voucher reseller, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「しこたま参考書を買ってやったぜ」
lines.english: “I went and bought a mountain of study guides.”

lines.japanese: 「……ありえねぇ」
lines.english: “…Unbelievable.”

lines.japanese:
「うるさい。だまれ。向こうが勝手によこしたもの
　だ。お礼とか言って」
lines.english: “Shut up. Just shut up. She gave them to me of her own accord. Said they were a thank-you.”

lines.japanese:
「まあ、確かにね……単にお礼以上のものを感じた
　けど」
lines.english: “True enough… though it felt like there was more to it than gratitude.”

lines.japanese: 「たらしー」
lines.english: “Playboy.”

lines.japanese: や
lines.english: do
“…Did you sleep with her?”

lines.japanese: や
lines.english: do

lines.japanese: 「まだ犯ってない」
lines.english: “Not yet.”

lines.japanese: 「まだって……」
lines.english: “Yet…?”

lines.japanese: 「本気になられても困る」
lines.english: “It'd be a problem if she got serious.”

lines.japanese: 「どう思いますか忍くん？」
lines.english: “What do you make of that, Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 「めっ」
lines.english: “Bad.”

lines.japanese: 「法には背いてない」
lines.english: “I'm not breaking any laws.”

lines.japanese: 「モラルには？」
lines.english: “What about morals?”

lines.japanese: 「漏れる」
lines.english: “It leaks.”

lines.japanese: 「漏らすな」
lines.english: “Don't leak.”

lines.japanese: 「話噛み合ってない」
lines.english: “That exchange made no sense.”

lines.japanese: 「法に、モラルねぇ……」
lines.english: “Law and morality, huh…”

lines.japanese: 「どっちも守ることなんてできやしないぜ」
lines.english: “You can't possibly obey both all the time.”

lines.japanese: 「うむん……」
lines.english: “Hmm…”

lines.japanese: 「最初から放棄する姿勢は糾弾されるわよ」
lines.english: “People will condemn you for giving up before you even try.”

lines.japanese: 「無理なもんは無理だ」
lines.english: “You can't do the impossible.”

lines.japanese:
「そうでしょうけど……口に出すと攻撃されやすい
　のよ」
lines.english: “Maybe so… but saying it out loud makes you an easy target.”

lines.japanese: 笛子はため息をついた。
lines.english: Fueko sighed.

lines.japanese: 「珍しい。笛子が悪を認めたぞ」
lines.english: “That’s unusual. Fueko just condoned evil.”

lines.japanese:
「何よ珍しいって……いつも正論ばかり言ってるみ
　たいじゃない」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘unusual’? You make it sound like all I ever do is preach.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってるだろう」
lines.english: “You do.”

lines.japanese: 「むか。若いから考え方だって柔軟なのよ」
lines.english: “Hmph. I'm young. My thinking is perfectly flexible.”

lines.japanese: 「それに悪を認めたわけじゃないわよ」
lines.english: “Besides, I did not condone evil.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえねえ」
lines.english: “Hey, hey.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「どうやったら正しいものになれるの？」
lines.english: “How do you become someone who's right?”

lines.japanese: 「……あんたもヘビィなこときくわね」
lines.english: “…You do ask some heavy questions.”

lines.japanese: 「気になった」
lines.english: “I was wondering.”

lines.japanese: 「自分が正しいと思えばいい」
lines.english: “Just believe you're right.”

lines.japanese: 「それはマイ正義でしょうが」
lines.english: “That's your own private justice.”

lines.japanese: 「まずルールは守らないといけないよね」
lines.english: “First you have to follow the rules, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうね」
lines.english: “R-Right.”

lines.japanese: 「で、あと見えない暗黙の常識とかを全部守る、と」
lines.english: “Then you follow every invisible, unspoken convention as well.”

lines.japanese: 「いい子だ」
lines.english: “Good boy.”

lines.japanese: 「それでいいんじゃないでしょうか、オス……」
lines.english: “That should do, I supp—”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ」
lines.english: “Then…”

lines.japanese: 「相反してる暗黙の了解ごとがあったら？」
lines.english: “What if two unspoken rules contradict each other?”

lines.japanese: 「目玉焼きにはソースかソイソースか」
lines.english: “Brown sauce or soy sauce on your fried eggs.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうの違う」
lines.english: “That's not what I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「た、たとえば？」
lines.english: “F-For example?”

lines.japanese: 「そうね」
lines.english: “Let's see.”

lines.japanese: 「自衛隊問題とか」
lines.english: “The question of the Self-Defense Forces.”

lines.japanese: 「重い、重いわ」
lines.english: “Heavy. Much too heavy.”

lines.japanese:
「たとえば自衛隊の一番偉い人は、どう振る舞
　ったら誰からも非難されないの？」
lines.english: “How, for example, could the person at the very top of the SDF behave without anyone condemning them?”

hyperlinks.preview: Ultimate responsibility for the Japan Self-Defense Forces rests with the Prime Minister.

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Ultimate responsibility for the Japan Self-Defense Forces rests with the Prime Minister.

lines.japanese: 「無理だ」
lines.english: “Impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね……どう振る舞っても、誰かが必ず……」
lines.english: “Right… No matter what they did, someone would always…”

lines.japanese: 「正しい状態を算出する方法がわからないな」
lines.english: “I don't know how to calculate the correct state.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃーやっぱり、一から考えてみっけていくし
　かないかと」
lines.english: “Well, you'd have to start from scratch and figure it out as you go, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「誰が？」
lines.english: “Who would?”

lines.japanese: 無言になった。
lines.english: She fell silent.

lines.japanese: 「忍さん、自衛隊、好き？」
lines.english: “Shinobu, do you like the Self-Defense Forces?”

lines.japanese: 「鉄砲こわいよ」
lines.english: “Guns scare me.”

lines.japanese:
「鉄砲は一度撃ったら装填に時間かかるので、騎馬
　隊で突入するのがいいですよ」
lines.english: “Once a gun has been fired, it takes time to reload, so the correct response is a cavalry charge.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「いつの戦法だ」
lines.english: “What era is that tactic from?”

lines.japanese: 「またなんで自衛隊なんですか」
lines.english: “Why the Self-Defense Forces, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「自衛隊はどうでもいいんだけど」
lines.english: “I don't actually care about the Self-Defense Forces.”

lines.japanese: 「正しいものになる方法ってあるのかなーと」
lines.english: “I was wondering if there was a way to become someone who's right.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese:
「まあ、法と倫理って理想社会の設計図みたいなも
　のだから」
lines.english: “Well, law and ethics are something like blueprints for an ideal society.”

lines.japanese:
「ただ現時点でそれが完全なものかどうかはわから
　ない。曖昧な言い方だけど、前向きにうまくまっ
　とうな道を探していくしかないわけで」
lines.english: “But we don't know whether that blueprint is perfect as it stands. I know that sounds vague, but all we can do is keep searching in good faith for the best, most decent way forward.”

lines.japanese:
「正しいことを、大多数が納得できるかという問題
　もあるぞ」
lines.english: “There's also the question of whether most people can accept what's right.”

lines.japanese:
「納得できない場合、間違っていても通ってしまっ
　たりするんだろうか？」
lines.english: “If they can't accept it, can something wrong still end up being accepted?”

lines.japanese: 「そうならないように、冷静な判断がデスネ」
lines.english: “To prevent that, we must exercise sober judgment, you see.”

lines.japanese: 「笛子ちゃん言ってることのらくらしてきた」
lines.english: “Fue, you're starting to waffle.”

lines.japanese: 「……これは伊月イジメか？」
lines.english: “…Is this Pick-on-Izuki Day?”

lines.japanese: 「ってわけでもないけど」
lines.english: “Not particularly.”

lines.japanese:
「……何をしても誰かから否定されるのは仕方ない
　ことなのか」
lines.english: “…So I suppose it's inevitable that someone will reject you, no matter what you do.”

lines.japanese:
「うんうん。部屋片づけようと思ってる時に片づけ
　ろって言われるのヤだよね」
lines.english: “Uh-huh, uh-huh. Like when you're about to clean your room and somebody tells you to clean it. That's the worst.”

lines.japanese: 「いやもう何がなんだか」
lines.english: “I don't even know what we're talking about anymore.”

lines.japanese:
「まあ、日本人はあまり民主主義には向いてないん
　だろう」
lines.english: “Well, the Japanese probably aren't terribly suited to democracy.”
“Communis—”

lines.japanese: 「ハイハイ、ストップストップ。脱線脱線」
lines.english: “All right, stop, stop. We're getting sidetracked.”
“…Tch.”

lines.japanese:
「まあ、そういう厳密なことは立場にふさわしい偉
　い人に任せよう、ね、忍？」
lines.english: “Anyway, let's leave questions that technical to important people in the proper positions, all right, Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 「それとも政治家になりたいの？」
lines.english: “Unless you want to be a politician?”

lines.japanese: 「……そういうわけじゃないんだけど」
lines.english: “…That's not it.”

lines.japanese:
「人間の社会にはふたつのルールがあって、そのど
　っちも守っていかないといけないのがもーなんか
　ゴチャっとしてなんか」
lines.english: “Human society has two sets of rules, and having to obey both of them just gets so tangled, and—and…”

lines.japanese: 拳を握った。
lines.english: He clenched a fist.

lines.japanese: 「二つのルール？」
lines.english: “Two sets of rules?”

lines.japanese: 「そして三つの袋」
lines.english: “And three bags.”

lines.japanese: 「法律と、ローカルルール」
lines.english: “The law, and local rules.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: 「ローカルルールは、善悪というより好悪なのかな」
lines.english: “Maybe local rules aren't so much about good and evil as what people like and dislike.”

lines.japanese:
「これも守らないとまともに生きてはいけないで
　しょ」
lines.english: “But you can't live a normal life without obeying those too, can you?”

lines.japanese:
「……生きていけないといけないんだけどね。どん
　な人でも」
lines.english: “…Everyone ought to be able to live. No matter what kind of person they are.”

lines.japanese: 「でも殺されるんだ」
lines.english: “But they get killed.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 思いも寄らない言葉に、笛子はぎょっとした。
lines.english: The words were so unexpected that Fueko started.

lines.japanese: 「生きたまま、殺されるんだ」
lines.english: “Killed while they're still alive.”

lines.japanese:
「振るまいとか性格とか、もしかしたら外見のこと
　でもあるかも知れない」
lines.english: “For how they act, or what they're like. Maybe even for how they look.”

lines.japanese:
「法律もローカルルールも、どっちも完全に守ろう
　と思ったら……その人は、何もできなくなると思う」
lines.english: “If someone tried to obey both the law and all the local rules perfectly… I don't think they'd be able to do anything at all.”

lines.japanese:
「この二つのルールは、時に入れ子になって部分を
　交換しながら、大きな流れに沿って人を押し流す
　んだ……」
lines.english: “Sometimes the two sets of rules nest inside each other, trading pieces as they go, and sweep people away on the larger current…”

lines.japanese:
「それがこの国の人間が言う、正しいってことなの
　かな」
lines.english: “Is that what the people of this country mean when they say something is right?”

lines.japanese: 「忍は、何のことを言ってるの？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about, Shinobu?”
“I mean—”

lines.japanese: 「おい」
lines.english: “Hey.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「欺瞞を、真に受けるな」
lines.english: “Don't buy into the hypocrisy.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうことだろ？」
lines.english: “That's what you're getting at, isn't it?”
“…More or less.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　え？　どういうこと？」
lines.english: “What? What? What does that mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ルールばかりじゃ成り立たないってことだ」
lines.english: “Rules alone aren't enough to make society work.”

lines.japanese:
「だから、そういうのを是正していくのが、理想と
　いうか……そういう話でしょうに！」
lines.english: “And correcting those flaws is the ideal—that's what we're talking about!”

lines.japanese:
「一万年くらいのうちに是正していけるといいなっ
　てことだ」
lines.english: “And with luck, we might get them corrected sometime in the next ten thousand years.”

lines.japanese: 笛子はむっとして、頬を膨らませた。
lines.english: Fueko puffed out her cheeks in a sulk.

lines.japanese: 「……間違ってないもん、私」
lines.english: “…I'm not wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、間違ってはいないと思う」
lines.english: “No. I don't think you are.”

lines.japanese:
「ただそれ以外のことで、気になることが多すぎた
　んだ」
lines.english: “There were just too many other things bothering me.”

lines.japanese:
「忍の疑問は、ちょっと難しいかな……ただ、だか
　らといって、無統制に振る舞うわけにはいかない
　もの」
lines.english: “Your question may be a little too difficult, Shinobu… But even so, we can't simply behave however we please.”

lines.japanese:
「ルールに間違いがあるなら、正しく直していくべき
　だし」
lines.english: “If a rule is wrong, we ought to set it right.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “You're right.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうすべきだったのかな」
lines.english: “…Was that what I should have done?”

lines.japanese:
空を見た。
　抜けるような青色。
　地表の淀みなどとは無縁の。
lines.english: He looked up at the sky. A blue so pure it seemed to go on forever. Untouched by the stagnation here on the ground.

lines.japanese:
「でも、今から勉強しようって思ってる時に勉強す
　るなはないよねぇ」
lines.english: “But if you're just about to start studying, it isn't fair for somebody to tell you not to.”

lines.japanese: 「……あずさや（涙）」
lines.english: “Oh, Azusa… (sob)”

lines.japanese: 頭を撫でた。
lines.english: He patted her head.

lines.japanese:
「うおっ、おっ？
　なんだなんだ？　誉められてる！？」
lines.english: “Whoa—huh? What's this? Am I being praised!?”

lines.japanese: 「あずさは可愛いなあ」
lines.english: “You're adorable, Azusa.”
“……thAnks.”

lines.japanese: 「あんま贔屓するな。つけあがる」
lines.english: “Don't play favorites. It'll go to her head.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだーやんのかーこのー」
lines.english: “Oh yeah? You wanna go?”

lines.japanese:
「喧嘩は大人になってから。まだまだ未成熟の
　あずさには販売できんな」
lines.english: “Fighting is for grown-ups. It's not for sale to an Azusa this underdeveloped.”

lines.japanese: 「がー」
lines.english: “Graaar!”

lines.japanese:
「どうだ笛子、オレは杓子定規なおまえと違い義と
　人情に厚い男だぞ」
lines.english: “You see, Fueko? Unlike a hidebound pedant such as yourself, I am a man of honor and compassion.”

lines.japanese: 「がー」
lines.english: “Graaar!”

lines.japanese: 「……何なんだおまえらは」
lines.english: “…What is wrong with you two?”

lines.japanese: 皆の語らいを、ぼんやりと眺める。
lines.english: He gazed absently at the others as they talked.

lines.japanese: （結論なんて、出る問題じゃないか……）
lines.english: (It isn't a question with an answer…)

lines.japanese: 少し昔を思い出した。
lines.english: He remembered something from not so long ago.

lines.japanese:
（結局、僕は彼女の手を取ることは
　できなかったんだし）
lines.english: (In the end, I couldn’t take her hand.)

lines.japanese: と、
lines.english: And then—

lines.japanese: 後ろから、誰かの手が伸ばされてきた。
lines.english: A hand reached toward him from behind.

lines.japanese:
斎だった。
　肩口に揺れる手には、あめ玉の袋。
lines.english: It was Itsuki. A hand hovered beside Shinobu's shoulder, holding a bag of candy.

lines.japanese: 「え？　飴くれるって？　サンクス」
lines.english: “Oh, you're giving me one? Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 袋に手を突っ込み、一つを取り出す。
lines.english: He reached into the bag and took one.

lines.japanese: 「梅飴だ。これ好きなんだよな」
lines.english: “Plum candy. I really like these.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　この飴は正しい飴かって？」
lines.english: “Hm? You want to know if this candy is right?”

lines.japanese: 黙考しかけて、忍は斎の意図に気が付いた。
lines.english: Shinobu almost stopped to ponder the question, then realized what Itsuki meant.

lines.japanese: 「……なるほど」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese:
笑う。
　斎も笑う。
lines.english: Shinobu laughed. Itsuki laughed too.

lines.japanese: 男の友情。
lines.english: Male bonding.

lines.japanese: 「あ、飴ちゃんだ。いいな」
lines.english: “Oh, candy! Lucky.”

lines.japanese:
「梅とかいうあたりがジジイくさくて反吐が出ます
　よね」
lines.english: “Plum, of all things. The sheer old-man stench is enough to make you retch.”

lines.japanese: 雲が出そうな兄妹喧嘩。
lines.english: A sibling quarrel fierce enough to summon storm clouds.

lines.japanese: 「やめてケンカはやめて！」
lines.english: “Stop! Please, don't fight!”

lines.japanese: 長閑だった。
lines.english: It was peaceful.

lines.japanese: その後、皆で梅の飴をなめながら歩いた。
lines.english: Afterward, they all walked along sucking plum candies.

lines.japanese: 「あ、なんかみんなのより大きな飴ちゃんだ」
lines.english: “Hey, my candy's bigger than everybody else's.”

lines.japanese:
「梅ちゃん飴の一袋に、一つだけ入っているという
　当たり飴ですね」
lines.english: “That’s the prize candy. They say there’s just one in each bag of Ume-chan Candies.”

lines.japanese: 「当たった！　なんか得した気分」
lines.english: “I got lucky! Feels like a bonus.”

lines.japanese:
男二人は複雑な気分。
　とりあえず、笑っておいた。
lines.english: The two men did not quite know how to feel. For the moment, they smiled.

lines.japanese: 人生に最善の答えなどありはしない―――
lines.english: There was no single best answer to life—

lines.japanese: 晴れた空の下、心からそう思う忍であった。
lines.english: And under that clear sky, Shinobu believed it with all his heart.

lines.japanese:
沙也加はいつもひとりだった。
　幾度か、声をかけてみたことがある。
lines.english: Sayaka was always alone. Shinobu had tried talking to her several times.

lines.japanese:
しかしどのようなタイミングで話しかけても、彼
女はまるで呼びかけに応じようとはしなかった。
lines.english: But no matter when he tried to speak to her, she never made the slightest attempt to answer.

lines.japanese: 頑なな拒絶の言葉を投げかけられることも多かった。
lines.english: Often, all he got was an adamant refusal.

lines.japanese:
はじめて出会った時、投げかけられた言葉の鋭さ
を、忍はなかなか忘れられない。
lines.english: Shinobu could never quite forget how sharply she had spoken to him when they first met.

lines.japanese:
同世代の人間から、心に影を落とすほどの影響を
受けたのははじめてだった。
lines.english: It was the first time anyone his age had affected him enough to cast a shadow over his heart.

lines.japanese:
だからというわけでもないのだろうが、いつしか
忍の視線は、沙也加の姿ばかりを追うようになる。
lines.english: That may not have been why, but before long Shinobu found his eyes following Sayaka and no one else.

lines.japanese: 沙也加について、忍が知っていることは多くない。
lines.english: Shinobu knew little about Sayaka.

lines.japanese:
成績は優秀であること。
　好き嫌いがないこと。
lines.english: That her grades were excellent. That she wasn't picky about food.

lines.japanese:
服装が地味なこと。
　友達がいないこと。
　資産家の娘であること。
lines.english: That she dressed plainly. That she had no friends. That she was the daughter of a wealthy family.

lines.japanese:
しかし両親を早くに亡くし、家族関係は希薄であ
ること。
lines.english: But that she had lost her parents young and had little connection with her family.

lines.japanese:
学年に二人用意しなければならない飼育委員を、
ひとりで担当していること。
lines.english: That she handled animal-care duty alone, though there were supposed to be two students from each grade.

lines.japanese:
それだけだ。
　学校である以上、多かれ少なかれ集団行動を強い
られるものだ。
lines.english: That was all. School inevitably forced its students into group activities to one degree or another.

lines.japanese:
しかしそれらは機械的にこなすことができる。
　暗黙の了解さえあれば、実質的な個が成立しうる
のである。
lines.english: But those obligations could be handled mechanically. As long as everyone tacitly agreed, a person could remain effectively on their own.

lines.japanese:
しかし定着するまでどれだけの軋轢があったのか
は、忍には想像もできなかった。
　忍もまたクラスでは、所属を持たない存在である。
lines.english: But Shinobu could not imagine how much friction it had taken to reach that arrangement. He too belonged nowhere in the class.

lines.japanese:
所属というのは、帰属集団のことだ。
　仲良しグループとも言う。
lines.english: By belonging, he meant membership in a group. A circle of friends, in other words.

lines.japanese:
