表面的には沙也加はずっと村八分であったし、忍
も良い助け手とは言えない。
lines.english: Outwardly, Sayaka remained an outcast, and Shinobu was hardly much help to her.

lines.japanese:
趣味も合わず、住む世界も違い、接点のまるでな
い二人だが、それでも互いの方針を覆すことはなか
った。
lines.english: They shared no interests, lived in different worlds, and had no points of contact at all. Even so, neither ever abandoned the course they had chosen.

lines.japanese:
長い旅のはじまりであった。
　二人は別物。
　互いの言語が異なっているに等しい。
lines.english: It was the beginning of a long journey. They were two different beings. They might as well have spoken different languages.

lines.japanese:
踏み越えることもできない広漠たる川を挟んで、
並行に進むに近い。
lines.english: They were like travelers moving in parallel on opposite banks of a vast river neither could cross.

lines.japanese:
歩調を合わせ、いつか渡河して触れあう瞬間を時
間をかけて探し求めた。
lines.english: Keeping pace, they took their time seeking the moment when they might one day ford it and touch.

lines.japanese:
限りなく恋人に近い友人とは、そういうものだか
らだ。
lines.english: For that is the nature of friends who stand just shy of being lovers.

lines.japanese: 時間が必要なのは当然である。
lines.english: Naturally, it would take time.

lines.japanese:
少しずつ、砂を一粒ずつ移しかえるように相互の
認識を観察し類推し演繹し、相対する理解……意識
の共有を模索するのであった。
lines.english: Little by little, as though moving one grain of sand at a time, they observed, inferred, and deduced each other's perceptions, searching for reciprocal understanding— for a consciousness they could share.

lines.japanese: ならびない何かを得んがために。
lines.english: All so they might gain something beyond compare.

lines.japanese:
沙也加はもう少し、かつての友を弔うのだと言う。
　忍は一人、帰路に就いていた。
lines.english: Sayaka had said she would remain a little longer to mourn her old friends. Shinobu was making his way home alone.

lines.japanese:
沙也加から受けた、重い相談のことを思い出さず
にはいられない。
lines.english: He could not stop thinking about the grave matter Sayaka had confided in him.

lines.japanese:
迷路のように錯綜した会話だが、つまるところ、
彼女はこう言っていたのだ。
lines.english: The conversation wound through a maze, but in the end, this was what she had said:

lines.japanese: 自分を支配して欲しい、と。
lines.english: She wanted him to control her.

lines.japanese:
自由意志もいらない。
　自我もいらない。
lines.english: No free will. No self.

lines.japanese:
ただ相手の意に添うだけの機械を友とすることが、
果たして正常であるのかどうか。
　まがりなりにも今の沙也加は個人である。
lines.english: Could it possibly be normal to call a machine a friend when all it did was submit to another person's will? Whatever else might be said, Sayaka as she was now was still an individual.

lines.japanese:
その資質をもスポイルすることになる。
　喪失ということだ。
　その意味では、忍は沙也加を放し飼いにしている。
lines.english: It would destroy even her individuality. It would be a loss. In that sense, Shinobu was letting Sayaka roam free.

lines.japanese: 語弊はあるかも知れないが、そう言うのが最も近い。
lines.english: The expression might give the wrong impression, but it was the closest fit.

lines.japanese:
放し飼いにされれば、沙也加は自分を見つめるこ
とになる。個人として。
lines.english: Left to run free, Sayaka was forced to confront herself as an individual.

lines.japanese:
となれば、自分と外部との差異を嫌でも自覚する
ことになる。
lines.english: That, in turn, would force her to recognize the difference between herself and the world outside.

lines.japanese:
この論理が感情のように極まった時、沙也加は忍
に反目するかも知れない。
lines.english: If that logic ever became as absolute as an emotion, Sayaka might turn against Shinobu.

lines.japanese: つまり、離れるということだ。
lines.english: In other words, she might leave him.

lines.japanese: （それは、嫌だ）
lines.english: (I don't want that.)

lines.japanese:
では一緒にいるとする。
　沙也加の望む形とは、つまりは隷属だ。
lines.english: Suppose, then, that they stayed together. The form Sayaka desired was, in a word, servitude.

lines.japanese:
亭主関白、というと簡単に過ぎるが、似たような
ものだ。
lines.english: A domineering husband was too simple a comparison, but it was something like that.

lines.japanese:
一個人ではなく、忍の従属物になってしまえば楽
である。
lines.english: It would be easier for her to cease being an individual and become something that belonged to Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
そうでなければ不安定な自分はいつか弾けてしま
う。怖い。
lines.english: Otherwise, her unstable self would one day burst apart. She was afraid.

lines.japanese: これが、沙也加の主張の概要となる。
lines.english: That, in outline, was Sayaka's argument.

lines.japanese:
どちらが良いのか？
　どちらも否定できるのか？
lines.english: Which is better? Can both be rejected?

lines.japanese:
理想的な回答としては、二人とも別個の人間とし
て互いを尊重し様々な問題を愛と理性の力で乗り越
えて幸せになりました……というものだろう。
lines.english: The ideal answer would presumably be that they respected each other as separate individuals, overcame their various difficulties through the power of love and reason, and lived happily ever after…

lines.japanese:
理想の是非は置くとしても、全ての状況にこの考
え方を強要するのが、現在の倫理であることは……
忍にもわかる。
lines.english: Whatever one thought of the ideal itself, Shinobu understood that modern ethics demanded that answer be imposed on every situation, without exception.

lines.japanese:
だが一個人のできることには限界がある。
　こと、気持ちの問題となればさらに傾向は加速する。
lines.english: But one person could do only so much. When the matter was one of feelings, that limitation grew more acute.

lines.japanese:
本当に理性を持つのであれば、平均的な倫理から
外れた問題については、より客観的な思考が必要と
なるはずだ。
lines.english: Anyone truly possessed of reason would have to think more objectively when confronting a problem that falls outside ordinary ethics.

lines.japanese:
その意味で、倫理に対する信仰を、忍は必要とは
しない。
lines.english: In that sense, Shinobu had no need to put his faith in ethics.

lines.japanese:
真に理想を標榜するのであれば、想い届かず辛辣
な現実に晒され破滅が訪れた時に、それを受け入れ
るだけの……ある種の諦念が必要となるはずだ。
lines.english: To profess an ideal sincerely, one must possess a certain kind of resignation… enough to accept the ruin that comes when one's feelings go unanswered and one is exposed to the cruelty of reality.

lines.japanese: 破滅に際し自らを顧みるだけの度量を要する。
lines.english: It would also require the fortitude to examine oneself in the midst of ruin.

lines.japanese:
だがそんな領域に立った人間が、どれほどいるだ
ろうか？
lines.english: But how many people have ever reached such a place?

lines.japanese:
大半が、自己憐憫か責任転嫁という恥ずべき思考
に身を委ねることになるのだ。
lines.english: Most people surrender to the shameful habits of self-pity or shifting blame.

lines.japanese: 忍はどちらも苦手だ。
lines.english: Shinobu had little patience for either.

lines.japanese:
可哀相な自分を愛でることが恥ずかしい。
　自分の不幸の責任を誰かになすりつけてもどうに
もならない。
lines.english: To cherish his own poor, pitiful self struck him as shameful. And pinning the blame for his unhappiness on someone else would solve nothing.

lines.japanese: 嫌いだというのに、周囲は悩み事で満ちている。
lines.english: He hated both, yet the world around him was full of troubles.

lines.japanese:
悩みは良くない。
　自己憐憫への直結コースだからだ。
lines.english: Brooding was no good. It led straight to self-pity.

lines.japanese: （……どーしよ……）
lines.english: (…What am I gonna do…?)

lines.japanese:
こんな時、章二だったらどうするのだろう？
　足を止め、工場へ至る道程を目でなぞった。
　今日は誰か来ているだろうか？
lines.english: What would Shouji do at a time like this? Shinobu stopped and traced the road to the factory with his eyes. Would anyone be there today?

lines.japanese:
くすぶった空間では、楽しく歓談が行われている
のだろうか？
lines.english: Would they be enjoying some lively conversation in that smoldering space?

lines.japanese: だが……今日は行けない。
lines.english: But… he could not go today.

lines.japanese:
無人だった場合うちひしがれた自分が予想できた
し、賑やかであればなおさら思考停止に陥りそうだ。
lines.english: If the place were empty, he could picture himself devastated; if it were lively, he would be all the more likely to stop thinking.

lines.japanese: （章二、いるのかな）
lines.english: (I wonder if Shouji's there.)

lines.japanese:
ふと気になった。
　こんな憂鬱な夕刻だったからだ。
lines.english: It occurred to him suddenly. Because it was such a melancholy evening.

lines.japanese:
忍は小屋の外で、しゃがみ込んでいた。
　時刻は夕暮れ。
　いよいよ校門が閉じられる時間も近い。
lines.english: Shinobu crouches outside the hutch. It is dusk. The hour when the school gates close is fast approaching.

lines.japanese:
見渡しても校庭には人はおらず、遊ぶ声も聞こえ
ない。
lines.english: Looking around, he sees no one in the schoolyard and hears no sound of children playing.

lines.japanese:
どこかから、帰宅を促す市営放送が聞こえてきて、
忍は薄い憂鬱にとらわれた。
lines.english: A municipal announcement urging children home drifts in from somewhere, and a faint melancholy takes hold of Shinobu.

lines.japanese: しかし帰るわけにはいかない。
lines.english: But he cannot leave.

lines.japanese:
フェンスごしに、ブチとマルが無警戒に、危機意
識の欠片も抱かず過ごす様子を咎めるように見つめ
ている。
lines.english: Through the fence, he watches Spot and Roly as though reproaching them for passing the time entirely off guard and without the slightest awareness of danger.

lines.japanese:
世の中に、これほど無害な生き物もいないだろう
と思う。
lines.english: Surely there can be no creature in the world so harmless.

lines.japanese: 実際その通りで、兎は生命としては極端に弱い。
lines.english: And indeed, rabbits are extraordinarily frail creatures.

lines.japanese:
こうして飼育していてわかったことだが、同種の
兎同士であっても、同じ小屋にいると互いをストレ
スに感じることがあるのだと言う。
lines.english: He has learned from caring for them that even rabbits of the same species may find sharing a hutch stressful, or so they say.

lines.japanese:
また雌雄であるならば、唯一の武器とも言うべき
繁殖力で猛然と増えてしまい、破綻を来すのだとも。
lines.english: He is also told that if male and female are kept together, they will breed at a furious rate, wielding what might be called their sole weapon—fertility—until the whole arrangement collapses.

lines.japanese:
幸い、二羽はメスで、仲も良い（のかどうかは不
明だが喧嘩はしない）。
lines.english: Fortunately, both are female, and they get along (or at least they do not fight; whether that counts is unclear).

lines.japanese: 健康状態も良好。
lines.english: They are in excellent health as well.

lines.japanese:
飼育に必要な一日の作業も終わり、今は餌箱にも
新鮮なペレットが盛られている。
lines.english: The day's necessary work is finished, and their feeder is now heaped with fresh pellets.

lines.japanese:
兎小屋には施錠されており、悪意ある来訪者によ
って害されないよう最低限の備えが施されている。
lines.english: The hutch is locked, providing at least the minimum protection against anyone who means them harm.

lines.japanese:
しかしなお、忍は疑惑を抱いていた。
　厳密な栄養管理であるはずの飼育方針であるにも
関わらず、なぜこうも軟便が多いのだろうか、と。
lines.english: And yet Shinobu has his suspicions. If their diet is so strictly regulated, why are there so many soft droppings?

lines.japanese: 軟便そして食糞は兎にとって、必要な行為ではある。
lines.english: Soft feces and coprophagy are necessary parts of a rabbit's life.

lines.japanese:
だが無論のこと、軽い体調不良による腹下しとい
うものも別個に存在する。
　いわゆる兎の悪臭の主原因は、これである。
lines.english: But naturally, diarrhea caused by mild illness is a separate phenomenon. That is the main source of the smell commonly associated with rabbits.

lines.japanese:
忍は道路側に座り込み、校庭からの死角に身を置
いて、じっと最終下校時刻を待っていた。
lines.english: Shinobu sits on the roadside, hidden from the schoolyard, and waits intently for final dismissal.

lines.japanese:
と―――
　一人の怪しい人物が、ちょうど校庭の向こうから
堂々と歩いてくるではないか。
lines.english: Then— a suspicious figure comes striding boldly toward him from across the schoolyard.

lines.japanese: とびかかるつもりもないのだが、つい忍は身構えた。
lines.english: He has no intention of pouncing, yet Shinobu instinctively braces himself.

lines.japanese: 子供だった。
lines.english: A child.

lines.japanese:
見た顔である。同じ学校、同学年。
　鋭い目つきをしている。
lines.english: A face he recognizes. Same school, same grade. The boy's eyes are sharp.

lines.japanese:
口元がニヒルに吊り上がっている。
　何者にも怖じず、媚びないという意志が、面差し
に透けて見えた。
lines.english: His lips curl into a cynical sneer. His features reveal a will that fears nothing and curries favor with no one.

lines.japanese: 悪の顔である。
lines.english: The very face of evil.

lines.japanese: （……まさか、あいつが？）
lines.english: (…Could he be the one?)

lines.japanese: 少年は肩を怒らせ、一直線に小屋に接近してきた。
lines.english: The boy squares his shoulders and advances straight toward the hutch.

lines.japanese:
悪そうな少年は、手にしていた不道徳そのものを示
すかのような黒いビニール袋から、悪辣極まりない
仕草でソレを取り出し、口元を悪鬼のように歪めた。
lines.english: The sinister boy reaches into his black plastic bag—the very embodiment of immorality—and, with a gesture of consummate villainy, draws forth the object, his mouth twisting like a demon's.

lines.japanese: 「ククク……お楽しみのはじまりだぜ」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh… Let the fun begin.”

lines.japanese:
その手に握られたものが何かは忍の側からは見え
ない。
lines.english: From Shinobu’s position, he cannot see what the boy is holding.

lines.japanese:
おそらくは、ペンチか錐などの悪質な器具に違い
ない。
lines.english: Surely it must be some vicious implement, a pair of pliers or an awl.

lines.japanese:
あるいは兎を恐怖させるための花火や爆竹かも知
れない。兎は爆竹のショックで死ぬこともある。
lines.english: Or perhaps fireworks or firecrackers meant to terrify the rabbits. A rabbit can die from the shock of an exploding firecracker.

lines.japanese:
見過ごすことはできない。
　相手はかなり悪そうだが、飼育委員として、行動
しなければならない。
lines.english: He cannot stand by and watch. The boy looks profoundly evil, but as a member of the animal-care committee, Shinobu has to act.

lines.japanese: 立ち上がり、側面にまわって少年の手元を確かめた。
lines.english: He rises and circles to the side to see what is in the boy's hand.

lines.japanese:
「どうした？　オレが恐ろしいか？　他ではそうそ
　う見られない、大ぶりのこいつが怖いか？
　クク、ハハハ！」
lines.english: “What's wrong? Frightened of me? Scared of this enormous specimen you won't see just anywhere? Heh. Hahahaha!”

lines.japanese:
夕映えに輝く血のような色のそれは……切り立っ
た峰のように鋭い、人参だった。
lines.english: The blood-red object blazing in the sunset is… a carrot, sharp as a sheer mountain peak.

lines.japanese:
「バカな奴らだ。てめぇの好物も、おキレイにカット
　されなきゃわからないらしい」
lines.english: “Stupid beasts. You don't even recognize your favorite food unless someone slices it up all pretty for you.”

lines.japanese: 「ならこいつはどうだ」
lines.english: “Then how about this?”

lines.japanese: また新たな得物を取り出す。
lines.english: He draws another weapon.

lines.japanese:
遠目には無骨な岩石にしか見えないそれは……大
きなジャガイモだ。
lines.english: From a distance it resembles nothing so much as a rugged boulder… but it is a large potato.

lines.japanese: 「見ろよ、頭をカチ割ることもできそうだ……」
lines.english: “Look at it. You could split a skull with this thing…”

lines.japanese: 少年はうっとりとした。
lines.english: The boy gazes at it in rapture.

lines.japanese:
「どうした、こいつが欲しいのか？　おまえらはも
　う、こいつなしじゃ生きては行けない体だ」
lines.english: “What's wrong? You want it? Your bodies can't survive without this stuff anymore.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなカリカリの食い物だけじゃ、おまえらは満
　足できない。そうだな？」
lines.english: “That dry, crunchy slop can't satisfy you now. Can it?”

lines.japanese:
「欲しいか、ならいつものように態度で示すんだな。
　足下に来い、尻尾を振ってオレ様に媚びてみろ！
　さあ！」
lines.english: “You want it? Then show me, like you always do. Come to my feet. Wag your tails and fawn over yours truly! Come on!”

lines.japanese: いろいろな意味で、見ていることはできなくなった。
lines.english: For any number of reasons, Shinobu can watch no longer.
“You—”

lines.japanese:
触れてもいないのに、少年はひっくり返った。
　そして凝然と忍を見上げた。
lines.english: Though Shinobu never even touches him, the boy topples backward. He stares up at Shinobu, frozen.
“You… Who are you?”

lines.japanese: これが、樋口章二との出会いであった。
lines.english: This was Shinobu's first encounter with Shouji Higuchi.

lines.japanese:
金曜日。
　休日である。
lines.english: Friday. A day off.

lines.japanese: 「……うーむ」
lines.english: “…Hmm.”

lines.japanese:
あまり眠れなかった。
　沙也加と試しにデートをすることになった。
　墓参りにつきあったためである。
lines.english: He had hardly slept. Today, he and Sayaka were going on a trial date. It had come about after he went with her to visit a grave.

lines.japanese:
幸か不幸か、まだわからない。
　微妙なところである。
lines.english: Whether that was good or bad, he still could not say. It was hard to call.

lines.japanese:
嬉しいことは嬉しいのだが……それとスムーズに
対応できるか否かは別問題である。
lines.english: He was happy, certainly… Whether he could carry it off gracefully was another matter.

lines.japanese:
相手を幻滅させてしまっては、かえってつらいこ
とになる。
lines.english: Letting her down would only make things worse.

lines.japanese: そして忍に、その手の経験は乏しい。
lines.english: And Shinobu had next to no experience with this sort of thing.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたものか」
lines.english: “What do I do?”

lines.japanese: 「ご相談が」
lines.english: “I was hoping for some advice.”

lines.japanese: 「私に？」
lines.english: “From me?”

lines.japanese:
休日の朝っぱらから、瓶の中にピンセットで帆船
を組み立てていた千鳥が、顔を上げた。
　寝癖のついた忍に、困惑の視線を向ける。
lines.english: It was first thing on a holiday morning, and Chidori had been building a ship in a bottle with tweezers. She looked up and regarded Shinobu's bed hair with a puzzled expression.

lines.japanese: 「うかがいましょう」
lines.english: “I'm listening.”

lines.japanese:
千鳥はピンセットを置いて、膝を閉じた。
　進水式にほど遠い亡国ブランデンブルグの三層甲
板艦が、物寂しく捨て置かれた。
lines.english: Chidori put down the tweezers and pressed her knees together. A three-decker from the vanished state of Brandenburg, still nowhere near ready to launch, sat forlornly abandoned.

lines.japanese: 「あのですね」
lines.english: “Well, you see…”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese:
「デートをすることになりまして、その、本堂沙也加
　とです」
lines.english: “I'm going on a date. With, um… Sayaka Hondou.”
“…Only now?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「互いに信頼関係を結んでいるあなたがたのこと」
lines.english: “Given the trust you two already share…”

lines.japanese: 「……勝負デートですね？」
lines.english: “…So this is the make-or-break date?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 人生の大事といった調子で、忍は頷いた。
lines.english: Shinobu nodded as solemnly as if his whole life hung on it.

lines.japanese: 「いつです？」
lines.english: “When?”

lines.japanese: 「今日です」
lines.english: “Today.”

lines.japanese: 千鳥はかぶりを振る。
lines.english: Chidori shook her head.

lines.japanese:
「なぜ今日になって
　言うんですか！」
lines.english: “Why are you only telling me today!”

lines.japanese:
「昨日、誘えと
　誘われたからです！」
lines.english: “Because yesterday she invited me to ask her out!”

lines.japanese:
「誘えと誘われ？　……とにかく何かできるような
　時間はないでしょう」
lines.english: “She invited you to invite her? …At any rate, there is hardly time to do anything now.”

lines.japanese: 「そこを何とか」
lines.english: “Please. Anything you can do.”

lines.japanese: 「ご経験から、なんとか」

その意味で完全にモデルのポテンシャルを生かした

lines.english: “Oh, how about this place?”

lines.japanese:
古着屋の前で立ち止まる。
　このショップは若者に定評があるという、話だ。
lines.english: He stopped outside a secondhand clothing store said to have a good reputation among young people.

lines.japanese: しかし、沙也加は眉をあつめた。
lines.english: But Sayaka knitted her brows.
“…Secondhand clothes?”

lines.japanese: 「好きなのプレゼントしようかな、と思って」
lines.english: “I thought I'd buy you something you liked.”

lines.japanese: 引かせてしまった。
lines.english: That had put her off.
“…H-Huh!?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、忍」
lines.english: “Um, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 大変申し訳なさそうに言う。
lines.english: She sounded terribly apologetic.

lines.japanese:
「どうせだったら、新品にしてもらった方が、嬉し
　いわね……」
lines.english: “If you're buying me something, I think… I would rather it were new.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんと……でも章二が言うには」
lines.english: “Wh-What… But Shouji said—”

lines.japanese: 「野の獣が、なんと言ったの？」
lines.english: “And what did that wild beast have to say?”

lines.japanese:
「……いえ、くだらぬことを少々吠えておりました
　が……」
lines.english: “…Nothing. He merely barked a little nonsense, that's all…”

lines.japanese:
「それに中古品というのであれば、もっと良い店が
　あるわよ」
lines.english: “If it's secondhand goods you want, I know a much better shop.”

lines.japanese: 「このあたりに？」
lines.english: “Around here?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、こっち」
lines.english: “Yes. This way.”

lines.japanese: と、今度は沙也加から手を取り、引いていく。
lines.english: This time, it was Sayaka who took his hand and pulled him along.

lines.japanese: （ドキドキ・リターンズ……）
lines.english: (The Return of the Heart-Pounding…)

lines.japanese: ちょっぴり幸せ。
lines.english: A tiny bit of happiness.

lines.japanese: 「アンティークショップ？」
lines.english: “An antique shop?”

lines.japanese: 「遠縁の者が経営しているの」
lines.english: “A distant relative runs it.”

lines.japanese:
「……この商店街って、全員本堂一族の関係者だっ
　たりする？」
lines.english: “…Don't tell me everyone in this shopping arcade is tied to the Hondou clan?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか」
lines.english: “Don't be ridiculous.”

lines.japanese: 「プレゼントしてくれるの？」
lines.english: “Will you buy me a present?”

lines.japanese: 悪戯っぽく微笑む。
lines.english: She smiled mischievously.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そんな高くないものなら……」
lines.english: “I-If it isn't too expensive…”

lines.japanese: 「見ましょう」
lines.english: “Let's look around.”

lines.japanese:
店内に入った途端、柔らかく落ち着いた光量に、
しばし視野が曇った。
lines.english: The moment they stepped inside, his vision dimmed briefly in the soft, subdued light.

lines.japanese:
だが慣れてみると、独特の趣がじんわりと染みて
きた。
lines.english: Once his eyes adjusted, however, the shop's distinctive charm slowly made itself felt.

lines.japanese: 西洋骨董、主に英国のそれを取り扱った店のようだ。
lines.english: It seemed to specialize in Western antiques, British pieces in particular.

lines.japanese:
ゆったりと流れる楽曲が、耳に心地よく、また雰
囲気に合っている。
　時間がゆるく感じられた。
lines.english: Unhurried music flowed through the shop, easy on the ear and perfectly suited to the mood. Time itself seemed to slacken.

lines.japanese: 沙也加が唇に指を添えた。
lines.english: Sayaka laid a finger to her lips.

lines.japanese: 「……店内では、静かにね」
lines.english: “…We should keep our voices down in here.”

lines.japanese:
頷く。
　この店の空気は、貴石のように価値を付されてい
るのだ。
lines.english: He nodded. The atmosphere of that shop was prized as carefully as any gemstone.

lines.japanese:
二人は結びついたまま、お世辞にも広くはないが
完成された店内を踏みしめていく。
lines.english: Still hand in hand, they walked through a shop that was by no means large but felt complete down to the last detail.

lines.japanese:
奥のガラスケースには、いかにも高額な骨董品が並
んでいるようだが、軒先に近いあたりは庶民にも買い
求められる範囲内の小さなアイテムが並んでいた。
lines.english: Expensive-looking antiques filled the glass cases at the back, while the front displayed smaller pieces an ordinary customer might still afford.

lines.japanese: 「沙也加」
lines.english: “Sayaka.”

lines.japanese: 「こんにちは」
lines.english: “Good afternoon.”

lines.japanese:
黒いタートルネックとジーンズが似合う、妙齢の
女性に、沙也加と忍は深々と頭を下げた。
lines.english: Sayaka and Shinobu bowed deeply to an attractive woman in a black turtleneck and jeans.

lines.japanese:
年の頃は三十代前半といったところだろうか。
　てっきり老女が出てくるとばかり思っていた忍は、
少し戸惑った。
lines.english: She appeared to be in her early thirties. Shinobu had been expecting another old woman, and the sight threw him slightly.

lines.japanese:
だが確かに顔立ちには、沙也加と同じ血が現れて
いる。
lines.english: But the family resemblance to Sayaka was unmistakable.

lines.japanese: 「いらっしゃいませ」
lines.english: “Welcome.”

lines.japanese: 女性は微笑んで、忍にも丁寧に礼をした。
lines.english: The woman smiled and bowed politely to Shinobu as well.
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: ぎこちなく、再度頭を下げる。
lines.english: He returned the bow awkwardly.

lines.japanese:
「このあいだ頼まれていたもの、向こうの業者から
　送られてきたわ。見てくださる？」
lines.english: “The item you asked me about the other day came in from the dealer. Would you like to have a look?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「悪いけど、少しここで見ていて」
lines.english: “Sorry, but could you browse around here for a minute?”

lines.japanese: 二人は店の奥に消えた。
lines.english: The two women disappeared into the back.

lines.japanese: 忍は取り残された。
lines.english: Shinobu was left behind.

lines.japanese: （見ていろって言われてもなぁ……）
lines.english: (Browse around, she says…)

lines.japanese: やるかたなく、小物を一つ持ち上げてみた。
lines.english: With nothing else to do, he tried picking up a trinket.

lines.japanese:
羽ばたく鷹のヴィエンナブロンズ。
『１８９０年頃／￥２１０００』というタグが
ぶらさがる。
lines.english: A Vienna bronze of a hawk in flight. A tag reading ‘c. 1890 / ¥21,000’ dangled from it.

lines.japanese: （……いやーん）
lines.english: (…Nooo.)

lines.japanese:
高い。
　小物でも結構高い。
lines.english: Expensive. Even the trinkets were expensive.

lines.japanese:
万里の長城を輪にした格調高いペントレー。
『１９００年頃／￥４５０００』
lines.english: An elegant pen tray in the shape of the Great Wall, curled into a ring. ‘c. 1900 / ¥45,000.’

lines.japanese: （……きゃいーん）
lines.english: (…Yipe.)

lines.japanese:
Ａ資金の限界さえも越えていた。
　事ここに至り、忍はいよいよ焦燥にとらわれはじ
めた。
lines.english: Even that was beyond the limits of the A Fund. By now, Shinobu was beginning to panic in earnest.

lines.japanese: （見付けないと……）
lines.english: (I have to find something…)

lines.japanese:
所持金で買い求められるものを。
　太い鼻息を落とすと、店内を走査することに専心
する。
lines.english: Something he could afford with the money in his pocket. He let out a mighty snort and turned his full attention to scanning the shop.

lines.japanese:
チェーンルーペ。
『１９２０年前後／￥２８０００』
lines.english: A loupe on a chain. ‘c. 1920 / ¥28,000.’

lines.japanese:
象牙の単眼鏡。
『１９０３年／クルックス家／￥７２０００』
lines.english: An ivory monocular. ‘1903 / Crookes family / ¥72,000.’

lines.japanese:
アールヌーボーの花器。
『￥１８００００』
lines.english: An Art Nouveau vase. ‘¥180,000.’

lines.japanese: 目利きが悪いのか、次第に高くなっていく。
lines.english: Either he had a terrible eye for bargains, or the prices were steadily rising.

lines.japanese: （そうだ、ペーパーナイフなら！）
lines.english: (Of course! A letter opener!)

lines.japanese:
銀製ペーパーナイフ。
『１９１０年頃／￥２２０００』
lines.english: A silver letter opener. ‘c. 1910 / ¥22,000.’

lines.japanese: やるせない。
lines.english: Hopeless.

lines.japanese: 「なら……この小皿はどうだ……」
lines.english: “Then… what about this little dish…?”
A little dish. ‘c. 1930 / ¥20,010.’

lines.japanese: （馬鹿なッ！！）
lines.english: (No way!!)

lines.japanese: これだけ端数１０円が存在する。明らかにおかしい。
lines.english: Only this one had an odd ten yen tacked on. Plainly suspicious.
(…A trap?)

lines.japanese:
荒唐無稽な想像に身をよじっていると、沙也加が
包みを抱えて戻ってきた。
lines.english: While he twisted himself into knots over this absurd notion, Sayaka returned carrying a parcel.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせ」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you.”
“…Oh, Sayaka…”

lines.japanese: 「何か欲しいものはあった？」
lines.english: “Did you find anything you wanted?”

lines.japanese:
首を振る。あるわけがない。
　どう切り抜けようか考え出した時、
lines.english: He shook his head. Of course he hadn't. He had just begun wondering how to get out of this when—

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ行きましょう」
lines.english: “Then let's go.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese:
「頼んでいたものも受け取れたし、私はもう出よう
　と思うのだけれど」
lines.english: “I got what I came for, so I'm ready to go.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん……出ようか」
lines.english: “Oh. Right… Let's go.”

lines.japanese:
無力だった。
　情けない男……いわゆるナサ男だった。
lines.english: He was powerless. A pathetic excuse for a man—a patheti-man, if you will.

lines.japanese: 「また来て頂戴」
lines.english: “Come again.”

lines.japanese: 見送られて、店を出る。
lines.english: The proprietor saw them out, and they left the shop.

lines.japanese:
きっと察してくれた、というか、察知されたのだ
ろう。
lines.english: She had probably understood—or rather, figured him out.

lines.japanese: 気を遣われたに違いなかった。
lines.english: No doubt she had gone out of her way to spare his feelings.

lines.japanese: 長い時間が過ぎていることにさえ気付かなかった。
lines.english: He had not even noticed how much time had passed.

lines.japanese: 「……ごめん」
lines.english: “…Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いいのよ」
lines.english: “It's all right.”

lines.japanese: 「高いもの、あのお店は」
lines.english: “Everything in that shop is expensive.”

lines.japanese: 「驚いた……」
lines.english: “I was shocked…”

lines.japanese: 「それは？」
lines.english: “What's in the parcel?”

lines.japanese: 「これは祖母の注文」
lines.english: “This was my grandmother's order.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: 安堵した。
lines.english: He breathed a sigh of relief.

lines.japanese: 「しかし、沙也加は愛されてるね」
lines.english: “You're certainly loved, Sayaka.”

lines.japanese: 「そうね、そう見えるかも知れないわね」
lines.english: “Yes. I suppose it might look that way.”

lines.japanese: 「違うの？」
lines.english: “Isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「愛されているわよ」
lines.english: “I am.”

lines.japanese: 「でもそれは、あなたがいてのことでしょうに」
lines.english: “But that's only because I have you, isn't it?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「今の私を望んだのは、忍よ」
lines.english: “You were the one who wanted me as I am now, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 湖めいた瞳が、忍を映した。
lines.english: Her lake-like eyes held Shinobu's reflection.

lines.japanese: 「……そうだった、かな」
lines.english: “…Was I?”

lines.japanese:
しばしの無言が、二人の間に挟まれた。
　こうなると周辺の話し声さえことさらに煩わしい。
lines.english: A silence settled between them. It made even the surrounding chatter especially grating.

lines.japanese:
少女の手をひっ掴む。
　力をこめて握りしめた。独占するように。
lines.english: He snatched the girl's hand. He squeezed it hard, as though to claim her for himself.
“…Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「でも……本当に僕だけが望んだ君なの？」
lines.english: “But… was I really the only one who wanted you to be this way?”

lines.japanese: 目をそらされることが、今の忍にはつらい。
lines.english: Right now, even her looking away was painful for Shinobu.
“Saya—!”

lines.japanese:
掴んだ手ごと、引き寄せる。
　よろめく少女は、驚くほど軽かった。
　目と鼻の先に傾く小顔。
lines.english: Still clutching her hand, he pulled her toward him. The girl stumbled, astonishingly light. Her small face tilted up inches from his own.

lines.japanese:
強い言葉を浴びせようとしたところで、乱暴な行
いと自覚できた。
lines.english: He was on the verge of hurling harsh words at her when he realized how rough he had been.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 手を離す。
lines.english: He let go.

lines.japanese:
張りつめたものが抜けていくのが傍目にもわかる。
　紛れもなくそれは、忍の感情だ。
lines.english: The tension visibly drained out of him. Those feelings were unmistakably Shinobu's own.

lines.japanese: 「……さっきのお店、戻ろう」
lines.english: “…Let's go back to that shop.”

lines.japanese: 「どうして？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
「何かプレゼントするって言ったし……その、もっ
　と探せば、買えるものも―――」
lines.english: “I said I'd buy you something… and if we look harder, there might be something I can afford—”

lines.japanese: 「いいのよ、それは」
lines.english: “You don't have to.”

lines.japanese: 「でも」
lines.english: “But—”

lines.japanese:
「忍には、とても素晴らしいものを、もうもらっ
　てる」
lines.english: “You've already given me something truly wonderful.”

lines.japanese: 「かけがえのないもの、尊いものを」
lines.english: “Something irreplaceable. Something precious.”

lines.japanese: 「でも私は……そのことで……」
lines.english: “But I… because of that…”

lines.japanese:
日が暮れるように表情が暗くなった。
　忍は問いつめることができない。
　漠然としていて、遠かった。
lines.english: Her expression darkened as though night were falling. Shinobu could not bring himself to press her. Whatever it was, it felt vague and far away.

lines.japanese: （ここにも、黄昏がある）
lines.english: (There was twilight here too.)

lines.japanese:
それはどこにでもあった。
　空はいつだって黄昏で満ちていたし、それは忍が
生まれた日からしてすでにそうだった。
lines.english: It was everywhere. The sky had always been full of twilight. It had been that way from the day Shinobu was born.

lines.japanese:
誕生と同時に終焉を知らされることは、いかなる
悲劇にも勝るあきらめを植えつける。
lines.english: To be told of the end at the moment of birth plants a resignation deeper than any tragedy.

lines.japanese: 虚無の花に育つ。
lines.english: That resignation grew into a flower of nothingness.

lines.japanese:
８０億人類の栽培した虚無の花畑が、今だ。
　輝かしかった未来展望はどこに行ったのだろう？
lines.english: The present is a field of flowers of nothingness cultivated by eight billion human beings. Where did that radiant vision of the future go?

lines.japanese:
空想はいつから奪われてしまったのだろう？
　このことを考えると、忍は狂いそうになる。
　ノイローゼに近い。
lines.english: When had imagination been taken away? Thinking about it drove Shinobu nearly mad. It bordered on neurosis.

lines.japanese:
自覚もある。
　だが制御がうまくない。
lines.english: He knew it too. But he could not control it well.

lines.japanese:
機械的に対処するしかないと知りつつ、そうすれ
ば今のわずかばかりの情感も失われる。
lines.english: He knew his only choice was to deal with it mechanically, but doing so would cost him what little feeling he had left.

lines.japanese:
胸に手を当てた。
　甘酸っぱい何かが、そこにあると信じた。
lines.english: He pressed a hand to his chest. He believed that something sweet and sour lived there.

lines.japanese: 信じた。
lines.english: He believed.

lines.japanese: 「僕はみんなが好きだ」
lines.english: “I love them all.”

lines.japanese: 「あずさも章二も、笛子も、兄妹も」
lines.english: “Azusa and Shouji, Fueko, the siblings.”

lines.japanese: 「……君が好きだ」
lines.english: “…I love you.”

lines.japanese:
足が止まる。
　見つめ合う。
　時間が経つ。
lines.english: They stopped. They looked at one another. Time passed.

lines.japanese: 過ぎゆく人々が、なぜか視線一つ向けない。
lines.english: For some reason, not one passerby so much as glanced at them.

lines.japanese: （個室のように）
lines.english: (Like a room to ourselves.)

lines.japanese:
認識の輪郭が溶けて、誰の心にも当たり前のもの
になる。
lines.english: The contours of recognition melted away, until their presence seemed perfectly ordinary to every mind.

lines.japanese:
その模糊とした情報群から、自分と少女について
の認識だけを、当事者だけにわかるように抽出すれ
ばもう架空の個室ができあがる。
lines.english: From that hazy mass of information, all he had to do was isolate the awareness of himself and the girl in a form only they could comprehend, and the imaginary private room was complete.

lines.japanese:
緋色に呪われながら、二人は軽く唇を接触させた。
　彼女は笑う。
lines.english: Cursed by the scarlet light, their lips brushed. She smiled.

lines.japanese: 「帰りましょう」
lines.english: “Let's go home.”

lines.japanese:
昔はあれほど欲しかった笑顔を、向けられている。
　なお、今では物足りなさを感じてしまう。
　まだ忍は帰りたくはなかった。
lines.english: She gave him the smile he had once wanted so desperately. Yet now it left him wanting. Shinobu did not want to go home yet.

lines.japanese: 「それとも……どこか行きたいところでもある？」
lines.english: “Or… is there somewhere you'd like to go?”

lines.japanese: 少し考えて忍は告げた。
lines.english: Shinobu thought for a moment before answering.

lines.japanese:
茜色にのっぺりと染められた校庭に、手を繋いで
立つ二人の影法師が狂ったオブジェのように伸びて
いる。
lines.english: Across the schoolyard, painted flat in madder red, the shadows of the two figures standing hand in hand stretched away like some mad sculpture.

lines.japanese:
休日であるためか、校庭には誰もいない。
　街並みも遠く眩しさに掻き消える。
lines.english: Perhaps because it was a holiday, the schoolyard was deserted. Even the cityscape dissolved in the distant glare.

lines.japanese:
忍と沙也加は、行き場を失った幼いつがいとなっ
て当惑し、虚ろな小屋を眺める。
lines.english: Shinobu and Sayaka, a bewildered pair of young creatures with nowhere left to go, stood before the hollow hutch.

lines.japanese: からっぽだった。
lines.english: It was empty.

lines.japanese: 「もう、飼ってないんだね」
lines.english: “They don't keep them anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese:
何年も生き物が棲まない空白はそらぞらしく乾い
ていた。
lines.english: The hollow left by years without a living thing inside was dry and unreal.

lines.japanese: 「でも知っていたんじゃない？　母校のことだもの」
lines.english: “But you knew that, didn't you? This is your old school.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ」
lines.english: “More or less.”

lines.japanese: 「なぜここに？」
lines.english: “Then why come here?”

lines.japanese: 忍は言葉を吟味するように、ゆっくりと口を開いた。
lines.english: Shinobu opened his mouth slowly, as though testing every word.

lines.japanese:
「ブチとマルが、彼女らが、君にとってどういう意味
　だったのか……僕にはわからない」
lines.english: “Spot and Roly—what they meant to you… I don't know.”

lines.japanese:
「それでも大切だったことは間違いない。そうだよ
　ね？」
lines.english: “But I know they mattered to you. They did, didn't they?”
“Yes…”

lines.japanese:
「それが、ブチとマルでなければならなかった理由っ
　てのは、」
lines.english: “But the reason it had to be Spot and Roly— that was—”

lines.japanese: 「やめて」
lines.english: “Stop.”

lines.japanese:
硬質な声も久方ぶりだ。
　だがこの硬さは、怯えに満ちている。
lines.english: It had been a long time since he had heard that hard voice. But there was fear in its hardness.

lines.japanese: 「……僕も今は、よくわかる」
lines.english: “…Now I understand it too.”

lines.japanese:
隣に立つ少女の髪を片手で梳く。
　上から下に。
　何度も繰り返す。

姉の千鳥が、両親のいない忍の寂しさを紛らわす
ために、水槽を与えた。
lines.english: His older sister Chidori gave him an aquarium to ease the loneliness of having no parents around.

lines.japanese:
中学年を越えた者には少し幼稚な娯楽だが、忍は
カラッポの水槽を箱庭に仕立てることに夢中になった。
lines.english: It was a slightly childish pastime for an upper elementary schooler, but Shinobu became absorbed in turning the empty tank into a miniature world.

lines.japanese:
砂を敷き、流木を置き、濾過器をつけ、水を張り、
水草を植えた。
　箱庭には住人が欠けていた。
lines.english: He spread sand, set down driftwood, attached a filter, filled the tank, and planted waterweed. The miniature world lacked inhabitants.

lines.japanese:
予算がそこで尽きたため、ショップで生物を買い
求めることはできなかったのだ。
　そこで忍は川に出かけた。
lines.english: His budget was exhausted, so he could not buy any living creatures from a shop. Instead, Shinobu went to the river.

lines.japanese:
田んぼを回った。
　あるいはタガメやミズカマキリといったものを期
待していたのかも知れない。
lines.english: He made the rounds of the rice paddies. Perhaps he hoped to find a giant water bug or a water scorpion or something of the sort.

lines.japanese:
大変にレアな生物だが、見合うだけの投資をした
のだ。
lines.english: They were extremely rare creatures, but he had made an investment to match.

lines.japanese:
結局、忍の箱庭に住まうものはザリガニたちとな
った。
lines.english: In the end, the inhabitants of Shinobu's miniature world were crayfish.

lines.japanese:
大きなハサミを持つ甲殻生物の姿は勇ましく、忍
の興味を誘う。
　だがそれも長くは続かなかった。
lines.english: The crustaceans looked valiant with their enormous claws, and they captured Shinobu's interest. But that did not last long.

lines.japanese:
共食いが起こったのだ。
　餌は充分にやっていた。
　水も清浄に保たれていた。
lines.english: They began eating one another. He had given them enough food. He had kept the water clean.

lines.japanese:
が、致命的なミスを犯していたのだ。
　“個室”を用意しなかったことである。
　ザリガニは脱皮をする。
lines.english: But he had made a fatal mistake. He had failed to provide them with “private rooms.” Crayfish molt.

lines.japanese:
脱皮直後は殻も柔らかく、固まるまで時間がかかる。
　そのため隠れ家を必要とするのである。
lines.english: Immediately after molting, their shells remain soft and take time to harden. They therefore require places to hide.

lines.japanese:
複数のザリガニが、よってたかって弱い個体を食
い殺している光景を見た。
　いつどの個体が襲われるかは予測できない。
lines.english: He saw several crayfish swarm a weaker one, kill it, and devour it. There was no predicting which individual would be attacked next, or when.

lines.japanese:
体格の大小は決まっているが、脱皮直後はどの個
体でも弱くなる。
lines.english: They differed in size, but immediately after molting every one of them became weak.

lines.japanese: 隙を逃さない略奪者の群れ。
lines.english: A pack of marauders that never missed an opening.

lines.japanese:
ザリガニは数を減じていった。
　忍は見守った。
　一匹に共食い癖がついたようだった。
lines.english: The crayfish dwindled in number. Shinobu watched. One of them seemed to have acquired a taste for cannibalism.

lines.japanese:
仲間だったはずの誰か、つがいであるはずの誰か、
兄妹であるはずの誰か。
lines.english: Someone who should have been a companion. Someone who should have been a mate. Someone who should have been a brother or sister.

lines.japanese: 襲ってこれを殺し、食い散らかした。
lines.english: It attacked and killed them, then scattered their remains as it fed.

lines.japanese:
水槽に棲むザリガニは、一匹だけになった。
　広々とした世界でただひとり略奪に明け暮れ、す
べてを失ったにもかかわらず、悲嘆を宿さない。
lines.english: Only one crayfish remained in the tank. It had spent its days plundering alone in that spacious world, and though it had lost everything, it harbored no grief.

lines.japanese: 箱庭は荒廃したのである。一片の悲しみさえもなく。
lines.english: The miniature world lay in ruins. Without so much as a shred of sorrow.

lines.japanese:
忍は彼ら小さきものたちがからっぽであることを
知った。
lines.english: Shinobu learned that those tiny creatures were hollow inside.

lines.japanese:
最後のザリガニを、忍は殺した。
　こうして最初の箱庭は終焉を迎えたのである。
lines.english: Shinobu killed the last crayfish. And so his first miniature world came to an end.

lines.japanese:
イジメが日常化した頃のこと。
　宗多らは最近開発された新しい遊び……『人間倒し』
に熱中していた。
lines.english: This was after the bullying became routine. Souta and the others were absorbed in a newly invented game… “Human Knockdown.”

lines.japanese:
単純な遊びである。
　必要なものはあまりない。
　忍ひとりいればいい。
lines.english: It was a simple game. It required very little. Only Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
決められた距離からタックルをかけて、忍を倒せ
れば１ポイント。
lines.english: Tackle Shinobu from the designated distance and knock him down for one point.

lines.japanese: 踏みとどまれば０ポイント。
lines.english: If he stayed on his feet, zero points.

lines.japanese:
誰がもっともうまく人間を倒せるかを競う。
　宗多はうまかった。
lines.english: They competed to see who could knock the human down best. Souta was good at it.

lines.japanese:
格闘技でも習っているのか、タックルのあとに足
を絡められると、忍は簡単に転倒した。
lines.english: Perhaps he had studied some martial art; when Souta hooked a leg after the tackle, Shinobu went down easily.

lines.japanese:
宗多は参加していない。
　一歩引いた位置から、退屈げに眺めつつ、弟分の
ような少年と何事か会話している。
lines.english: Souta is not taking part. He watches from a step removed with a bored expression, talking about something with a boy he treats like a kid brother.

lines.japanese:
「なあ、そういやこんなこと続けてて門倉の方、
　平気なんかな？」
lines.english: “Hey, if we keep this up, you think Kadokura's bunch are gonna let it slide?”

lines.japanese: 「やりすぎっとシュクセーされね？」
lines.english: “We go too far, won't they, like, purge us or something?”

lines.japanese: 「目立たなければ口出ししてこねぇよ」
lines.english: “They won't butt in as long as we keep it quiet.”

lines.japanese:
「コイツもあいつらと関わりないから、何したって
　文句言ってこねーよ」
lines.english: “This kid's got nothing to do with them. We can do whatever we want and they won't say a word.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんかよ」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese:
「考えてみろよ。あいつらの仲間になるってことで、
　守ってもらえるって話じゃん」
lines.english: “Think about it. The whole point of joining their crew is that they'll protect you, right?”

lines.japanese:
「仲間でもないヤツのことまで守ったら、わざわざ
　こぞって仲間に入る意味がなくなる」
lines.english: “If they protected people who weren't members, nobody'd have a reason to go running to join them.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese:
「俺のいない時に人間遊びする時は気をつけろよ。
　間違って門倉の誰かに手出すとウゼー」
lines.english: “Watch yourself when you play the human game without me around. Hit one of Kadokura's by mistake and it'll be a pain in the ass.”

lines.japanese:
「平気だろ。コイツいるし。それに、あいつら中坊
　高坊まで広がってるもんな。さすがにこえーって」
lines.english: “We'll be fine. We've got this guy. And their bunch goes all the way up through middle school and high school. No way I'd mess with them.”

lines.japanese:
「ＯＢ会みたいな大人連中までいるぜ。ずっと続い
　てきたことだからな」
lines.english: “They've even got adults—like some alumni club. This thing's been going on forever.”

lines.japanese: 「おれらは関わらない、と」
lines.english: “So we stay out of their way.”

lines.japanese: 「くせぇよ、あいつら」
lines.english: “Those people stink.”

lines.japanese: 「ハハハ」
lines.english: “Hahaha.”

lines.japanese:
彼はディフェンディング・チャンピオン。
　誰もがその記録に挑むのである。
　身体能力があり口がまわり結果を出す。
lines.english: He is the defending champion. Everyone challenges his record. He is athletic, has a way with words, and gets results.

lines.japanese:
子供の集団においては、宗多はまさに英雄の資質
を持つのである。
lines.english: In a society of children, Souta possesses precisely the qualities of a hero.

lines.japanese:
名も知らぬ少年が突っかかってくる。
　頭部を低くするスタイルも、当初は見られなかっ
た実戦的なものだ。
lines.english: A boy whose name Shinobu does not know charges him. Keeping his head low is a practical refinement they had not used in the beginning.

lines.japanese:
幾度も繰り返すごとに最良のスタイルが確立され、
今では全員が同様のテクニックを身につけている。
lines.english: Repetition has refined the technique, and now every one of them has mastered the same form.

lines.japanese:
忍は、危険な部分への直撃だけをずらすようにし
て避ける。
lines.english: Shinobu evades by shifting only enough to keep the blow from landing on a dangerous spot.

lines.japanese: 鳩尾などの急所さえ外せば、どうということはない。
lines.english: As long as it misses a vital point such as the solar plexus, it is nothing serious.

lines.japanese:
だがあまり大きく逃げてしまうと、押さえつけら
れた状態でタックルを受けることになる。
lines.english: But if he moves too far out of the way, they will hold him still and tackle him while he is restrained.

lines.japanese:
最小限の動きで、気取られないよう、回避しなく
てはならない。
lines.english: He has to evade with the smallest possible movement, without letting them notice.

lines.japanese:
目端がきく宗多がいるとそれも難しい。
　今日は楽なスケジュールと言えた。
lines.english: That is difficult when the sharp-eyed Souta is present. By that measure, today is an easy day.

lines.japanese: 「……おい、貴宮固定しろって」
lines.english: “…Hey. Hold Atemiya still.”

lines.japanese:
そう命じた。
　固定すると難易度が下がってしまい、つまらない。
　戸惑う少年たちに、さらに説明した。
lines.english: Souta gives the order. Restraint lowers the difficulty and spoils the fun. He explains further to the confused boys.

lines.japanese: 「クリティカルヒットの出し方、教えてやるよ」
lines.english: “I'll show you how to land a critical hit.”

lines.japanese:
少年たちの顔に、笑みが浮かぶ。
　忍は両腕をそれぞれ固められ、胴体を剥き出しに
される。
lines.english: Smiles spread across the boys' faces. The boys pin Shinobu by both arms, leaving his torso exposed.

lines.japanese: 「見てろよ」
lines.english: “Watch this.”

lines.japanese:
宗多が身を低く固定する。
　鳩尾を突き上げるつもりのようだ。
　しかも直撃。回避不可。
lines.english: Souta sets himself low. He seems intent on driving upward into Shinobu’s solar plexus. A direct hit. No possibility of evasion.

lines.japanese:
死ぬことはないだろうが、げんなりとした。
　少しでも衝撃を吸収しようと力を抜いた。
lines.english: It probably will not kill him. Still, his heart sinks. He lets his body go limp, hoping to absorb even a little of the impact.

lines.japanese:
宗多が今まさにダッシュをかけようとした時、水
風船が破裂したような音がした。
lines.english: Just as Souta is about to charge, there comes a sound like a water balloon bursting.
“…Huh?”

lines.japanese: 忍の頬に、水滴が飛んできた。
lines.english: Droplets spatter Shinobu's cheek.
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 右腕を押さえていた少年の指が、爆ぜていた。
lines.english: A finger on the boy holding his right arm has burst open.
“……What?”

lines.japanese:
ピンク色の肉。
　白い骨。
　遅れて、血。
lines.english: Pink flesh. White bone. Then, belatedly, blood.

lines.japanese:
抜けた腕で頬をぬぐう。
　肉だった。
lines.english: With his freed arm, Shinobu wipes his cheek. It is flesh.

lines.japanese:
「うわぁぁぁ、
　はぅあわぁぁぁっ！」
lines.english: “Aaaaaah— Huaaaaaagh!”
“What…”

lines.japanese: 粗暴でいてどこか冷静な宗多も、目を剥いていた。
lines.english: Even Souta, for all his brutality and strange composure, is staring wide-eyed.

lines.japanese:
「いて、いててっ、
　いてぇ、いてぇぇぇぇぇぇぇぇっ！？」
lines.english: “It—ow, ow— It hurts, it huuuuuuuurts!”

lines.japanese:
半狂乱になった少年が、傷口を押さえることもで
きずに呻いた。
lines.english: Half-crazed, the boy moans, unable even to clutch the wound.

lines.japanese: 「先公に救急車呼ばせろ！　校門だ！」
lines.english: “Get a teacher to call an ambulance! Tell 'em to send it to the front gate!”

lines.japanese:
一人が校舎に走る。
　宗多は怪我人の背中を押して、校門に歩くよう促す。
lines.english: One of them runs toward the school building. Souta pushes the injured boy from behind, urging him toward the gate.

lines.japanese: 「ひぎゃ、ああああっ、いて、いて、痛いぃぃっ！」
lines.english: “Higyaaaaah! Ow, ow, it huuurts!”

lines.japanese: 「死んだりしねぇよ、数でも数えてろ！」
lines.english: “You're not gonna die. Just start counting!”

lines.japanese: 「宗ちゃん……いてぇぇぇぇ……」
lines.english: “Souta… it huuuurts…”

lines.japanese:
悲鳴が遠のいていく。
　忍は一人、取り残された。
lines.english: The screams recede into the distance. Shinobu is left behind alone.

lines.japanese: 「今のは……」
lines.english: “That was…”

lines.japanese:
強烈な存在感を察知し、忍は視線を移動させずに
はいられなかった。
lines.english: Sensing an overwhelming presence, Shinobu cannot help looking toward it.

lines.japanese:
宗多もまた、一瞬遅れて同じ箇所を見る。
　彼女がいた。
lines.english: A moment later, Souta looks the same way. She is there.

lines.japanese: 飼育小屋の脇に立ち、忍たちを注視している。
lines.english: She stands beside the animal shed, watching Shinobu and the others intently.

lines.japanese: （……まさか）
lines.english: (…It couldn't be.)

lines.japanese:
銃で指先を狙えば、ああなるのだろうか？
　強力なスリングショットなどでも再現できるかも
知れない。
lines.english: Would a fingertip look like that if struck by a bullet? Perhaps the effect could also be reproduced with a powerful slingshot.

lines.japanese:
いずれにしても超人的な腕前と、得物が必要になる。
　沙也加は赤手だ。
lines.english: Either way, it would require superhuman skill and a weapon. Sayaka is bare-handed.

lines.japanese: 何かを投じた様子もない。
lines.english: Nor does she appear to have thrown anything.

lines.japanese:
だが忍は、彼女の視線に意味がないはずはないと
確信していた。
lines.english: Yet Shinobu is certain that her gaze means something.
“…Witch—”

lines.japanese: 立ち尽くす。
lines.english: He stands rooted to the spot.

lines.japanese:
やがて救急車のサイレンが聞こえてくる頃、沙也加
は姿を消していた。
lines.english: By the time the ambulance siren comes into earshot, Sayaka is gone.

lines.japanese:
淀みなく紡がれる教師の言葉を、忍はふと遠く感
じた。
lines.english: The teacher's unbroken flow of words suddenly seemed very far away to Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
集中しているとごく稀に、狭間に落ちてしまうか
のように、現実を見失う。
lines.english: Very rarely, when he concentrated, reality slipped from his grasp, as though he had fallen into the space between.

lines.japanese: 真面目にやった反動だろうか。
lines.english: Was this the price of taking things seriously?

lines.japanese: そして時間感覚がぼんやりとしている。
lines.english: His sense of time had gone hazy as well.

lines.japanese:
何日だろう。
　何限目だろう。
lines.english: What day was it? What period?

lines.japanese: （わからない）
lines.english: (I don't know.)

lines.japanese:
唐突に、過去未来のいずれかに放逐された感じだ。
　現在を手放す方法などないというのに。
lines.english: It felt as though he had suddenly been cast into either the past or the future. Even though there was no way to let go of the present.

lines.japanese: 頭を振った。
lines.english: He shook his head.

lines.japanese: 無形の空想を追い払うために。
lines.english: To dispel that formless fantasy.

lines.japanese: （目薬だ）
lines.english: (Eye drops.)

lines.japanese: 沙也加の座っている席に目線をスライドさせた。
lines.english: His gaze slid toward Sayaka's desk.

lines.japanese:
彼女はいない。
　不在だ。
lines.english: She was not there. Absent.

lines.japanese: 欠席、なのだろう。
lines.english: She must be absent.

lines.japanese: 脇に鞄もかけられていない。
lines.english: Her bag was not hanging beside the desk either.

lines.japanese:
座る者がなくとも、登校の気配一つぶら下がって
いれば、暖かみは残るものだ。
lines.english: Even with no one sitting there, a seat retained some warmth if a single sign that its owner had come to school hung beside it.

lines.japanese:
それがない。
　鈍いショックがあった。
lines.english: There was no such sign. A dull shock struck him.

lines.japanese: 本堂沙也加は、学校を休んでいた。
lines.english: Sayaka Hondou was absent from school.

lines.japanese:
自室の窓、カーテンごしに見ていると、夕日に感
染した気分になる。
lines.english: Looking through the curtains of his room, he felt infected by the sunset.

lines.japanese: 立ち上がり、表に向かう。
lines.english: He rose and headed outside.

lines.japanese: 無人のリビングはどこかよそよそしい。
lines.english: The empty living room seemed somehow aloof.

lines.japanese:
忍の精神が、リビングによそよそしいのかも知れ
ない。
lines.english: Or perhaps it was Shinobu's own mind that held the living room at a distance.

lines.japanese:
定量的に確認する術はない。
　出て行く。
lines.english: There was no quantitative way to verify it. He went outside.

lines.japanese:
中庭は整えられている。
　いや、忍が整えているのだ。
lines.english: The courtyard was well kept. No—Shinobu kept it that way.

lines.japanese: 何のために？
lines.english: What for?

lines.japanese:
理由はない。
　強いて言えば惰性である。
　人を招いたことはない。
lines.english: There was no reason. If anything, it was sheer inertia. He had never invited anyone over.

lines.japanese: 忍らは工場に集まる。
lines.english: Shinobu and the others gathered at the factory.

lines.japanese:
たまには、こうした庭に呼び寄せてもいいのでは
ないか？
lines.english: Couldn't he invite them to the garden sometime?

lines.japanese: 「……お茶会……か」
lines.english: “…A tea party…”

lines.japanese: そんな言葉が口を突いて出た。
lines.english: The words slipped from his mouth.

lines.japanese: 「と、その前に沙也加、捜さないとな……」
lines.english: “But first, I've got to find Sayaka…”

lines.japanese: ひとりごちて、門を抜けていく。
lines.english: Muttering to himself, he passed through the gate.

lines.japanese: あの日を最後に、沙也加はいなくなってしまった。
lines.english: Sayaka had been gone since that day.

lines.japanese:
学校にも来ていない。
　工場にも来ていない。
　自宅にも戻っていないそうだ。
lines.english: She had not come to school. She had not come to the factory. Nor, apparently, had she returned home.

lines.japanese:
沙也加を包んでいた老いた人々の心痛は見ていて
哀れを誘うほどで、それも月日の経過とともに苦い
憔悴へと変質していった。
lines.english: The anguish of the elderly people who had watched over Sayaka was painful to see; as time passed, it turned to bitter exhaustion.

lines.japanese:
少女の行方は知れることはなく、やがて本堂の古
びた屋敷からは、人の姿が消えた。
lines.english: No word ever came of the girl's whereabouts, and before long the old Hondou mansion stood empty.

lines.japanese:
忍は勝手に、本堂家に踏み込んだ。
　目撃者はいない。潜入に成功した。
　いたとしても、咎めたかどうか。
lines.english: Shinobu let himself into the Hondou home without permission. No witnesses. The infiltration was a success. Even if there had been any, would they have objected?

lines.japanese:
靴を脱いで、室内に上がる。
　予想していたほど汚れてはいなかった。
lines.english: He removed his shoes and went inside. It was not as dirty as he had expected.

lines.japanese: （……結構きれいだな）
lines.english: (…It's pretty clean.)

lines.japanese:
人が住まない時の荒れ方は、すぐにわかる。
　心臓を掴まれたように、ハッと息を呑む。
　急ぎ足で部屋をひとつひとつ見ていく。
lines.english: It was easy to tell how a place deteriorated when no one lived there. His breath caught as if a hand had seized his heart. He hurried from room to room.

lines.japanese:
いない。
　いない。
　いない。
lines.english: No one. No one. No one.

lines.japanese:
どこにも、誰もいない。
　最後の襖に手をかける。
lines.english: No one, anywhere. He put his hand to the last sliding door.

lines.japanese: （ここは確か）
lines.english: (If I remember, this was…)

lines.japanese:
記憶の刺激に呼応するように、その一室に繋がる
矩形を切り抜いた。
lines.english: As though answering the pull of memory, he slid the door aside, cutting out a rectangle that opened onto the room.

lines.japanese:
以前に来た時とは雰囲気が違っていた。
　客室ではなくなっていたのだ。
　だが。
lines.english: It felt different from the last time he had visited. It was no longer a guest room. But.
“…Sayaka?”

lines.japanese:
人の姿はない。
　だが、ごくごく微量に漂っているのは、線香では
ないだろうか？
lines.english: No one was there. But wasn't there the faintest trace of incense in the air?

lines.japanese: 「おーい？」
lines.english: “Hellooo?”

lines.japanese:
空気は忍を無視して、シンと静まりかえる。
　四方から押し寄せる虚無が、重く体を四つ足に屈
させた。
lines.english: The air ignored Shinobu and remained perfectly still. Nothingness closed in from every side, its weight forcing him down onto all fours.

lines.japanese: 涙声。
lines.english: A tearful voice.

lines.japanese:
駆けていた。
　いつしか駆けていた。
　夕日に追いかけられていた。
lines.english: He was running. At some point he had begun to run. The sunset chased him.

lines.japanese:
不安からか、忍は止まれない。歩けない。
　工場に行くわけではない。
　そこに沙也加はいないだろう。
lines.english: Perhaps it was anxiety. Shinobu could not stop. Could not walk. He was not going to the factory. Sayaka would not be there.

lines.japanese:
森を走る。
　沙也加の行きそうな場所は他にない。
　誰にも発見されなかった少女だ。
lines.english: He ran through the forest. There was nowhere else Sayaka was likely to go. She was a girl no one had been able to find.

lines.japanese:
忍と彼女だけが知っているその場所が、最後の希
望だった。
lines.english: That place, known only to Sayaka and Shinobu, was his last hope.

lines.japanese: （……長老のところに行けば）
lines.english: (…If I go to the Elder…)

lines.japanese:
彼女が膝を抱えて、待っている気がした。
　忍は息も切れ切れに、足を動かした。
lines.english: He felt she would be there waiting, knees drawn to her chest. Gasping for breath, Shinobu drove his legs onward.

lines.japanese:
足を止めた。
　大きく息を吸う。
　吸っては吐く。
lines.english: He stopped. He drew a deep breath. In. Out.

lines.japanese: 濃緑の大気が気道にまとわる。
lines.english: The deep-green air clung to his throat.

lines.japanese: （……見当たらない……）
lines.english: (…I can't find it…)

lines.japanese:
ブチとマルが埋葬された場所が、どこかにあるは
ずなのだ。
lines.english: Somewhere there had to be the place where Spot and Roly were buried.

lines.japanese:
決して広大ではない、この森の中に。
　これほどかけずり回っても見つからない。
　魔法のよう。
lines.english: This forest was hardly vast. Yet after all that running around, he still could not find it. As if by magic.

lines.japanese: （もしかして）
lines.english: (What if…)

lines.japanese: 仮定とも言えない、愚かしい思考。
lines.english: A foolish thought—hardly even a supposition.

lines.japanese:
（あんな場所、最初からなかったのかも
　知れない―――）
lines.english: (Maybe a place like that never existed in the first place—)

lines.japanese:
いつからか忍は妄想にとらわれ、ありもしない場
所を夢見ていたのではないか。
lines.english: Had Shinobu succumbed to delusion at some point and dreamed up a place that was never there?

lines.japanese: そもそも本堂沙也加なる人物がいたのかどうか。
lines.english: Had anyone named Sayaka Hondou ever existed in the first place?

lines.japanese: （いないなんてことが、あるか……）
lines.english: (How could she not exist…?)

lines.japanese: （彼女は実在の人物だ！）
lines.english: (She's a real person!)

lines.japanese:
事実、沙也加は寡黙だった。
　仲間と会話したことなど、数えるほどだ。
lines.english: It was true that Sayaka rarely spoke. She had talked with the others only a handful of times.

lines.japanese:
ことによると、最初から忍たちは六人だったので
はないか。
lines.english: What if, from the very beginning, there had only ever been six of them?
(……That's a lie.)

lines.japanese:
信じたくはない。
　一笑に付したい。
lines.english: He did not want to believe it. He wanted to laugh it off.

lines.japanese:
だがイメージは途轍もなく過酷すぎて、忍を知ら
ず大地に打ち付け、跪かせた。
lines.english: Yet the image was so unthinkably cruel that it struck Shinobu to the ground before he knew it, forcing him to his knees.

lines.japanese: 「……嘘だよ」
lines.english: “…It's a lie.”

lines.japanese:
もう夜である。
　一つだけ確実なことがあった。
　肌で感じていたこと。
lines.english: Night had fallen. There was only one thing he knew for certain. One thing he could feel against his skin.

lines.japanese: 誰も、いやしないのだ、と。
lines.english: There was no one here. No one at all.

lines.japanese:
そしてあとは崩壊しそうになる心を繋ぎ止めるた
め、懸命に記憶に眠るあたたかな空気を想起しよう
とするばかりであった。
lines.english: After that, all he could do was strain to summon the warmth sleeping in his memories, desperate to keep his heart from falling apart.

lines.japanese: 忍とあずさは、二人で缶蹴りをしていた。
lines.english: Shinobu and Azusa are playing kick the can by themselves.

lines.japanese:
この極めて虚しい遊戯は、ルールを調整しかけっ
こに近いものとすることで、かろうじて体裁を成した。
lines.english: They salvage this profoundly pointless game by bending the rules until it becomes something closer to a footrace.

lines.japanese: 夕刻。
lines.english: Evening.

lines.japanese:
大半の子供たちが引き上げる時刻となったが、半
日動き続けて、二人はなお余力を残していた。
lines.english: Most of the children have gone home by now, but even after half a day in constant motion, the two still have energy to spare.

lines.japanese:
そこに沙也加が通りかかる。
　忍と目が合った。
lines.english: Sayaka happens to pass by. Her eyes meet Shinobu's.

lines.japanese: 微妙な空気。
lines.english: An awkward silence.

lines.japanese: 「……お？　お？　なんだなんだ？」
lines.english: “…Oh? Oh? What's all this?”

lines.japanese:
頭上に引かれた見えない糸電話めいたものを、あ
ずさはしきりに気にした。
lines.english: Azusa keeps puzzling over the invisible tin-can telephone line strung above their heads.

lines.japanese: ぷい、と目をそらして、沙也加は歩み去る。
lines.english: Sayaka turns pointedly away and walks on.

lines.japanese: 肩を落とした。
lines.english: Shinobu's shoulders slump.

lines.japanese: 「気にするな」
lines.english: “Don't let it get to you.”

lines.japanese: 背中を叩かれる。
lines.english: She thumps him on the back.

lines.japanese: 「……きみこそ、気にしないでいい……」
lines.english: “…You don't have to worry about it either…”

lines.japanese: 「でも、無愛想なやつだぁ」
lines.english: “Still, what a grouch.”

lines.japanese:
過ぎ去る背中を眺めて、あずさはジト目で鼻を鳴
らした。
lines.english: Azusa watches her go with narrowed eyes and a derisive snort.

lines.japanese: 「それより、そっちの門限は？」
lines.english: “More importantly, what time's your curfew?”

lines.japanese: 「あうえ」
lines.english: “Uh-oh.”

lines.japanese: 校舎の時計は、五時を指していた。
lines.english: The clock on the school building reads five.

lines.japanese: 「あと三十分は行ける」
lines.english: “I've got another half hour.”

lines.japanese: 親指を立てる。
lines.english: She gives a thumbs-up.

lines.japanese: 「五時半か」
lines.english: “Five thirty?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん。日が長いときは六時まで」
lines.english: “No. When the days are long, it's six.”

lines.japanese: 「冬とかは五時半」
lines.english: “In winter and stuff, it's five thirty.”

lines.japanese: 「まだ一時間あるのに三十分なの？」
lines.english: “You have an hour, but you're only staying for half of it?”

lines.japanese: 「……一分でも遅れると愛のムチだから」
lines.english: “…If I'm even one minute late, it's the whip of love.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: あずさの家までは、歩いても十五分くらいだろうか。
lines.english: Azusa's house is perhaps fifteen minutes away on foot.

lines.japanese:
用心して早めに帰るということなのだろう。
　忍は大きく頷く。良い心がけだ。
lines.english: Apparently, she means to leave early just to be safe. Shinobu gives a solemn nod. A fine attitude.

lines.japanese: 「いい軍人になる」
lines.english: “You'll make a fine soldier.”

lines.japanese: 「……あんですか？」
lines.english: “…Whuzzat?”

lines.japanese: 「貴宮」
lines.english: “Atemiya.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 斎と葉子が立っていた。
lines.english: Itsuki and Youko are standing there.

lines.japanese: 「きみたち……」
lines.english: “You two…”

lines.japanese:
「みんな帰ってしまったらしいので、少しだけ時間
　ができた」
lines.english: “Everyone seems to have gone home, so we have a little time.”

lines.japanese:
「見ていたら、二人だけで遊んでいるようだったの
　で、俺たちに何か手伝えることがないかと思って」
lines.english: “We saw the two of you playing alone, so we wondered whether there might be anything we could do to help.”

lines.japanese: 葉子が頭を下げた。いくぶん、ぎこちなく。
lines.english: Youko bows her head, somewhat awkwardly.

lines.japanese: 「なにこの人たち。ともだち？」
lines.english: “Who're these people? Your friends?”

lines.japanese: ドキッとして、あずさを見つめた。
lines.english: His heart skips a beat, and he stares at Azusa.
“…Friends?”

lines.japanese: 「ちがうのか？」
lines.english: “Aren't they?”

lines.japanese: 斎と葉子の顔、視線を往復させる。
lines.english: He looks from Itsuki to Youko and back again.

lines.japanese: 「……違わない。友達だ」
lines.english: “…No, you're right. They're my friends.”

lines.japanese:
笑う。
　笑ってみる。
　うまくいった。
lines.english: He smiles. Tries it, anyway. It works.

lines.japanese: 「友達だよね」
lines.english: “We're friends, aren't we?”
“…Mm. I suppose.”

lines.japanese: 葉子が頭を下げた。
lines.english: Youko bows.

lines.japanese: 「なんかヘン」
lines.english: “Something's weird.”

lines.japanese: 「す、すまん……」
lines.english: “S-sorry…”

lines.japanese: 「いいかな？」
lines.english: “Is it all right?”

lines.japanese: 「そーだなー」
lines.english: “Lemme see…”

lines.japanese: あずさは腕を組んだ。
lines.english: Azusa folds her arms.

lines.japanese: 「ま、いっか！」
lines.english: “Eh, why not!”

lines.japanese:
満面の笑みで、あずさは指を立てた。
　とてもとても、偉そうに。
lines.english: Beaming, Azusa raises one finger. Very, very imperiously.

lines.japanese: 「ふたりはなに。ステディか？」
lines.english: “What about you two? Going steady?”

lines.japanese: 「……バカな。兄妹だ」
lines.english: “…Don't be ridiculous. We're brother and sister.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese:
「……確かに少しヘンなんだ。そのあたりは、見逃
　してもらえる、か？　その……」
lines.english: “…We are a little strange, I admit. Could you let that much slide? Um…”

lines.japanese: 「紅緒あずさ様だ」
lines.english: “The name's Azusa Benio, if you please.”

lines.japanese: えっへりと胸を張るではないか。
lines.english: She puffs out her chest with a proud little harrumph.

lines.japanese: 「塚本斎。こっちが葉子。歳は……」
lines.english: “Itsuki Tsukamoto. This is Youko. As for our ages…”

lines.japanese: 「……やっぱ一番年下か」
lines.english: “…So I'm the youngest after all.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないね」
lines.english: “Can't be helped.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、でもでも、豆じゃないからなー！」
lines.english: “But, but, but I’m not a bean!”
“A bean?”

lines.japanese:
「ドロケイとかやっても、逮捕されないヤツ！
　みそっかすのこと！」
lines.english: “The baby who can't get arrested when we play cops and robbers! You know, the little kid who doesn't count!”

lines.japanese: 忍がいまいち理解できない顔をした。
lines.english: Shinobu looks as though he does not entirely understand.

lines.japanese:
「ああ……あるんだ。そういうのが。
　要するにハンデだ」
lines.english: “Ah… Yes, that's a thing. It's a handicap, essentially.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど……体格・年齢を考慮して、か」
lines.english: “I see… to account for differences in build and age.”

lines.japanese: 「むずかしいこと言ったこの人……」
lines.english: “This guy's using big words…”

lines.japanese: あずさが凹む。
lines.english: Azusa wilts.

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。豆はナシだ」
lines.english: “Fine. No beans.”

lines.japanese: 「承知だ」
lines.english: “Understood.”

lines.japanese: 「まめなしまめなし」
lines.english: “No beans, no beans.”

lines.japanese: 勝ち誇って笑う。
lines.english: She grins in triumph.

lines.japanese: 「そんで、なんかわかんないけど見逃す」
lines.english: “And I don't get it, but I'll let it slide.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 穏やかに告げられ、あずさは少し赤面した。
lines.english: At his gentle words, Azusa blushes slightly.

lines.japanese: 「で、手伝うというのは……つまり」
lines.english: “And by helping… you mean…”

lines.japanese: 「一緒に遊んでくれるということかな」
lines.english: “You'd like to play with us?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そうなる」
lines.english: “Yes, I suppose it comes to that.”

lines.japanese:
斎もどう言っていいのかわからないといった感じ
だった。
lines.english: Itsuki too seems at a loss for how to put it.

lines.japanese: 言葉を選んではいるようだが、やはりぎこちない。
lines.english: He appears to be choosing his words, but remains awkward all the same.

lines.japanese: 「ではこれより一緒に遊ぶことにしよう」
lines.english: “Then let us play together from this point forward.”

lines.japanese: 「承知だ」
lines.english: “Understood.”

lines.japanese: 二人の会話を観察して、怪訝な顔のあずさだ。
lines.english: Azusa watches the exchange with a puzzled expression.

lines.japanese: 「にしてもこっちの子、全然しゃべらないね」
lines.english: “This girl doesn't talk at all, though.”

lines.japanese: 「ものしらずでな。いろいろ教えてやってくれ」
lines.english: “She doesn't know much. Please teach her whatever you can.”

lines.japanese: 「葉子、ちゃん？」
lines.english: “Youko… right?”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 人形のようにあずさを見た。
lines.english: She turns a doll-like gaze on Azusa.

lines.japanese: 「元気ないねー、おたく」
lines.english: “You've got no pep, do you?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Yes. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「元気ださなきゃ」
lines.english: “You gotta perk up.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、だします」
lines.english: “Yes. I will.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁいとーいっぱーつ」
lines.english: “Go for it—full power!”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、言う。ふぁいとーいっぱーつ」
lines.english: “Come on, say it. Go for it—full power!”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁいとーいっぱーつ」
lines.english: “Go for it—full power!”

lines.japanese: 「いいでしょう」
lines.english: “Very good.”

lines.japanese: 「葉子ちゃん？　ボケね」
lines.english: “Youko? You be the comic.”

lines.japanese: 「ホケ」
lines.english: “The comet.”

lines.japanese: 「いいところでボケてね」
lines.english: “Throw in a joke when the timing's right, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「はい……でもよくわからないですよ？」
lines.english: “Yes… but I don't really understand.”

lines.japanese: 「空気読むんだよ」
lines.english: “Read the room.”
“…The room…”

lines.japanese: 「だいじょび。行けるって」
lines.english: “S'okay. You can do it.”

lines.japanese: ぽんぽんと背中を叩いた。
lines.english: She pats Youko twice on the back.

lines.japanese: 「はい、がんばります」
lines.english: “Yes. I will try.”

lines.japanese: 「で、どうすればいい？」
lines.english: “So, what should we do?”

lines.japanese:
「あっ、あんま時間ないよ！
　がっつり遊ばないと！」
lines.english: “Oh! We don't have much time! We gotta play a whole lot!”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね、じゃ普通ルールで……」
lines.english: “Right. Then we'll use the normal rules…”

lines.japanese:
とその時だった。
　校門のあたりからカラフルなバンが入ってきたのは。
lines.english: Just then, a brightly colored van comes through the school gates.

lines.japanese:
女教師が忍たちに近づいて
「暇だったら手伝ってくれる？」と告げた。
lines.english: A female teacher approaches Shinobu and the others and says, “If you're not busy, could you give us a hand?”

lines.japanese: 「だってさ」
lines.english: “You heard her.”

lines.japanese: 「……うえー」
lines.english: “…Aww.”

lines.japanese: あずさは凹んだ。
lines.english: Azusa wilts again.

lines.japanese:
生まれてはじめてかも知れない四人遊びに、あず
さは超ウキウキしていたのだ。
lines.english: Azusa had been beside herself with excitement over what might be her first-ever chance to play in a group of four.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ珍しい組み合わせだな。イジメか貴宮？」
lines.english: “What an unusual group. Are they bullying you, Atemiya?”

lines.japanese: 「……違います。大切な友達です」
lines.english: “…No. They're dear friends.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかそうか」
lines.english: “Good, good.”

lines.japanese:
その答えを予想していたかように笑うと、いかつ
い教師は忍の頭を撫でた。
lines.english: As though he had expected that answer, the burly teacher smiles and ruffles Shinobu's hair.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあお願いね」
lines.english: “Then I'm counting on you.”

lines.japanese:
業者の人間と教師らにまじって、様々な荷物を飼
育小屋の前まで移送。
lines.english: They join the delivery workers and teachers in carrying an assortment of supplies to the animal shed.

lines.japanese: すのこやら乾草やらいろいろだ。
lines.english: Wooden slats, dry hay, and all sorts of other things.

lines.japanese:
そして最後の荷物は……ケージ。
　これは業者の人間だけで運ばれた。
lines.english: And the final piece of cargo is… a cage. The delivery workers carry that one by themselves.

lines.japanese: あずさが目をムギ球のように輝かせる。
lines.english: Azusa's eyes shine like tiny light bulbs.

lines.japanese: 「うっわあ！　ねえねえ、忍くんあれあれ！」
lines.english: “Whoa! Hey, hey, Shinobu—look, look!”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「新しい動物が来るんだ！」
lines.english: “We're getting a new animal!”
“…Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
カラッポになった飼育小屋。
　新たな入居者は……やはり兎。
lines.english: The animal shed, empty until now. Its new resident is… another rabbit.

lines.japanese:
その事実が、大きな一区切りと感じられてならな
かった。
lines.english: He cannot help feeling that fact marks a major dividing line.

lines.japanese: 業者が兎を小屋に入れた。
lines.english: The delivery worker puts the rabbit in the shed.

lines.japanese: 「飼育委員、続行ですね」
lines.english: “So we're still on animal duty.”

lines.japanese: 「うむ。頼むぞ。おまえは期待の星なんだから」
lines.english: “Indeed. We're counting on you. You're our rising star.”

lines.japanese:
つまらない冗談だった。
　忍は笑った。
lines.english: It is a feeble joke. Shinobu laughs.

lines.japanese: 「でもごめんなさい、今度はレンタルなの」
lines.english: “I'm sorry, though. This one's a rental.”

lines.japanese: 「レンタル？」
lines.english: “A rental?”

lines.japanese:
「飼育動物は愛情を学ばせてくれるものだけど……
　衛生面や世話の面などで今、いろいろと難しくな
　っているの」
lines.english: “Keeping animals teaches children about love… but between hygiene concerns, the work involved, and everything else, it’s becoming difficult nowadays.”

lines.japanese:
「親御さんもな、あまりいい顔をせんのだ。
　自由に動物に触れられる環境というのは」
lines.english: “Parents don't like the idea much either— children being able to handle animals whenever they please, I mean.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうなんですか？　別に無害ですけど……」
lines.english: “…Really? But they're harmless…”

lines.japanese: 「そういうことだけでもないのよ」
lines.english: “That isn't the only issue.”

lines.japanese: いつもは朗らかな声が、疲労を感じさせた。
lines.english: Her normally cheerful voice sounds tired.

lines.japanese:
「飼育委員以外、誰も触れない動物……でも、その
　飼育委員だけでも触れることには価値があるとは
　思うのだけれど……やるせないわね」
lines.english: “An animal no one but the care committee can touch… I still think there's value in even those few children being able to touch it, but… it's disheartening.”

lines.japanese: （……学ぶ……感情を、学ぶ……？）
lines.english: (…Learn… Learn emotions?)

lines.japanese: 「どしたの？」
lines.english: “What's up?”

lines.japanese:
「ブチとマルでなくとも、そういうメリットもある
　か。なるほど……」
lines.english: “So there are benefits even if it isn't Spot or Roly. I see…”

lines.japanese: 「ねー？」
lines.english: “Right?”

lines.japanese: 「どいて」
lines.english: “Move.”

lines.japanese: 忍はあずさを機械的な動作でどかした。
lines.english: Shinobu moves Azusa aside with a mechanical motion.

lines.japanese: 「ふぎー！」
lines.english: “Fngh!”

lines.japanese: フェンス際に歩み寄る。
lines.english: He approaches the fence.

lines.japanese: 「も、もののように……」
lines.english: “L-like I'm a thing…”

lines.japanese:
格子模様の向こう、見えない位置に、沙也加が待
機していた。
lines.english: Beyond the lattice, hidden from view, Sayaka is standing by.

lines.japanese: 「やあ」
lines.english: “Hi.”

lines.japanese: 「一緒に、見れない？」
lines.english: “Won't you come look with us?”

lines.japanese: 「兎だよ？」
lines.english: “It's a rabbit.”

lines.japanese: 「おいでよ」
lines.english: “Come on.”

lines.japanese:
形の良い顎が、ほんの少しだけ傾いた。
　正門側に歩いていく。
lines.english: Her finely shaped chin tilts ever so slightly. She starts walking toward the front gate.

lines.japanese: （やっぱり気になってたのかな？）
lines.english: (I guess she was curious after all?)

lines.japanese: 皆のもとに戻る。
lines.english: He rejoins the others.

lines.japanese: 「誰かいたのか？」
lines.english: “Was someone there?”

lines.japanese: 「来たら紹介するよ」
lines.english: “I'll introduce her if she comes.”

lines.japanese:
業者の人間は、飼育小屋が新しい兎に適した住ま
いになるよう、手を加えているようだった。
lines.english: The workers appear to be modifying the animal shed to make it a suitable home for its new rabbit.

lines.japanese:
「もうちょっと待っててもらえるか？　なんだった
　ら、お家にはこっちから電話しておくが」
lines.english: “Could you wait a little longer? We can call your homes for you if you like.”

lines.japanese: 「平気です」
lines.english: “We'll be fine.”

lines.japanese:
丁度良い。
　やがて沙也加がやってくる。
lines.english: Perfect timing. Before long, Sayaka arrives.

lines.japanese:
斎だけが少し驚く。
　他は、目立った反応はない。
lines.english: Only Itsuki shows a little surprise. The others show no obvious reaction.

lines.japanese: 「さっきのブー（無愛想）」
lines.english: “It's Miss Grumpy from before.”

lines.japanese: 一人、少し不機嫌。
lines.english: One of them looks mildly displeased.

lines.japanese: 「本堂沙也加。飼育委員一号」
lines.english: “Sayaka Hondou. Animal Caretaker Number One.”

lines.japanese: そう紹介した。
lines.english: That is how he introduces her.

lines.japanese: 「……怒ってる？」
lines.english: “…Are you mad?”

lines.japanese: 「別に」
lines.english: “Not really.”

lines.japanese: 沙也加は決して誰とも目を合わせなかった。
lines.english: Sayaka never meets anyone's eyes.

lines.japanese: 「本堂だな、知ってる」
lines.english: “Hondou. Yes, I know who you are.”

lines.japanese: 「知ってるの？」
lines.english: “You know her?”

lines.japanese: 「有名だからな」
lines.english: “She's famous.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょうね」
lines.english: “I expect so.”

lines.japanese:
特に自嘲するでもなく、沙也加は実体のない肯定
を重ねた。
lines.english: Sayaka agrees without a trace of self-mockery, though the words seem to affirm nothing in particular.

lines.japanese:
となれば語られない特異性がおぼろに漂うの
だが、気に掛ける者は一人もいない。
lines.english: That leaves an unspoken strangeness hanging faintly in the air, but no one pays it any mind.

lines.japanese: 「塚本斎だ。こっちは妹の葉子。よろしく頼む」
lines.english: “I'm Itsuki Tsukamoto. This is my sister Youko. A pleasure.”

lines.japanese: 「頼む。こっちは兄の斎。頼む」
lines.english: “A pleasure. This is my brother, Itsuki. A pleasure.”

lines.japanese: 「……お好きに」
lines.english: “…As you like.”

lines.japanese:
素っ気なく応じた。
　あるいはそこに、少量の戸惑いがあったのかどうか。
lines.english: Her answer is curt. Perhaps there is a small measure of bewilderment in it. Perhaps not.

lines.japanese: 「新しい兎だってさ」
lines.english: “It's a new rabbit.”

lines.japanese: 「見てたわ」
lines.english: “I was watching.”

lines.japanese: 「名前つける？」
lines.english: “Want to name it?”

lines.japanese: 「……やめておくわ」
lines.english: “…I'd rather not.”

lines.japanese: 「そう。そうだろうね」
lines.english: “I see. I suppose not.”

lines.japanese: 「で、こっちが紅緒あずさ」
lines.english: “And this is Azusa Benio.”

lines.japanese: 「……紅緒だ」
lines.english: “…Benio.”

lines.japanese:
まがりなりにも上級生に対して、腰も頭も高く、
あずさは名乗る。
lines.english: She may be facing an older girl, but Azusa introduces herself with chin and posture equally high.

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 「創せつメンバーだから」
lines.english: “I'm a founding member.”

lines.japanese: 「なんですって？」
lines.english: “Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「年下だけど、創せつメンバーだから」
lines.english: “I'm younger, but I'm a founding member.”

lines.japanese: 胸を張る。
lines.english: She puffs out her chest.

lines.japanese: 「わかったわ」
lines.english: “Understood.”

lines.japanese:
幼い矜持を汲んで、頷いた。
　業者は飼育用のリーフレットを置いて立ち去る。
lines.english: Understanding the child's pride, she nods. The delivery workers leave behind a leaflet on animal care and depart.

lines.japanese: 「あなたたち、どうもありがとうね」
lines.english: “Thank you very much, all of you.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 「今度は一羽なんですね」
lines.english: “Only one this time?”

lines.japanese:
「ええ。兎は人の愛情があれば、一羽でも寂しくな
　いの」
lines.english: “Yes. A rabbit won't get lonely on its own as long as people give it plenty of affection.”

lines.japanese:
「仲良くしてあげて。あなたたちが友達に対するよ
　うに」
lines.english: “Be friends with it, the way you are with one another.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: （友達に対するように、か）
lines.english: (The way we treat our friends, huh…)

lines.japanese: 全員の顔を眺める。
lines.english: He looks around at every face.

lines.japanese:
もしかしたら、ここは自らを笑うべきところなの
ではないかと直感的に思った。
lines.english: He has a sudden sense that perhaps this is where he ought to laugh at himself.

lines.japanese:
不自然なだけだ。
　実行はしなかった。
lines.english: It would only feel unnatural. He does not.

lines.japanese:
「とりあえず今晩はこれでいいそうです。明日、獣
　医さんが来て指導してくれることになっているの
　で、飼育委員のあなたたちはよろしくね」
lines.english: “They say this will do for tonight. A veterinarian is coming tomorrow to show you what to do, so I'm counting on you two from the animal-care committee.”

lines.japanese: 「放課後ですか？」
lines.english: “After school?”

lines.japanese:
「昼休みになるかも。放送で呼ぶことになると思う
　から」
lines.english: “It might be during lunch. I expect we'll call you over the PA.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「もう帰るのか？」
lines.english: “Heading home now?”

lines.japanese: 「少しだけ兎を見ていってもいいですか？」
lines.english: “May we stay and watch the rabbit for a little while?”

lines.japanese: 「おし。いいぞ。怯えさせるなよ」
lines.english: “All right. Go ahead. Just don't frighten it.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese:
「宿直室にいるから、何かあったら呼びに来いよ。
　で、六時前には学校を出るようにな」
lines.english: “I'll be in the night-duty room, so come get me if anything happens. And make sure you're out of the school before six.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 子供たちだけになった。
lines.english: Only the children remain.

lines.japanese: 「さて、と」
lines.english: “Now then.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、もう時間だ……」
lines.english: “Aw, it's time already…”

lines.japanese: 悲痛な声。
lines.english: The anguish in her voice.

lines.japanese: 「ごめん」
lines.english: “Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「これで解散か？」
lines.english: “Are we disbanding?”

lines.japanese: 「カイさん」
lines.english: “Mr. Kai.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、また次にでも」
lines.english: “Well, maybe next time.”

lines.japanese: 「クク……新顔か。いい面構えだな」
lines.english: “Heh… A new face. You've got a good look about you.”

lines.japanese:
全員の目線を、その少年は集める。
　飼育小屋に張りついて、兎を怯えさせていた。
lines.english: The boy draws every eye. He is pressed up against the animal shed, frightening the rabbit.

lines.japanese:
「ここに来て最初に覚えるのはオレ様の顔だ。
　この人参が欲しかったら―――」
lines.english: “The first thing you'll learn here is my face. If you want this carrot—”

lines.japanese:
迷ったが、とりあえず忍は蹴った。
　蹴ってもいいような気がしたのだ。
lines.english: After a moment’s hesitation, Shinobu kicks him. He feels as though it would be all right to do so.

lines.japanese: 「何しやがる！」
lines.english: “What the hell was that for?”

lines.japanese:
尻餅をついたまま、樋口章二は低く呻いた。
　強く打ったらしい。顔をしかめている。
lines.english: Still sitting where he fell, Shouji Higuchi groans low in his throat. He seems to have landed hard. His face is twisted in pain.

lines.japanese: 「……人参をまるごとやらないでくれ。消化に悪い」
lines.english: “…Don't give it a whole carrot. It's bad for digestion.”

lines.japanese: 「昔から兎には人参と決まってる。イラストとかで」
lines.english: “Rabbits and carrots have always gone together. In pictures and stuff.”

lines.japanese: 再度蹴った。
lines.english: He kicks him again.

lines.japanese: 「ぐわっ」
lines.english: “Gwah!”

lines.japanese: 「……忍くんがキレた」
lines.english: “…Shinobu snapped.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、たぶん遊んでる」
lines.english: “No, I think they're playing.”

lines.japanese: 「楽しそう」
lines.english: “It looks fun.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ……そうなのかな。そんな気がしてきた」
lines.english: “Oh… Is that it? Yeah, I'm starting to see it.”

lines.japanese: 誰も止めない。
lines.english: No one stops them.

lines.japanese: 「乱暴なんだよテメェ」
lines.english: “You're a violent little bastard.”

lines.japanese:
「人参は少量ならまだいい。タマネギとかやったら
　大変なんだ。何も知らない人間が、自分だけの判
　断で無茶なことしないでくれ」
lines.english: “A little carrot is one thing. If you fed it an onion or something, the consequences could be serious. If you don't know anything about rabbits, don't do anything reckless on your own.”

lines.japanese: 「……はいはい」
lines.english: “…Yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese:
立ちあがって土を払った。
　忍ら五人を眺め、
lines.english: He stands and brushes off the dirt. Then he surveys the five of them.

lines.japanese: 「なんだこいつら？」
lines.english: “Who're these guys?”

lines.japanese: 「友達だ」
lines.english: “My friends.”

lines.japanese: 「たいしたメンツじゃねーか」
lines.english: “That's quite a lineup you've got.”

lines.japanese: 「“軍団”に“魔女”入りかよ」
lines.english: “So you've got both the ‘Legion’ and the ‘Witch,’ huh?”

lines.japanese: 「それをおまえが率いるのかよ、貴宮？」
lines.english: “And you're their leader, Atemiya?”

lines.japanese: 「……僕らのリーダーは、彼女だ」
lines.english: “…She's our leader.”

lines.japanese: 「ういん」
lines.english: “Yup.”

lines.japanese:
あずさがへの字口で前に出た。
　小型のその生物を、章二はしげしげと見下ろした。
　身長差からどうしてもそうなってしまうのだ。
lines.english: Azusa steps forward with her mouth drawn into a crooked line. Shouji looks the tiny creature up and down. With their difference in height, he can hardly do otherwise.

lines.japanese: 「……このマスコットキャラは？」
lines.english: “…What's with the mascot?”

lines.japanese: 「マスコットじゃねぇよ！」
lines.english: “I'm not a mascot!”

lines.japanese: 「そんで好きな食べ物はマスカットか？」
lines.english: “And let me guess—your favorite food is muscat grapes?”

lines.japanese: 「え……ますかっとってなに？」
lines.english: “Huh…? What's a muscat?”

lines.japanese: 忍に。
lines.english: She turns to Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「……緑色のぶどうみたいなのだよ」
lines.english: “…It's something like a green grape.”

lines.japanese:
「あっ、あれか！　ぺっ、なんだよ、わけかんね！
　ぺっぺっ、すぺぺぺっ！　あたしはブドウなんか
　じゃありませんーだ！」
lines.english: “Oh, those! Bleh! What the heck, that makes no sense! Bleh, bleh, pbbbt! I'm not any kind of grape, thank you very much!”

lines.japanese: べぇ、と見事な舌の出しっぷり。
lines.english: She sticks her tongue out magnificently.

lines.japanese: 顔をしかめた。
lines.english: He grimaces.

lines.japanese: 「……ガキの中のガキだな」
lines.english: “…You're the kiddest kid of them all.”

lines.japanese: 「小児性は関係ない」
lines.english: “Childishness has nothing to do with it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　しょうに……なに？」
lines.english: “Huh? Child… what?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえもガキだろ！」
lines.english: “You're a kid too!”
“Oh. Right…”

lines.japanese: 「それに本堂だったよな？」
lines.english: “And you're Hondou, right?”

lines.japanese: 無視され、章二は鼻白む。
lines.english: The snub takes the wind out of Shouji's sails.

lines.japanese:
「なんだおまえら。バラバラじゃんか。おい、そっ
　ちの軍団組、マズイんじゃないのか、こーいうの
　は？」
lines.english: “What is with you people? You're a total mismatch. Hey, you two from the Legion— aren't you gonna get in trouble for hanging around like this?”

lines.japanese: 「だからこうして人目につかない時間帯に合流した」
lines.english: “That is why we joined them at a time when we would not attract attention.”

lines.japanese: 章二は大げさに肩をすくめる。
lines.english: Shouji shrugs theatrically.

lines.japanese: 「どいつもこいつも仲間とつるみやがる」
lines.english: “Every last one of you has to run with a pack.”

lines.japanese: 「樋口には仲間は？」
lines.english: “Don't you have friends, Higuchi?”

lines.japanese:
「オレ様は十字架背負ったロンリーウルフだから誰
　ともつるまねぇ」
lines.english: “I'm a lone wolf carrying his cross. I don't run with anybody.”
“…A wolf?”

lines.japanese: 「友達いないだけじゃん」
lines.english: “You just don't have any friends.”

lines.japanese: 「なれあわねーだけだ」
lines.english: “I just don't buddy up with people.”

lines.japanese: 「みえっぱりだな」
lines.english: “What a poser.”

lines.japanese: 「……言ってろ」
lines.english: “…Keep talking.”

lines.japanese:
「見てりゃ、二人だけで缶蹴りしやがって。寒すぎ
　るんだよ」
lines.english: “I saw you two playing kick the can all by yourselves. That's too pathetic for words.”

lines.japanese: 「うるへーな！　いいだろそんなの、カッテだろ」
lines.english: “Shut uuup! So what? We can do what we want!”

lines.japanese: 沙也加がこれみよがしにため息をつく。
lines.english: Sayaka heaves a pointed sigh.

lines.japanese: 「……ヘンなのばかり集めたものね」
